title: IT Project Management Director
description:
Job Description

Nova IT Project Management Director will own intake, prioritization, sequencing, dependency management, delivery flow, and release execution across the Nova Platform team. The Director establishes the delivery system that connects product priorities, architecture decisions, engineering capacity, quality requirements, and release commitments, creating transparency and predictability across the Left Arm.

This leader will manage a team of delivery and project-management professionals and partner closely with Product and Platform Engineering, Product Management, Architecture, Build Quality, DevSecOps, the Orchestration Hub, and Right Arm teams. The role is accountable for delivery governance, integrated planning, risk and issue management, executive reporting, and continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, and release reliability.

Core Responsibilities Include

Delivery Strategy & Operating Model

  • Define and operate the delivery model, including intake, prioritization, planning cadence, governance, and escalation pathways.
  • Turn product and platform priorities into clear plans, milestones, release commitments, capacity needs, and accountable ownership.
  • Establish consistent delivery practices across engineering teams while allowing fit-for-purpose execution at the workstream level.
  • Align delivery plans with architecture, quality, security, infrastructure, data, and operational-readiness requirements.
  • Ensure Left Arm plans connect to the integrated Nova roadmap and cross-arm milestones.

Flow, Dependency & Release Management

  • Own sequencing, dependency management, milestone tracking, and release coordination across the software factory.
  • Identify bottlenecks, conflicting priorities, capacity constraints, and cross-team risks before they affect committed outcomes.
  • Coordinate release scope, readiness activities, decision points, and communications across engineering and partner teams.
  • Partner with the Orchestration Hub and Right Arm planning leaders on dates and dependencies that cross organizational boundaries.
  • Create escalation and recovery plans when delivery performance moves outside agreed tolerances.

Performance, Governance & Reporting

  • Establish metrics and scorecards for predictability, throughput, cycle time, work in progress, dependency health, quality, risk, and release reliability.
  • Provide concise, decision-ready reporting to Nova leadership, highlighting outcomes, tradeoffs, risks, and actions required.
  • Maintain disciplined risk, issue, assumption, dependency, and decision management across the portfolio.
  • Use delivery data to identify systemic constraints and drive continuous improvement across teams and processes.
  • Ensure commitments, changes, decisions, and readiness evidence are documented and transparent.

People & Stakeholder Leadership

  • Lead and develop a team of project, program, release, and delivery-management professionals.
  • Build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Architecture, Quality, Security, Infrastructure, Data, Finance, and business teams.
  • Facilitate resolution of cross-functional conflicts and maintain focus on enterprise outcomes.
  • Manage delivery resources, vendor support, budgets, and capacity within the function.
  • Promote an accountable, fact-based, and collaborative culture that enables rapid escalation and resolution.

Critical Leadership Competencies

  • Drives Vision and Purpose: Connects the role’s work to Nova’s broader transformation objectives and communicates a clear path forward.
  • Delivers Results: Creates accountability, removes barriers, and drives measurable outcomes under demanding timelines.
  • Manages Complexity: Synthesizes complex and sometimes conflicting information to establish practical solutions.
  • Decision Quality: Makes sound, timely decisions using technical, delivery, risk, and business considerations.
  • Collaborates: Builds effective partnerships across engineering, architecture, product, delivery, and business teams.
  • Communicates Effectively: Provides clear, concise, and audience-appropriate communications, recommendations, and escalations.
  • Manages Ambiguity: Establishes direction and momentum where requirements, solutions, or precedents are still emerging.
  • Instills Trust: Builds credibility through transparency, expertise, follow-through, and sound judgment.
  • Balances Stakeholders: Anticipates and reconciles competing priorities across product, engineering, architecture, quality, and business partners.
  • Directs Work: Sets clear priorities and accountability for delivery professionals and cross-functional execution teams.

Critical Technology Competencies

  • Demonstrated expertise in technology program, portfolio, delivery, release, and dependency management.
  • Experience operating Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery models across complex engineering environments.
  • Strong knowledge of software-development lifecycles, architecture governance, quality gates, DevSecOps, and production-readiness practices.
  • Experience establishing delivery metrics, executive scorecards, dashboards, and data-driven improvement routines.
  • Strong financial, capacity, vendor, resource, risk, and portfolio-management capabilities.
  • Ability to translate technical complexity into clear plans, decisions, and executive communications.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent related experience required; advanced degree and relevant program-management certification preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive technology program, portfolio, project, or delivery-management experience, including significant people-management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex enterprise technology portfolios or transformation programs.
  • Proven success establishing scalable governance, integrated plans, performance measures, and executive reporting.
  • Experience managing teams, budgets, vendors, capacity, delivery risks, and cross-organizational dependencies.
  • Exceptional facilitation, negotiation, problem-solving, written communication, and presentation skills.
  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy benefit management, regulated technology, or similarly complex environments preferred.

title: O&M Technician I
description:

Provides day-to-day monitoring and basic plant and pump station operations, routine lab tests and basic corrective and preventative operational / maintenance activities.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Operates equipment manually and through instrumentation panels, computer terminals and programmable logic control units following process control procedures. Monitors and observes operating conditions, records observations and data in shift log. Diagnoses basic operational problems and takes corrective action per procedure.

Performs field tests and Laboratory analysis (chemical, physical and biological) in order to maintain compliance with state issued permit. Prepares chemical solutions, monitors supplies and recommends reorder.
  • Performs routine instrument calibration for benchtop and portable meters including, but not limited to, dissolved oxygen, pH, BOD,TSS etc.
  • Performs manual labor including cleaning equipment, facilities and grounds as required and properly disposes of waste according to safety and environmental policies.
  • Operates vehicles, mobile equipment and material handling equipment for operational and maintenance purposes.

  • Possible Work Hazards: May be exposed to possible operations hazards including biological ,fumes, dust, toxic and caustic chemicals, noise, rotating machinery, high pressure and hot and cold temperatures, slippery surfaces, water and electrical hazards.

Education/Experience/Background:

  • High School Diploma or GED with the ability to read, write and comprehend English (operational, process, safety and quality instructions) and be able to carry out verbal and written instructions.

title: Natural Gas Compression Subject Matter Expert (SME) - Remote
description:
AECOM is seeking a Natural Gas Compression Subject Matter Expert (SME) to join our multi-disciplinary design team in support of a major gas transmission projects. This role is a remote position and the selected candidate as the opportunity to work a remote schedule.

In this role, the selected individual will serve as the firm’s lead technical authority for compression stations, establishing overall compression philosophy, equipment selection criteria (reciprocating vs. centrifugal compressors), driver selection (gas turbines, electric motors), and station layout standardization.

This position serves as the primary technical authority for gas compression process and equipment selection, providing top-level engineering direction, technical governance, and oversight across all compression station designs.

For this role, AECOM offers the freedom and flexibility to work remotely and/or be located at a variety of Industrial and Power Generation offices across the United States. Primary locations are Houston, TX, Austin, TX, Denver, CO, and New Orleans, LA.

The job responsibilities of the position will include but are not limited to

  • Define over-pressure protection systems, relief valves, and blowdown system strategies in strict accordance with API, ASME, and CFR.
  • Lead and review complex thermodynamic and gas hydraulic calculations, including multi-stage compressor sizing, intercooling/aftercooling design, fuel gas system conditioning, and transient gas flow behavior.
  • Direct and review specialized dynamic analysis, including pulsation/acoustic studies (API 618/API 688), torsional vibration analysis, and pipe stress/surge analysis (ASME B31.8 / AFT Impulse) to ensure system integrity across operating envelopes.
  • Author and review critical technical specifications and data sheet packages for major rotating equipment (compressor packages, gas turbines, engines, coolers, scrubbers, gas filtration).
  • Lead high-level Technical Bid Evaluations (TBEs), vendor package integration, factory acceptance testing (FAT) witness points, and technical alignment across major OEM suppliers.
  • Drive standardization to streamline engineering, procurement, and constructability while adapting to site-specific pressure ratios, flow regimes, and gas compositions.
  • Review critical project deliverables, including Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs), Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), compressor building layouts, ESD (Emergency Shut-Down) system logic, and hazard mitigation plans.
  • Support proposal development with technical write-ups, compression strategy narratives, engineering hour estimations, and client presentation support.
  • Interface directly with client leadership, regulatory bodies, and operations teams as AECOM's key technical representative for gas compression strategy.
  • Conduct high-level technical reviews and check engineering calculations produced by design teams.
  • Mentor senior and mid-level mechanical engineers on pipeline dynamics, rotating equipment specifications, and industry best practices.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • BA/BS in Mechanical Engineering or related field + 8 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
  • 8 years of experience in mechanical design engineering within the natural gas, pipeline midstream, or energy infrastructure sectors.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) License.
  • Proven track record as a Lead Engineer or SME on large-scale natural gas compression station projects (greenfield or major brownfield expansions).
  • Understanding of design, industrial process and energy projects.
  • Experience in industrial and/or energy-related fields.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Masters Degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field.
  • Extensive experience with major compressor technologies (large reciprocating compressor packages and/or gas-turbine-driven centrifugal units) and associated auxiliary systems (lube oil, seal gas, fuel gas, glycol/cooling water, wash systems).
  • Expert-level knowledge of ASME B31.8 (Gas Transmission and Distribution Piping Systems), 49 CFR Part 192, API 618 (Reciprocating Compressors), API 617 (Centrifugal Compressors), API 619, API 692 (Dry Gas Seals), API 520/521, and ASME Section VIII Div 1/2.
  • Hands-on expertise or oversight capabilities with gas hydraulic and compressor performance tools (e.g., AFT Arrow, AFT Impulse, Synergy, HYSYS/UniSim, Pipe-Flo, CAESAR II, or proprietary OEM compressor sizing tools like Ariel Performance / Solar Compressors).
  • Strong working understanding of environmental, air quality, and acoustic compliance constraints related to compressor station noise and emissions control (NOx, methane slip, turbine exhaust).
  • Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
  • Relocation is not available for this position.

Job Description

The Retail Compliance and QC Analyst will establish and monitor deposit compliance and quality control processes, including first line of defense management to ensure regulatory compliance and effective risk management. In addition, they will track laws and regulations ensuring the Retail business unit complies with federal, state, and local regulatory requirements that might affect the organization's policies.

Retail Compliance

  • Monitor the impact of new regulations or changes to existing regulations, and general compliance issues and concerns.

  • Establish and maintain Risk and Controls Self-Assessment (RCSA) and compliance-centric Key Risk Indicators (KRI) and Key Performance Indicators (KPI) to assess performance and identify potential risk.
  • Ensure retail compliance objectives are met and activities related to standards and legal regulations are tracked and identified.
  • Establish and maintain operating procedures and processes, including first line of defense management monitoring.
  • Collaborate with Regional Operations Managers to facilitate compliance meetings to identify both existing and emerging risks and implement changes in controls to mitigate those risks.
  • Collaborate with key stakeholders within the Compliance Team, Internal Audit Team and Operational Risk Team.
  • Provide compliance guidance to and answer questions from retail staff on federal and state regulations including FinCEN, BSA, FCRA, FDIC, OFAC, Reg CC, Reg DD, Reg E, Reg V, UDAP, privacy laws, Dodd-Frank and other consumer related laws and regulations.
  • Collect and disseminate information related to compliance and other relevant subjects.
  • Perform re-test of findings due to an internal or external retail audit.
  • Provide assistance at all levels of operations as needed to complete projects on time and stay in compliance with Origin Bank policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Work with the Core Support and Deposit Operations teams to test and document all new policy and procedure releases on the Deposit Origination platform.

Quality Control

  • Collaborate with vendors and partners to ensure timely and accurately prepared reports and findings.
  • Work with management team and department managers to ensure findings and/or deficiencies are addressed and corrected.
  • Oversee first line of defense management monitoring.
  • Test Risk and Controls Self-Assessments (RCSA) and Key Risk Indicators (KRI) and Key Performance Indicators (KPI) to assess performance and identify potential risks.
  • Maintain knowledge of deposit account requirements and Origin Bank policies and procedures.
  • Compile, distribute, and present monthly management reports based on review of findings.
  • Report unresolved critical deficiencies to appropriate management.
  • Recommend quality operational improvements based on review of findings.
  • Review deposit account and compliance exceptions to determine QC selections.
  • Determine QC trends and challenges and implement resolutions as required.
  • Coach bankers on QC trends and challenges.

Training

  • Collaborate with Learning and Development to produce high quality training materials.
  • Compile and maintain training materials and assist in or conduct training sessions as needed to address deficiencies.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job has no supervisory responsibilities.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, expert level knowledge of federal and state regulatory compliance and related laws. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor's degree (B. A.) from four-year College or University, or alternatively, five to seven years of senior level compliance and quality control experience. Prior compliance experience at a large/regional bank with subject to direct CFPB oversight and supervision preferred.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms; climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This position operates in a professional banking environment and routinely uses standard office equipment and digital tools such as secure financial systems, computers, phones, photocopiers, and scanners. The role requires maintaining a high level of professionalism, confidentiality, and attention to detail in all interactions.

Work is typically performed in a corporate office setting with a moderate noise level and a dynamic, collaborative, and inclusive workplace where innovation thrives. Expect a fast-paced, supportive atmosphere where your ideas are heard, and your contributions make an impact. This role may occasionally require travel.


Remote positions are intended to be filled in states within our footprint, which includes: Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas. Any exception to this policy requires further regulatory review and approval by management.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Join the future of news


We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join the Subscriptions team at The Washington Post. This role spans the full application stack with a strong emphasis on the cloud infrastructure, delivery systems, and operational practices that keep our subscription products reliable and scalable. As a senior engineer, you will take ownership of complex technical work, contribute to architectural decisions, and help improve how the team builds, deploys, and operates software.


The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in AWS, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and production operations, along with strong application development experience in Java - our primary backend language - and Node.js, and familiarity with React. We value autonomy, initiative, strong communication, and meaningful day-to-day use of AI-assisted engineering tools, including continually finding new ways to apply AI to development, automation, operations, and team effectiveness.


What Motivates You

  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability for both the software you build and the systems that run it.
  • Passionate about reliable, scalable systems and making software delivery faster, safer, and more repeatable.
  • Proactive and comfortable driving complex work with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Comfortable moving across application code, AWS infrastructure, CI/CD, developer tooling, and production operations.
  • Actively uses AI in day-to-day engineering and continually looks for ways to expand its impact on development, automation, operations, and productivity.
  • Enjoys collaborating across teams, mentoring others, and communicating technical decisions clearly upward and sideways.

How You'll Support the Mission

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and operate applications and services supporting our subscription products.
  • Own technical solutions throughout their lifecycle, from design and implementation through deployment, observability, production support, and continuous improvement.
  • Design and maintain scalable, reliable AWS infrastructure using services such as ECS, Lambda, S3, RDS, IAM, CloudWatch, and related technologies.
  • Build and evolve Infrastructure as Code, with experience using AWS CDK strongly valued.
  • Design, maintain, and continuously improve CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, and developer workflows.
  • Configure, operate, troubleshoot, and improve self-hosted engineering platforms such as Jenkins, Airflow, and similar systems.
  • Develop backend services and APIs primarily using Java, with Node.js used across supporting services, automation, and tooling.
  • Contribute to frontend applications built with React and modern JavaScript/TypeScript when needed.
  • Build automation that reduces operational overhead and improves the reliability and repeatability of development and production processes.
  • Establish strong observability and diagnose complex issues spanning applications, infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and third-party integrations.
  • Participate in the team’s on-call rotation, taking ownership of incident diagnosis, mitigation, communication, and systemic follow-up.
  • Identify technical debt, operational bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement and proactively drive solutions.
  • Communicate technical decisions, risks, tradeoffs, and progress clearly to engineering peers, leadership, product partners, and adjacent teams.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to technical standards, architecture discussions, documentation, and engineering best practices.
  • Use AI extensively throughout the engineering lifecycle and identify opportunities to apply it to development, infrastructure, troubleshooting, automation, incident investigation, and operational workflows.

The Skills and Experience You Bring


Minimum Qualifications

  • BA/BS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of hands-on AWS experience, including designing, deploying, operating, and troubleshooting production workloads.
  • 4+ years of experience with CI/CD, deployment automation, and Infrastructure as Code in production environments.
  • 3+ years of backend development experience with Java, including building and operating production services and APIs. Java is the team’s primary backend language.
  • 2+ years of professional experience with Node.js, including services, automation, developer tooling, or infrastructure tooling.
  • Experience administering and operating self-hosted engineering platforms such as Jenkins, Airflow, or similar technologies in production environments.
  • Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, IAM, security, scalability, reliability, and operational best practices.
  • Experience building and maintaining Infrastructure as Code using AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience with containerized workloads and services such as Docker and ECS.
  • Strong production operations and observability experience, including logs, metrics, tracing, dashboards, alerting, and troubleshooting across applications and infrastructure.
  • Experience supporting business-critical systems through an on-call rotation, incident response, and post-incident remediation.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to contribute to application code when needed.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently identify, scope, and drive complex technical work with limited oversight.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively upward and across organizational boundaries.
  • Significant hands-on use of AI-assisted engineering tools in day-to-day work. Candidates should be able to discuss concrete examples of applying AI to infrastructure, automation, software development, troubleshooting, incident investigation, documentation, or other engineering workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 7+ years of hands-on AWS, DevOps, SRE, or cloud infrastructure experience, including ownership of highly available, scalable production environments.
  • 5+ years of experience designing and operating CI/CD, deployment automation, and Infrastructure as Code across multiple applications or teams.
  • 5+ years of backend development experience with Java and 3+ years with Node.js.
  • 2+ years of experience with React or a comparable modern frontend framework, with the ability to contribute to and support modern JavaScript/TypeScript applications when needed.
  • Deep experience with AWS CDK and building reusable infrastructure patterns, constructs, and deployment tooling.
  • Significant production experience administering and evolving Jenkins, Airflow, or comparable self-hosted engineering platforms.
  • Deep experience with AWS services such as ECS, Lambda, S3, RDS, IAM, CloudWatch, and related technologies.
  • Experience building reusable infrastructure, deployment patterns, automation, and developer tooling used across engineering teams.
  • Experience with observability platforms such as DataDog and AWS-native monitoring services.
  • Experience improving developer experience and engineering productivity through platform engineering, automation, and self-service tooling.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and influencing infrastructure, reliability, and operational practices across team boundaries.
  • Advanced use of AI-assisted engineering tools, including experience helping other engineers expand their effective use of AI across infrastructure, operations, automation, troubleshooting, and software development.

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

description:

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.

title: Senior Actuary (FSA)
description:
Job Description:

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own.


We’re seeking a Senior Actuary (FSA) to join our Consumer Markets Division (CMD) FP&A team, where you’ll play a strategic role in shaping the future of life insurance and annuity solutions. This is an opportunity to leverage your actuarial expertise in forecasting, analytics, and financial strategy while collaborating with cross-functional teams in hedging, valuation, pricing, and investments.


This role is on-site 4 days per week and work from home 1 day per week in Newport Beach, CA, Omaha, NE, or Charlotte, NC. If you are not currently located near one of our offices, we offer comprehensive relocation assistance.


Join a team that embraces digital transformation, predictive analytics, and risk modeling innovation. Your work will influence strategic planning, capital optimization, and customer-centric product development in a rapidly evolving insurance landscape.


How you’ll help move us forward:

  • Lead advanced driver analysis across multiple product lines, comparing results to prior quarter, plan, and best-estimate projections.
  • Develop predictive models and reporting tools to analyze investment income, option costs, and reserve attributions.
  • Communicate financial impacts of capital market changes across LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements) US GAAP, statutory, and economic frameworks.
  • Innovate forecasting methodologies and integrate feedback loops to improve accuracy.
  • Shape executive decisions through actionable insights and scenario modeling.

The experience you bring:

  • Education & Credentials: Bachelor’s degree or higher; FSA designation with 6+ years of relevant insurance experience.
  • Technical Expertise: Strong knowledge of life and annuity products in areas such as Valuation, Modeling, Hedging, or Pricing.
  • Analytical Skills: Ability to interpret trends, communicate findings, and assess downstream impacts.
  • Tools & Technology: Familiarity with actuarial modeling platforms, data visualization tools, and forecasting software.

What makes you stand out:

  • Deep understanding of Asset Liability Management (ALM) and hedging strategies for life/annuity products.
  • Experience with reserve roll forwards and financial attribution analysis.
  • Hands-on experience with Fixed Index Annuity (FIA), Multi-Year Guarantee (MYGA), Registered Index-Linked Annuity (RILA), or Payout Annuities.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and adaptability in ambiguous environments.
  • Exposure to data analytics, machine learning applications in actuarial science, and automation tools for forecasting.

  • Omaha, NE: $144,810 - $176,990

title: Data & Context Architect
description:
Function

Cloud & Data Engineering

Our Company

We’re Hitachi Digital Services, a global digital solutions and transformation business with a bold vision of our world’s potential. We’re people-centric and here to power good. Every day, we future-proof urban spaces, conserve natural resources, protect rainforests, and save lives. Job description

Role Summary


We are seeking a Data and Context Architect to design the semantic, knowledge, and governance layers that enable AI agents to operate on trusted, well-structured, and governed data assets.


Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop the metrics layer, ontology framework, search indexes, and business glossary.
  • Establish and evaluate data readiness across dimensions such as scope, freshness, semantic clarity, quality, governance, usability, and operational effectiveness.
  • Elicit business rules from SMEs and translate them into reusable, governed, and scalable models.
  • Define entitlement frameworks, data lineage standards, and agent identity requirements.

Required Technical Skills

  • Expertise with lakehouse and cloud-based data platforms, preferably Databricks, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, PySpark, or comparable technologies.
  • Strong knowledge of semantic and metrics layers, dimensional modeling, and domain-driven data modeling.
  • Hands-on experience with ontologies and knowledge graphs, including RDF/OWL, Neo4j, or similar property graph technologies.
  • Experience with vector databases, semantic search, embeddings, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures.
  • Deep understanding of data governance disciplines, including data lineage, access management, business glossaries, and master data management.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures and business rules implementation using technologies such as Kafka, Amazon MSK, alerting platforms, and rules engines.
  • Proficiency in data quality management, data reconciliation, and data readiness assessments.

Minimum Experience Required

  • 12+ years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, or analytics architecture.
  • Proven delivery of at least one enterprise-scale semantic layer, knowledge graph, or governed data product.
  • Experience leading requirements workshops with business subject matter experts (SMEs) and developing architectural recommendations for senior leadership and stakeholders.

Preferred Skills

  • Domain experience in automotive, manufacturing, or supply chain environments.
  • Exposure to GenAI grounding techniques, text-to-SQL solutions, and natural language analytics platforms.
  • Professional certifications in Databricks, cloud architecture, or data architecture.

title: Power Integrity Engineer
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

The Role and Impact

As a Power Integrity Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring optimal power delivery solutions for Intel's client, edge and physical AI platforms. You'll focus on analyzing, designing, and verifying power delivery networks for complex systems, including silicon, packages, and boards. Your work will directly contribute to delivering top-tier performance and reliability for Intel products, enabling seamless functionality across diverse computing platforms.

Business group

Intel Corporation's Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) is widely recognized as Intel's PC business, delivering innovative solutions to enhance customer experiences and drive business growth. The group focuses on developing cutting-edge technologies that support Intel's client platforms by providing exceptional performance and ease of integration. Joining CCPG offers the opportunity to contribute to Intel's vision of creating world-class computing solutions.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Architect and implement power integrity solutions for client, edge and physical AI platforms, including voltage rail merging, isolation schemes, and decoupling strategies.
  • Extract, develop, and simulate electrical models across DC to high-frequency components for power delivery networks, ensuring design targets are met.
  • Define design constraints and guide the implementation of package and board components for optimal performance.
  • Perform power noise analysis and measurements to characterize power noise profiles across frequency ranges, ensuring correlation to pre-silicon estimations.
  • Collaborate with silicon integration teams, package design teams, and die floor planners to optimize decoupling partitions and voltage regulation schemes.
  • Develop platform-level specifications and design validation methods to continuously enhance power integrity methodologies.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering.
  • Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience in electrical design engineering, focusing on silicon, package, or board-level design.
  • Proficiency in electrical simulation tools, such as Sigrity PowerSI, PowerDC, HSpice, or Matlab.
  • Experience with package and board CAD tools, including Cadence Allegro or Mentor Graphics.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills in English (upper intermediate to advanced level).
  • Must have unrestricted - permanent right to work in Costa Rica.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Master's degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering.
  • 5+ years of experience as a Power Integrity or Power Delivery Engineer, specifically within the PC business environment.
  • Familiarity with platform system architecture, input/output structures, and topologies.
  • Advanced expertise in electrical simulation software, such as Sigrity PowerSI, PowerDC, HSpice, and Matlab.

We're excited about the possibility of you joining our team and contributing to the delivery of exceptional client platforms. Your innovative talent and technical expertise can help shape the future of Intel's computing solutions.

As a core member of the Clinical Trial Team (CTT), the Trial Vendor Manager (TVM) serves as the CTT vendor sub-team lead, providing direct operational management and oversight of clinical trial vendors to deliver study outcomes in accordance with schedule, budget, quality, compliance, and performance standards. The TVM is accountable for vendor service delivery at the study level and collaborates closely with the Vendor Start-up Manager (VSM) across major clinical vendor categories, including central labs, eCOA/ePRO, IRT, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, patient recruitment and retention (PR&R), and imaging. During study start-up, the TVM applies technical and operational expertise to translate protocol requirements into clear vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs), helping to ensure timely study initiation.


You will proactively manage vendor-related risks and potential issues and implement global vendor strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the single point of contact for vendor service delivery at the study level, partnering with vendors and cross-functional teams within the Clinical Trial Team (CTT)
  • Provide direct, end-to-end operational oversight of clinical trial vendor deliverables, ensuring alignment with study timelines, scope, quality, and compliance expectations across major vendor categories, including central labs, IRT, eCOA/ePRO, imaging, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, and PR&R.
  • Review vendor-related protocol sections during protocol development and partner with the Vendor Start-up Manager to translate protocol requirements into accurate vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs).
  • Oversee vendor financials, including forecasting, budget tracking, validation of work performed, service confirmations, invoice reconciliation, and purchase order management and close-out.
  • In collaboration with vendors, study start up leads and vendor start up managers, ensure that all key vendor deliverables and documentation are in place to support submission during study start-up
  • Lead UAT activities for vendor systems (e.g., eCOA, IRT), and contribute to vendor system validation
  • Drive site activation from a vendor perspective, compile vendor related central documents, and address risks/issues during site activation and throughout the life-cycle of a site

title: Engineer III - Land Development (EIT III)
description:
Job Description:

As Pape-Dawson’s headquarters, our San Antonio office is where the company’s legacy and future come together. Since 1965, our team has helped shape the region through iconic destinations, thriving master-planned communities, and the infrastructure that supports everyday life. Today, our multidisciplinary professionals continue to deliver meaningful work across transportation, water, wastewater, and drainage—making a lasting impact in the communities we call home.


Our San Antonio HQ office is seeking an Engineer III (EIT III) who will support the planning, design, analysis, and delivery of engineering projects under the guidance of a licensed professional engineer (P.E.) and may provide technical guidance to junior staff. The role applies experience and problem-solving skills to moderately complex assignments while collaborating with project managers, clients, and multidisciplinary teams.


Responsibilities

  • Prepare design deliverables for site development projects, including grading, drainage, and utility layouts.
  • Analyze site constraints and evaluate design alternatives to meet client objectives and jurisdictional requirements.
  • Develop permitting support materials and coordinate responses required for land development approvals.
  • Perform engineering planning, design, and analysis tasks in accordance with applicable codes, standards, and regulations, producing work that requires minimal revision.
  • Prepare engineering calculations and technical deliverables such as memoranda, reports, drawings, specifications, and cost estimates, clearly documenting assumptions and design decisions.
  • Evaluate and compare design alternatives, apply sound engineering judgment, and recommend appropriate solutions to support project objectives.
  • Coordinate with project managers, multidisciplinary teams, and external stakeholders to support project delivery, with guidance as appropriate.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to junior engineers and designers to support team development and quality outcomes.
  • Participate in quality control and quality assurance practices to support accuracy, consistency, and compliance with standards.
  • Manage assigned tasks independently, meet deadlines, and demonstrate accountability for assigned portions of a project.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field from an ABET-accredited program.
  • Minimum of 2 years of professional engineering experience performing progressively responsible engineering work.
  • Engineer-in-Training (EIT/EI) certification
  • Working knowledge of engineering principles, design standards, and applicable codes and regulations relevant to assigned service areas.
  • Ability to apply established engineering practices and exercise sound judgment on moderately complex assignments.
  • Proficiency with relevant engineering software and tools.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, clients, and external agencies.
  • Ability to manage assigned tasks, meet deadlines, and work under general supervision.
  • Willingness to work primarily in an office environment with periodic field work, site visits, meetings, or agency coordination as required.
  • Ability to work Monday – Friday, 8am – 5pm with overtime as needed

If you need an accommodation or assistance with completing your application due to a disability or special need, please contact our team at Recruiting@pape-dawson.com or call (210) 375-9000.

All qualified applicants for Pape-Dawson Engineers will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

title: Assistant Video Editor / AD
description:
Job Description:

TTI Consumer Power Tools, Inc., has an opening in its Anderson, SC office for an Assistant Video Editor / AD that supports video production from pre-production planning through post-shoot by using diverse video equipment knowledge, exceptional time management and quality assessment skills. We offer competitive wages and a comprehensive benefits package -- tuition assistance, 401(k), medical/dental/vision coverage, vacation and holidays.

Primary Responsibilities:

Assist video director by managing and organizing multi-day shoot schedules and ensuring efficient planning through storyboard assessments at pre-production meetings.

Assess and accurately communicate time and equipment needed to accomplish each video shot with full scope of production in mind.

Perform DIT (Digital Imaging Technician) responsibilities by downloading, tagging, converting and transferring footage to editing team, as well as being responsible for all camera card workflow.

Responsible for confirming focus, exposure, image quality and continuity issues through monitor.

Perform duties as an active part of the video crew responsible for video shoot day including, but not limited to: audio assist, packing and unpacking vehicles, equipment set up and tear down and help with logistics when appropriate.

Culture:

Model and support TTI’s cultural values; People First, Total Ownership, Candid Communication, Innovation Leaders, and a One Team Mentality.

Must work as a team player to instill trust and facilitate a good working environment with the creative team. Have a positive attitude, work well under pressure, problem solving skills, detail oriented, relationship skills and be able to prioritize and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.

Process:

Have experience with on set commercial video workflows and process from concept to footage transfer. Be experienced in video on-set communication to call shots and judge time allotment per shot as the shoot day progresses.

Requirements:

4-year college degree or equal work history in field.

Must have 5 years commercial film AD and DIT experience.
Must be proficient in Adobe Premiere and Silver Stack or like software.

Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times.

Pluses: Film degree, Editing or Camera/lighting experience a plus.

title: AI Research Engineer/Scientist
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

Since the announcement of the world's first on-chip silicon photonics laser more than a decade ago, Intel continues to lead the industry with cutting-edge technology, silicon photonics integration, and scalable AI systems. Our dedication to advanced development ensures that Intel Silicon Photonics continues to drive future bandwidth growth in data center networks and AI infrastructure, with higher density, better power efficiency, and faster speeds. In the future we will deploy co-packaged silicon photonics optical I/O chip lets to enable higher performance, larger-scale and more power efficient AI systems. We are looking for great talent to accelerate this journey so if you are interested in joining our organization we want to hear from you. In this position, the selected candidate will join the Corporate Technology Office Team, contributing to its mission of advancing datacenter connectivity and strengthening Intel's competitive edge in scalable AI system design. As an expert in application parallelization, parallel system simulation and HW/SW co-design, the individual will be responsible for exploring the design of electro-optical systems for research and development (R/D) purposes. Key Responsibilities: • Define architectures and designs that meet specifications and performance targets for next-generation Intel systems using optical interconnects and advanced electrical networks-on-chip. • Optimize network-on-chip performance. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to lead overall project development. • Develop simulation methodologies for scalable electro-photonic systems. • Advise on the development of test plans for overall system characterization. • Thoroughly document all design work with review materials and detailed design descriptions. The ideal applicant should possess excellent oral and written communication skills.

Minimum Qualifications:
• Ph.D. in Computer Science or Electrical and Computer Engineering.
• At least 2+ peer-reviewed publications and/or patents in the simulation, design, optimization and implementation of parallel algorithms and network system simulations.
• 6+ months experience with the gem5 simulation system.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Strong proficiency CPU and GPU parallelization.
• Extensive design experience using hardware in high-level programming languages (C/C++, python).
• Familiarity with switch fabric architectures and related routing algorithms.
• Proven experience of building end-to-end simulation frameworks bridging electronics, and photonics in an overall system design.

title: Network Operations Engineer III
description:
What this Job Entails:


The Network Operations Engineer III is a senior-level role that focuses on the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of both optical and IP networks. This position demands a
high degree of independence, accuracy, and attention to detail. The engineer will address a wide range of complex network issues, working on diverse problems with minimal supervision.

This role requires a deep understanding of optical and IP networking, hardware technologies, and network management tools.


Scope:

  • Resolve a wide range of network issues creatively and effectively.
  • Monitor the performance and health of optical and IP networks using advanced
    network management tools.
  • Tackle diverse and complex problems, applying sound judgment and innovative
    solutions.
  • Operate with minimal guidance on daily tasks, requiring only general instructions for
    new assignments.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve network issues to ensure minimal downtime and service
    disruptions.

Your Roles and Responsibilities:

Network Management:

  • Manage and optimise hardware technologies to maintain network performance and capacity.
  • Engage in day-to-day troubleshooting, working with multiple vendor equipment, and resolving various software and hardware issues.


Issue Resolution:

  • Address network traffic issues and respond to queries raised by XFNs and partners.
  • Collaborate with XFNs and vendors to resolve network-related problems promptly and effectively.
  • Conduct root cause analysis for network outages, providing detailed reports and solutions.


Cross-functional Collaboration:

  • Work closely with service providers, colocation facilities, and XFNs globally, ensuring seamless network operations.
  • Support network infrastructure projects and collaborate with cross-functional teams on new network initiatives.


Additional Duties:

  • Take on other duties as required, contributing to the overall success and reliability of the network infrastructure.

Required Qualifications/Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree (B.S/B.A) from a four-year college or university, with 5 to 8 years of related experience and/or training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Proven experience in optical networking (DWDM, CWDM) and IP networking (IPv4/IPv6, MPLS, BGP, OSPF).
  • Strong judgment in selecting appropriate methods and techniques for obtaining network solutions.
  • Comprehensive understanding of fiber-optic technology, including cable types, connector types, optic types, patch panels, and optical transport technologies.
  • Experience in preparing root cause analysis reports for network and server outages.
  • Strong communication skills, capable of effectively working with global service providers, colocation facilities, and ISPs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a multi-vendor network environment.
  • Relevant network certifications such as CCNP, NCIP, OCA, or equivalent.

Physical Demand & Work Environment:

  • Ability to perform office-related tasks, including prolonged sitting or standing.
  • Capability to move within an office environment and effectively use a computer.
  • Must have strong communication skills for effective collaboration and coordination.
  • Occasional repetitive motions of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers may be required.
  • This position offers the opportunity to work independently on complex network operations tasks while playing a critical role in maintaining and optimizing a global network infrastructure.

title: Transportation Project Manager - Wisconsin
description:
AECOM is seeking an experienced Transportation Project Manager to join our growing Transportation team in Middleton/Madison, Wisconsin. This is an opportunity to lead the delivery of impactful transportation infrastructure projects that improve mobility, enhance safety, and strengthen communities throughout Wisconsin.

In this role, you will lead multidisciplinary teams delivering roadway, highway, intersection, and other transportation improvement projects for the Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT), county highway departments, municipalities, and other public-sector clients. You will guide projects from planning and preliminary engineering through final design and construction support, balancing technical excellence, client expectations, budgets, schedules, and quality requirements.

As a trusted client partner and project leader, you will help develop project delivery strategies, build lasting relationships, mentor technical staff, and identify opportunities to expand AECOM's transportation portfolio. You will collaborate with a broad network of engineering and planning professionals to deliver innovative, sustainable, and cost-effective infrastructure solutions while contributing to the continued growth of AECOM's Transportation business in Wisconsin.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of transportation engineering projects, ensuring compliance with scope, budget, schedule, quality, and client expectations.
  • Manage multidisciplinary project teams delivering roadway, highway, intersection, and transportation infrastructure improvements.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, including WisDOT, county highway departments, municipalities, and other transportation agencies.
  • Develop and maintain project work plans, budgets, schedules, staffing plans, risk registers, and quality management procedures.
  • Oversee preliminary and final design deliverables, technical reports, plans, specifications, cost estimates, and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate engineering disciplines, including roadway design, traffic engineering, bridge and structural engineering, drainage, utilities, environmental services, and construction support.
  • Monitor project performance, identify potential risks and challenges, implement corrective actions, and communicate progress to clients and internal leadership.
  • Lead project meetings, facilitate technical discussions, resolve project issues, and maintain effective communication among clients, stakeholders, and project teams.
  • Support contract negotiations, scope development, change management, invoicing, and financial performance monitoring.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen client relationships, pursue new projects, support proposal development, and contribute to transportation business growth across Wisconsin.
  • Mentor and develop project staff, promote collaboration, and uphold AECOM's commitment to technical excellence, safety, and quality.

    Minimum Requirements

    • BA/BS + 8 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Demonstrated experience managing transportation engineering projects from planning and preliminary design through final design and construction support.
    • Experience delivering roadway, highway, intersection, interchange, or other transportation infrastructure projects for state and local transportation agencies.
    • Experience working with WisDOT, county highway departments, municipalities, or other public-sector transportation clients, with familiarity with applicable design standards, project development processes, and delivery requirements.
    • Professional Engineer (PE) license in Wisconsin, or the ability to obtain Wisconsin licensure.
    • Demonstrated ability to manage project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), risk, and financial performance.
    • Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and coordinating roadway, traffic, bridge, drainage, environmental, utility, and other technical disciplines.
    • Strong client relationship management skills, including experience leading project meetings, communicating technical recommendations, resolving issues, and maintaining client satisfaction.
    • Experience with project pursuits, proposal preparation, scope and fee development, contract negotiations, and identifying opportunities for continued client engagement.
    • Familiarity with transportation design and project delivery tools, including Bentley OpenRoads Designer, MicroStation, AutoCAD Civil 3D, and relevant project management and scheduling software.
    • Demonstrated ability to mentor staff, delegate assignments, review technical deliverables, and foster a collaborative, high-performing project team.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical information clearly to clients, stakeholders, and executive leadership.
    • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities while maintaining quality and schedule commitments.
    • Experience applying innovative, sustainable, and cost-effective engineering solutions to transportation infrastructure challenges.
    • This role does not provide Visa Sponsorship

    At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

    AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. title: Basketball & Soccer Referees - Adult League, Oklahoma City ($40-45/hr)
description:
Now hiring basketball and soccer referees for an established adult recreational league in Oklahoma City.

The OKC Catholic Young Adult Sports League runs organized basketball and soccer seasons for adults ages 18–35. The league is bringing on dedicated outside officials so every game has consistent, reliable coverage, and is looking for refs who want a steady seasonal schedule.

Pay

- $40–45 per hour (final rate set directly with the league)

Seasons

- Basketball: January 25 – March 22, 2027

- Soccer: April 19 – June 14, 2027

Apply for one sport or both. The league runs on the same schedule every year, so strong officials have the opportunity to return season after season.

What we're looking for

- Basketball and/or soccer officiating experience (rec, high school, college, or adult league)

- Solid knowledge of the rules and game management

- Reliability: you show up for every game you commit to, on time

- Professional, calm presence with adult players

title: PBM Product & Platform Engineering Director
description:
Job Description

PBM Product & Platform Engineering Director will lead a Software Engineering team that delivers innovative healthcare technology solutions to our patients, members, and customers as we build and scale the New PBM Platform. Reporting to the VP, Technology Delivery for the New PBM Platform, the Director is accountable for implementation and operational execution across assigned core services, runtime, data services, shared components, product capabilities, and ensures engineering delivery aligns with New PBM Platform standards and enterprise requirements.

This leader will build and direct teams of engineers and technical professionals, partner with Product Management Platform, Product and Operations Architecture to clarify requirements and sequencing, and work closely with Delivery, Build Quality, DevSecOps, Data, Security, and Infrastructure teams. The role owns delivery outcomes, engineering quality, technical health, operational readiness, and talent development for the assigned domain.

Core Responsibilities Include

Engineering Strategy & Execution

  • Translate the New PBM Platform roadmap, architecture, and product priorities into executable engineering plans for the assigned domain.
  • Lead design, development, integration, release, and production-readiness activities with clear commitments and measurable outcomes.
  • Ensure solutions meet functional, performance, scalability, reliability, recovery, security, privacy, and compliance expectations.
  • Prove that delivered capability holds at production volumes, covering load, soak, throughput, latency, and recovery, and produce the supporting evidence before capability is accepted.
  • Drive disciplined engineering practices, design reviews, code quality, documentation, and technical decision-making.
  • Balance near-term delivery with long-term sustainability, reuse, maintainability, and reduction of technical debt.

Product & Platform Partnership

  • Partner with Product Management and Product Architecture to own the engineering half of the specification, confirming requirements are clear, complete, testable, and buildable before work enters a sprint.
  • Partner with Platform Architecture and shared engineering teams to apply common patterns, standards, and reusable services.
  • Coordinate dependencies across product domains, platform teams, enterprise integrations, and the teams integrating, modernizing, and re-implementing the existing PBM systems.
  • Contribute engineering insight to roadmap decisions, sequencing, capacity planning, and investment tradeoffs.
  • Ensure assigned capabilities can operate at required enterprise scale without unnecessary client-specific rebuilding.

Engineering Performance & Operations

  • Establish metrics for delivery predictability, throughput, quality, reliability, technical health, and operational performance.
  • Partner with Build Quality and Test Architecture leaders to meet the program quality bar and produce required readiness evidence.
  • Ensure observability, support models, runbooks, incident response, resilience, and recovery capabilities are built into delivered solutions.
  • Lead resolution of critical technical issues, production risks, and cross-team engineering barriers.
  • Manage the engineering resources that carry production support for delivered capability, including sustaining and on-call coverage, defect and incident workload, and the balance between support demand and new delivery commitments.
  • Drive continuous improvement in automation, developer productivity, release practices, and operational excellence.

People & Organization Leadership

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing organization of engineers and technical professionals.
  • Establish clear roles, accountability, objectives, feedback, and development plans across the team.
  • Recruit and retain talent with the technical depth and learning agility required to scale the New PBM Platform.
  • Create an inclusive, collaborative, and outcomes-focused engineering culture.
  • Manage employees, contractors, vendor resources, capacity, and budget within the assigned function.

Critical Leadership Competencies

  • Drives Vision and Purpose: Connects the role’s work to the broader PBM transformation objectives and communicates a clear path forward.
  • Delivers Results: Creates accountability, removes barriers, and drives measurable outcomes under demanding timelines.
  • Manages Complexity: Synthesizes complex and sometimes conflicting information to establish practical solutions.
  • Decision Quality: Makes sound, timely decisions using technical, delivery, risk, and business considerations.
  • Collaborates: Builds effective partnerships across engineering, architecture, product, delivery, and business teams.
  • Communicates Effectively: Provides clear, concise, and audience-appropriate communications, recommendations, and escalations.
  • Manages Ambiguity: Establishes direction and momentum where requirements, solutions, or precedents are still emerging.
  • Instills Trust: Builds credibility through transparency, expertise, follow-through, and sound judgment.
  • Builds Effective Teams: Develops a strong engineering identity and brings diverse capabilities together around common outcomes.
  • Directs Work: Provides clear direction, priorities, standards, and accountability while removing barriers to execution.

Critical Technology Competencies

  • Deep practical experience designing, building, and supporting enterprise software platforms and product capabilities.
  • Strong knowledge of cloud-native engineering, APIs, distributed systems, event-driven architecture, data services, and scalable application design.
  • Experience with modern programming languages, software-development frameworks, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, observability, and secure engineering practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage non-functional requirements, including performance, reliability, resilience, recovery, security, and maintainability.
  • Experience applying Agile and product-oriented delivery practices in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Ability to evaluate emerging technologies and engineering approaches based on business value, technical fit, risk, and operational sustainability.
  • Working knowledge of AI-assisted engineering tooling and agentic development patterns, and the engineering practices needed to keep generated output reviewable, testable, and maintainable.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information technology, or equivalent related experience required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressive software engineering or technology experience, including significant people-management experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale application, platform, or product engineering teams.
  • Proven record of delivering complex technology capabilities from strategy and design through production operations.
  • Experience delivering within an AI-assisted software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC), including AI-assisted requirements, design, code and test generation, and code review, along with the quality, security, and traceability controls required around them in a regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated judgment about where AI meaningfully accelerates engineering work and where it does not, evidenced by measurable gains in throughput or quality rather than tool adoption alone.
  • Experience managing employees, contractors, vendors, budgets, capacity, and delivery commitments.
  • Strong technical judgment, problem-solving, stakeholder-management, and executive-communication skills.
  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy benefit management, regulated technology, or high-volume transaction-processing environments preferred.

title: General Manager I - Store 8477 - Louisville, KY
description:
Job Description

A General Manager must be committed to inspiring our team, as well as helping our Customers succeed and growing our business with integrity. Professional level sales and management position capable of supporting functions on both sides of the business. The role requires understanding of store systems, automotive systems, parts knowledge and has the ability to identify, troubleshoot and project assist for DIY. Responsible for developing and maintaining Professional Customer relationships and program growth. Is accountable for achieving financial metrics and maintaining service and appearance standards. Position is exempt and requires a minimum of 50-55 hours per week (excluding meal break periods). The average schedule is 5-6 days a week, 11 hour shifts, including rotating nights and weekends, with an hour for lunch. Additional hours may be required based on staffing, store conditions, sales to target, and other business demands. Education, Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

ASE certification preferred, but not required

The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. title: Biobank/Compound Management Technician I
description:
Azenta Inc.

At Azenta, new ideas, new technologies and new ways of thinking are driving our future. Our customer focused culture encourages employees to embrace innovation and challenge the status quo with novel thinking and collaborative work relationships.

All we accomplish is grounded in our core values of Customer Focus, Achievement, Accountability, Teamwork, Employee Value and Integrity

Job Title

Biobank/Compound Management Technician I

Job Description

At Azenta, new ideas, new technologies and new ways of thinking are driving our future. Our customer-focused culture encourages employees to embrace innovation and challenge the status quo with novel thinking and collaborative work relationships.


Azenta Life Sciences is a global leader in the life sciences space with headquarters with offices and operations worldwide. We are a market leader in automated bio sample management solutions and genomic services across areas such as drug development, clinical and advanced cell therapies for the industry's top pharmaceutical, biotech, academic and healthcare institutions globally. We provide unparalleled capabilities with our lab analysis, sample management and storage services, informatics software, and consumables, with the largest installed base managing over 1 billion samples globally.


How You’ll Add Value:


The Biobank & Compound Management Technician is responsible for the full life cycle of the small molecule compounds stored at Azenta. The incumbent is accountable for performing all assigned tasks with full attention and accuracy while maintaining the integrity of the material and the storage processes. The incumbent is also responsible for performing data entry, data analysis, cleaning, maintenance/qualification activities and facilities activities to ensure smooth and continuous functioning of the repository.


What You’ll Do:


  • Perform all functions methodically and in accordance with Policies and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Support day-to-day compound handling processes to fulfil sample requests in both dry and solution formats. This includes but is not limited to weighing samples, creating stock solutions, plating sample requests in various formats, and preparing samples for shipment.
  • Adhere to FDA Good Practices (GMP, GTP, GLP, GDP), International Organization of Standards (ISO), College of American Pathologists (CAP) standards, International Air Transport Association (IATA) and other regulatory requirements as outlined in SOPs and site location.
  • Handle materials in a manner that maintains required temperatures (+30°C to -196°C) per the project definition and SOPs.
  • Follow all safety requirements for working with infectious and non-infectious biological materials, radioactive materials, chemical compounds and drug products.
  • Managing the whole life cycle of the samples/materials:
    • Reception
    • Manifesting
    • Registration
    • Retrievals
    • Discard/Shipment
    • Other client specific tasks
  • Receive and process samples and inventory ensuring proper labeling, sorting, and storage
  • Utilize automated stores, liquid handling systems, robotic platforms, and different repository instrumentation to fulfil daily customer requests
  • Use the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) for all sample handling tasks, including chain of custody, to ensure proper tracking of samples during regular operations
  • Ensure all laboratory and Biobank equipment is properly maintained and in proper working order
  • Responsible for order fulfillment with established timelines
  • Collaborate with other Azenta employees to meet customer deliverables
  • For sites with a laboratory:
    • Independently operate laboratory equipment
    • Accurately and precisely use of pipettes
    • Proper use of reagent
  • Manage storage of samples with established inventory management SOP
  • Review requests for accuracy and availability of compounds and samples
  • Release requests and fill orders based on order type
  • Prepare orders for shipments following SOPs for domestic and international shipments
  • Laboratory equipment maintenance and calibration (balances, automated stores, liquid handling devices)
  • Generate reports and custom reports as assigned/ needed.
  • Proactively manage and drive the resolution of client issues while promoting continuous process improvements
  • Participate in on-call rotation for emergency response in the event of a storage unit failure as needed

What You Will Bring:


  • Bachelor’s degree with some laboratory experience OR
  • Associates degree with 2+ year relevant experience OR
  • HSD with 5+ years relevant experience
  • Must be able to work as a team as well as independently
  • Demonstrate attention to detail and strong organizational skills
  • Demonstrate high level of initiative and ability to triage/prioritize and work independently and in teams
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and make good judgment about what to reveal to customers
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in English.
  • Ability to read/understand/interpret basic correspondence, instructions, rules, procedures in English and other location’s specific official languages
  • Ability to make decisions and judgements based on reasoning
  • Ability to perform tasks with care, is thorough and checks work for accuracy and completeness
  • Proficient with Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Demonstrate trouble shooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience and working knowledge of a GxP laboratory environment preferred
  • Familiarity with Titian Mosaic is preferred
  • Familiarity with liquid handling equipment such as the Echo acoustic dispenser, or Hamilton Vantage is preferred
  • Familiarity with automation, automation specialist is preferred
  • Strong oral and written communication skills

Physical Requirements:


  • Ability to lift 50 pounds.
  • Reaching/lifting/bending
  • Extended periods of standing or sitting while wearing lab coat, safety glasses, and gloves
  • Right- and left-hand finger dexterity.
  • Ability to discern colors or use of color correction glasses.
  • Ability to work with refrigerants (e.g., dry ice and LNs) using proper PPE

Join us and help enable life‑changing discoveries by keeping critical life science systems running reliably—every day.
