Job Description

INSTRUCTIONS TO APPLICANT:


During the application process the “My Experience” page has a section provided “Attachments (Resume/CV, References, Cover letter, etc.)” to upload required documents.

  • Use the Upload button to add each document.
  • You will be able to upload up to 5 documents. Be aware that the maximum size allowed for any one document is 5MB.
  • All documents must be electronically submitted through the Texas A&M Online Employment Services website to be considered.
  • Incomplete or improperly submitted applications may be excluded from consideration.

Please provide the following documents:

  • Cover Letter
  • Resume/CV
  • Three professional references with complete contact information (Unsolicited letters of recommendation will not be considered).
  • Transcripts (Unofficial will be accepted with application. Official transcripts are required at time of verbal offer).
    If transcripts are from an international institution, it is the responsibility of the applicant to have the transcripts translated and evaluated by an approved credential evaluator.


Please do not withdraw your application in an attempt to upload a missing document. If you need assistance with this or any other matter, please contact us at HR.Hiring@etamu.edu.


A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee.


In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.






SUMMARY:

The Communications Specialist, under general supervision, serves as a primary communications and administrative resource for the Graduate School. The position independently interprets and communicates graduate admissions requirements, policies, and procedures; evaluates international academic credentials; coordinates communications with students, faculty, and staff; and maintains Graduate School informational resources. The position exercises independent judgment in resolving routine and moderately complex issues and provides guidance to student employees and graduate assistants.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serves as a primary communications resource for the Graduate School, independently responding to inquiries from prospective students, current students, faculty, and staff and determining when issues require escalation or specialized review.
  • Coordinates the receipt, distribution, and routing of departmental correspondence, admissions materials, and official documents, ensuring timely processing and compliance with Graduate School procedures.
  • Coordinates front office operations by monitoring supply inventories and equipment needs, identifying operational requirements, and facilitating procurement, maintenance, and service requests to support departmental activities.
  • Reviews and maintains Graduate School communications, webpages, electronic forms, and informational materials to ensure compliance with university policies, accuracy of information, and effective communication with stakeholders.
  • Assists with Graduate School projects, events, and special initiatives that support departmental operations and student engagement.
  • Develops and maintains cross-functional expertise in Graduate School operations, admissions processes, and student services to support operational continuity, workflow coordination, and resolution of service-related issues.
  • Interprets and communicates graduate admissions requirements, policies, procedures, and deadlines to students, faculty, and staff, exercising judgment in applying established guidelines and determining appropriate responses to unique situations.
  • Serves as a liaison between applicants, academic departments, and Graduate School staff to resolve admissions and enrollment-related issues.
  • Reviews admissions-related documentation for completeness and compliance with university requirements; identifies discrepancies, determines necessary follow-up actions, and communicates requirements to applicants and academic departments.
  • Develops, coordinates, and distributes Graduate School communications and marketing materials, including newsletters and informational campaigns, to support student engagement, recruitment efforts, and program awareness.
  • Coordinates the international admissions document review process by assessing submitted materials for completeness, communicating document requirements and deficiencies to applicants, and facilitating the collection of information necessary for credential evaluation and admissions review.
  • Evaluates international academic credentials by researching foreign educational systems, interpreting institutional documentation, determining degree equivalencies, and applying university admission standards and established credential evaluation guidelines.
  • Responds to inquiries from international applicants regarding credential evaluation procedures, documentation requirements, admission standards, and application status in accordance with established university policies and guidelines.
  • Maintains current knowledge of foreign educational systems, international credential evaluation practices, and admissions standards through ongoing professional development and training.
  • Coordinates, trains, assigns, and monitors the work of student employees and graduate assistants; provides guidance on office procedures, prioritization of work, and customer service expectations.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience / Knowledge / Skills: No prior experience required. Knowledge of word processing and spreadsheet applications. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills.
  • Ability to: Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others. Ability to present information clearly and concisely.
  • Licensing/Professional Certifications: None
  • Physical Requirements: None
  • Other Requirements: None

PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:

Knowledge of Banner and Laserfiche

Knowledge of foreign degree requirements

SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:

Student Workers and Graduate Assistants




WHY WORK AT EAST TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY?

Competitive Benefits & Work-Life Balance:

  • Employee tuition assistance for master’s and doctoral programs.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, vision, life, and long-term disability insurance.
  • ETAMU contributes to employee health and basic life insurance premiums.
  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays, plus up to eight hours of paid sick leave and vacation each month.
  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS), with optional additional retirement plans (ORP).
  • Physical wellness program and wellness release time for eligible employees.

Career Growth & Development:

  • Access to cutting-edge research opportunities at a designated R2 Research Institution.

Academic Excellence:

  • ETAMU is ranked among the top 30% in five online degree programs and offers national recognized academic programs.
  • Over 140 degree programs, including nationally ranked online and graduate options.
  • First accredited institution to offer a competency-based bachelor’s degree in criminal justice.
  • Distance education offerings in Corsicana, Dallas, Frisco, McKinney, Mesquite, Bryan, and online.

State-of-the-Art Facilities:

  • Work in advanced facilities such as the 113,470-square-foot Nursing and Health Sciences Building, featuring a state-of-the-art simulation hospital and a 1,300-acre agricultural research farm.

Vibrant Campus Life:

  • Engage with over 95 student organizations and 14 NCAA Division I athletic teams, contributing to a thriving campus community.

Prime Location & Growth:

  • Enjoy the benefits of working in rapidly growing regions, with abundant career opportunities at six locations across Dallas and Northeast Texas.

Visit us on our social media:

  • Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, and ETAMU News

Vas veseli reševanje izzivov in iskanje rešitev, ki neposredno prispevajo k zanesljivemu delovanju proizvodnih procesov? Hkrati boste vključeni v projekte prenosa novih izdelkov na lokacijo ter izboljšave obstoječih procesov. S svojim objektivnim pristopom, odgovornostjo in usmerjenostjo v rešitve boste prispevali h kakovosti, skladnosti in robustnosti proizvodnih procesov v skladu z zahtevami GMP.


Job Description

Vaše ključne odgovornosti:

  • Zagotavljanje strokovne podpore proizvodnji ter sodelovanje pri raziskovanju in odpravljanju procesnih in tehničnih težav.

  • Spremljanje proizvodnih procesov in trendov ter pravočasno prepoznavanje priložnosti za izboljšave in optimizacijo.
  • Izvajanje in koordiniranje korektivnih ukrepov ob ugotovljenih težavah ali odstopanjih v proizvodnji.
  • Sodelovanje pri projektih prenosa novih izdelkov na lokacijo ter pri izboljšavah in optimizacijah obstoječih procesov.

  • Sodelovanje pri usposabljanjih ter drugih aktivnostih, potrebnih za zagotavljanje kakovostnega, skladnega in nemotenega delovanja proizvodnje.

Vaš doprinos k delovnem mestu:

  • Zaključena najmanj univerzitetna izobrazba naravoslovne smeri; prednost predstavljajo kemijsko inženirstvo, kemijska tehnologija ali kemija. Prednost bodo imeli kandidati z magisterijem.

  • Veselje do reševanja izzivov ter iskanja učinkovitih in praktičnih rešitev.
  • Izkazana visoka stopnja odgovornosti, samostojnosti in zanesljivosti.
  • Sposobnost objektivnega in analitičnega razmišljanja.
  • Dobro poznavanje orodij Microsoft Office.

Zaželene izkušnje:

  • Izkušnje iz farmacevtske ali kemijske industrije, na primer na področju proizvodnje, kakovosti ali razvoja.
  • Poznavanje programiranja in/ali uporabe orodij umetne inteligence.


Z izbranim kandidatom bomo sklenili delovno razmerje za nedoločen čas s poskusno dobo 6 mesecev. Prijavo oddajte z življenjepisom v slovenskem in angleškem jeziku.

Nagrajevanje:

V Novartisu smo zavezani k soustvarjanju prihodnosti medicine ter priznavanju in nagrajevanju ljudi, ki to omogočajo.


Pričakovani letni osnovni razpon plače za delovno mesto:

22.050,00 - 40.950,00 EUR


Osnovna plača se določa na podlagi vnaprej opredeljenih in transparentnih kriterijev, kot so relevantne veščine, kompetence in izkušnje, ne glede na spol, ter v skladu z Novartisovo politiko določanja plač. Po zaposlitvi v Novartisu se plača periodično pregleda v skladu z internimi akti in postopki.


Plačna enakost je temeljno načelo naše kadrovske politike in odraža našo zavezo k ustvarjanju raznolikega, pravičnega in vključujočega okolja, ki vse zaposlene obravnava dostojanstveno in spoštljivo, kot je opredeljeno v našem Kodeksu etike.


Poleg osnovne letne bruto plače so zaposleni upravičeni tudi do spodaj navedenih ugodnosti:

  • Letni bonus, ki pripada vsakemu zaposlenemu: 10% letne plače.
  • Regres za dopust: Leta 2025 je znašal 2.496 € (neto). Za leto 2026 znaša 2.678,28 € (neto).
  • Nagrada za poslovno uspešnost: Leta 2025 je znašala 2.538,64 € (bruto), skupaj z zimskim regresom.
  • Prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje: Novartis v Sloveniji zagotavlja prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje (5,844 % bruto izplačila, letno omejeno na 3.224,18 €).
  • Zavarovanje: Dodatno nezgodno zavarovanje: V času zaposlitve pri Novartisu je zaposleni 24/7 zavarovan za primer smrti ali invalidnosti, ki bi bila posledica nezgode. Zavarovanje – Specialisti: Kolektivno zdravstveno zavarovanje, ki omogoča hitrejši dostop do specialističnih zdravstvenih storitev pri Zavarovalnici Triglav d.d. za vas in vaše družinske člane.
  • Care Connect: Program, ki ponuja zaupno, osebno podporo za vaše duševno zdravje in dobro počutje s pomočjo terapij, svetovanj, orodij in še mnogo več.
  • Ostale ugodnosti v skladu z zakonom in kolektivno pogodbo: Prevoz, prehrana ter ostali dodatki.

Preberite brošuro in izvedite več o našem sistemu nagrajevanja:


Opomba: Ugodnosti se lahko razlikujejo glede na državo ter so skladni z lokalno zakonodajo, vključno z določili kolektivnih pogodb. Celovit pregled vašega paketa prejemkov, vključno z morebitnimi relevantnimi določbami kolektivne pogodbe, ki veljajo za vašo delovno mesto glede na lokacijo zaposlitve in delodajalca Novartis, vam bo posredovan v okviru nadaljnjih korakov zaposlitvenega postopka.


Predani smo raznolikosti in vključenosti: Novartis si prizadeva ustvariti izjemno, vključujoče delovno okolje in oblikovanje raznolikih timov, saj ti predstavljajo naše bolnike in skupnosti, ki jih oskrbujemo.


Zakaj Novartis: Pomagati bolnikom in njihovim družinam zahteva več kot le inovativno znanost. Potrebna je skupnost zavzetih ljudi, kot ste vi. V Novartisu cenimo sodelovanje, podporo in navdihovanje drug drugega za razvoj prebojnih terapij, ki spreminjajo življenja pacientov. Ste pripravljeni ustvariti svetlejšo prihodnost skupaj z nami?

Function / Position Summary

The Multi Abilities Classroom (MAC) paraeducator supports the classroom by assisting in the implementation of structured instructional, behavioral, social and communication supports aligned to the MAC curriculum and practices. Provide direct support to students with significant academic learning, communication and behavioral needs, including assistance with personal care, feeding and toileting as required. Perform duties under the direct supervision of a certified staff member, contribute to a consistent, hands on and supportive learning environment while maintaining confidentiality of student, staff and department information.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

  • Implement individual or small group instructional activities under the direction of the MAC teacher, using established routines, visual supports and structured practices.
  • Familiarize yourself with student IEP goals, objectives, accommodations and behavior supports to assist with consistent implementation across the school day.
  • Support the use of communication systems, visual schedules, reinforcement systems and other structured supports that align with MAC expectations and individual student needs.
  • Follow through on defined behavioral intervention plans and procedures, including implementation of proactive strategies, reinforcement systems and de-escalation supports as directed by the teacher.
  • Assist with data collection, including academic, behavioral, social and communication data, and document information as requested by the teacher.
  • Support a structured classroom environment by preparing, organizing and maintaining materials and assisting with environmental setup as directed by the teacher.
  • Supervise students during lunch, recess, arrival, departure and community-based activities.
  • Escort students within the building, including transitions to specials/electives, therapies and other instructional spaces.
  • Assist with the loading and unloading of student buses during assigned work hours.
  • Work cooperatively with the teacher by assisting with any activity aligned to student IEP needs, including instructional tasks, communication supports, social skills and behavior routines.
  • Provide personal care support to students, including lifting, transferring, positioning, feeding, toileting and hygiene needs, consistent with special skills expectations.
  • Support students in building independence, communication, self-regulation and engagement throughout the school day.
  • Provide input to the teacher regarding student responses, communication attempts, behavior patterns and other needs.
  • Attend staff meetings and professional development activities as assigned
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, staff and department information within the school and community.
  • Be willing to complete and maintain certification in CPI and Ukeru to support safe, proactive approaches to behavior support.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education

  • Para Educator, Substitute, Professional Educator or Provisional Educator License required.
  • Minimum education requirement for a Para Educator license is completion of at least 60 semester hours of college course work or a passing score on the ETS Para Pro exam or two specific Work Keys exams.
  • Bilingual – Spanish/English (written/verbal) preferred.
  • Assignments in multi-lingual or bilingual classrooms require Bilingual-Spanish/English

Experience / Knowledge

  • 3 years of Para Educator experience or classroom assistant for students with disabilities preferred
  • Experience with students who have behavioral needs preferred
  • Experience as a Behavior technician or Registered Behavior Technician strongly preferred
  • Ability to collaborate with staff and students in a way that is collaborative, student friendly and productive
  • Familiarity with data collection preferred

Physical Demands

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work through many interruptions throughout the school day
  • Required prolonged standing, bending, start/stop and sitting
  • Lifting may be required to manually move, carry, pull or push heavy objects or materials
  • Assisting with toileting needs may be required as needed
  • Ability to perform CPI approved restraint once trained
  • Excellent physical agility and quick response time

Terms of Employment

title: Test Architect Principal
description:
PBM Test Architect Principal

Enterprise Test Strategy, Architecture & Quality Governance

Job Description

PBM Test Architect Principal will serve as the senior technical authority for end-to-end testing strategy, quality architecture, and release-readiness evidence across the New PBM Platform program. The role defines the test framework spanning the New PBM Platform, retained and modernized ESI systems, enterprise integrations, and client re-implementation activities. Working across both the build of new capability and the integration and re-implementation of existing systems, this Principal will establish common standards for test scope, sequencing, automation, data, environments, evidence, and readiness criteria so that quality decisions are consistent across the full delivery lifecycle.

This role partners with the Build Quality Lead, Integration and End-to-End Test Lead, PBM Test Lead, PBS Test Lead , platform and product engineering, enterprise architecture, delivery, security, infrastructure, and business readiness teams. The Principal provides direction on the most complex quality and testing matters, resolves issues with limited organizational precedent, and translates technical risk into clear recommendations for senior leaders and release-governance forums.

Core Responsibilities Include

Test Strategy & Architecture

  • Define and maintain the program’s end-to-end test strategy, architecture, operating model, and multi-year quality roadmap.
  • Establish standards for unit, contract, integration, end-to-end, regression, performance, resilience, security, data-conversion, migration, and operational-readiness testing.
  • Define the release ladder, entry and exit criteria, evidence standards, sign-off expectations, and traceability requirements used across every delivery team in the program.
  • Create reusable testing patterns and reference architectures that support platform scale, frequent releases, and successive client waves.
  • Ensure test architecture aligns with enterprise architecture, security, privacy, compliance, environment, and data-handling requirements.

Quality Governance & Readiness

  • Provide technical governance for quality decisions and independently assess whether test evidence supports progression through readiness gates.
  • Establish quality scorecards, risk indicators, defect measures, and executive reporting that present a clear view of release and migration readiness.
  • Define severity, triage, root-cause, risk-acceptance, and exception-management practices across the program.
  • Identify systemic quality risks and drive corrective actions that improve prevention, detection, and recovery.
  • Advise leaders on quality tradeoffs, unresolved risks, and the evidence required for go/no-go decisions.

Automation, Test Data & AI-Assisted Quality

  • Own the test automation strategy for the program, covering framework and tooling selection, the balance of coverage from unit through end-to-end, pipeline integration, and the standards that keep automation maintainable as the platform changes.
  • Define the test data strategy, including synthetic data generation, masking and de-identification of production-derived data, provisioning and refresh models across shared environments, and the controls that keep PHI and client data handled appropriately.
  • Define how testing is performed within an AI-assisted software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC), including the use of AI-generated tests, test data, and defect analysis, the human review required before generated assets are trusted, and how traceability back to requirements is preserved.
  • Establish the evidence automation approach so readiness evidence is produced as a byproduct of the pipeline rather than assembled by hand.
  • Set the standard for what good automation looks like, including stability and flakiness thresholds, execution time, and the decision rules for when a manual test remains the right answer.

Cross-Program Technical Leadership

  • Partner with the Build Quality Lead to ensure in-factory testing executes against the program strategy and quality bar.
  • Partner with the Integration and End-to-End Test Lead to ensure cross-estate and client-wave testing produces complete, reliable evidence.
  • Set direction for the PBM Test Lead on testing of new platform capability, confirming that in-factory coverage, automation, and evidence meet the program standard before capability leaves the build teams.
  • Set direction for the PBS Test Lead on testing across the existing estate, confirming that regression of current systems, integration across both estates, and client-wave testing produce evidence that holds at the readiness gate.
  • Convene the PBM and PBS Test Leads on a standing cadence to resolve seam issues, including shared environments, test data spanning both estates, defect ownership when a failure crosses the boundary, and whose schedule wins when test windows collide.
  • Align platform, product, integration, migration, and business testing into one coherent strategy and sequence.
  • Mentor architects, engineers, and quality professionals and elevate test engineering capability across the program.
  • Evaluate emerging testing tools and techniques and make the adoption call where they measurably improve quality, cycle time, or cost of testing.

Critical Leadership Competencies

  • Drives Vision and Purpose: Connects the role’s work to the broader PBM transformation objectives and communicates a clear path forward.
  • Delivers Results: Creates accountability, removes barriers, and drives measurable outcomes under demanding timelines.
  • Manages Complexity: Synthesizes complex and sometimes conflicting information to establish practical solutions.
  • Decision Quality: Makes sound, timely decisions using technical, delivery, risk, and business considerations.
  • Collaborates: Builds effective partnerships across engineering, architecture, product, delivery, and business teams.
  • Communicates Effectively: Provides clear, concise, and audience-appropriate communications, recommendations, and escalations.
  • Manages Ambiguity: Establishes direction and momentum where requirements, solutions, or precedents are still emerging.
  • Instills Trust: Builds credibility through transparency, expertise, follow-through, and sound judgment.

Critical Technology Competencies

  • Deep expertise in enterprise test architecture, quality engineering, automation strategy, and software-delivery controls.
  • Experience designing test approaches for complex distributed platforms, APIs, event-driven integrations, data pipelines, and legacy-modern ecosystems.
  • Strong knowledge of performance, scalability, resilience, disaster recovery, security, accessibility, and other non-functional testing disciplines.
  • Experience with test data management, environment strategy, service virtualization, observability, CI/CD integration, and evidence automation.
  • Ability to assess emerging testing tools and AI-enabled techniques while maintaining appropriate security, privacy, compliance, and validation controls.
  • Hands-on experience testing cloud-native workloads on AWS, including containerized and serverless services, managed data and messaging services, and the observability tooling used to diagnose failures such as CloudWatch and X-Ray.
  • Depth in test automation tooling across layers, such as Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress at the interface level, REST Assured, Karate, or Postman at the API level, and JUnit, TestNG, or pytest at the unit and component level, with the judgment to standardize rather than accumulate frameworks.
  • Experience with performance and resilience tooling such as JMeter, Gatling, k6, or LoadRunner, and with contract testing and service virtualization such as Pact, WireMock, or commercial equivalents.
  • Experience with test data management tooling such as Delphix, Informatica TDM, GenRocket, or Tonic, including masking, subsetting, and synthetic generation for regulated data.
  • Experience with test management and traceability tooling such as Jira with Xray or Zephyr, qTest, or TestRail, and with embedding quality and security gates in CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Harness, alongside scanning tools such as SonarQube, Snyk, or Checkmarx.
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted engineering tooling such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q Developer, or Cursor, and with AI-enabled testing capabilities including generated test cases and data, self-healing automation, and visual validation.
  • Products named above are illustrative of the depth expected in each category rather than individually required.
  • Ability to translate highly technical findings into concise, decision-ready recommendations for executive and governance audiences.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent related experience required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in software testing, quality engineering, technology architecture, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience defining enterprise-scale test strategies and governing quality across multiple engineering and delivery organizations.
  • Proven success influencing senior technical leaders and executives without relying on direct authority.
  • Experience supporting large-scale platform transformation, systems integration, or enterprise migration programs.
  • Hands-on experience building and governing test automation at enterprise scale, including framework design, CI/CD integration, and test data management under regulated data constraints.
  • Experience testing within an AI-assisted software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC), including AI-generated tests and test data, and the validation and traceability controls required to rely on them.
  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and presentation skills.
  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy benefit management, regulated technology, or similarly complex transaction-processing environments preferred.

Produce lists of market options and concise technology landscape summaries.
  • Support the assessment of internal Innovation-as-a-Service needs by bringing external trends into the company context and translating internal innovation ideas into evidence-based inputs for clear technology recommendations. Coordinate input from other contributors, including market and internal options, to help define a clear innovation path.
  • Conduct feasibility assessments in cooperation with other stakeholders. Outline validation options where a proof of concept or further investigation is recommended, ensuring the outputs are technically grounded and appropriately scoped.
  • Select the delivery format appropriate to the audience, including written reports, comparison matrices, shared knowledge-base entries, and presentation-ready summaries.
  • Produce structured evidence packages containing technology landscape summaries, option comparisons, feasibility findings, and validation outlines. Ensure these are clear, concise, and ready for use in preparing recommendations.
  • Proactively maintain selected technology trend overviews, reusable trend profiles, and documented insights. Maintain emerging technology deep dives and contribute to trend reports where relevant.
  • Document completed innovation assessments in a shared knowledge base. Before initiating new research, proactively flag existing internal capabilities that may address an incoming topic.
  • Oversee and collaborate with other Innovation-as-a-Service specialists to ensure comprehensive and well-aligned proactive research and innovation consulting services.
  • Support and oversee the solution architect and the specialist responsible for vendor and ecosystem relationships, where needed.
  • Guide and coordinate other analytical contributors, including junior analysts. Review output quality, provide direction on research methodology, and ensure consistent research and analysis within agreed scope boundaries.

Your background

  • At least five years of professional experience in emerging digital technology research, technology scouting, technology foresight, innovation consulting, market intelligence, or applied AI research in an enterprise context.
  • Strong research and analytical skills across AI, data, and digital technologies, with experience producing technology landscape comparisons, feasibility assessments, and vendor evaluations.
  • Strong understanding of and passion for emerging technology trends, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence. Familiarity with innovation lifecycle concepts and frameworks, including insights, validation, proof of concept, and delivery.
  • Experience working with ambiguous, early-stage innovation topics and producing structured outputs that support decisions in a complex corporate environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate input from multiple contributors and to guide and coordinate junior analysts.
  • Excellent documentation practices and the ability to prepare clear written materials ready for use by non-specialist audiences. Fluent English
  • Proactive and creative mindset: You anticipate and adapt to new challenges and topics, readily connecting the dots.
  • Patience and persistence in research: You seek a deep understanding of a topic and conduct thorough scouting research that goes beyond a superficial assessment.

title: Junior Game Developer
description:
About the Role

We are looking for a technically proficient Junior Game Developer to join our studio team as an apprentice, contributing to the development of the MMO game, 5th Dimension. This is a fully remote, US Department of Labor registered apprenticeship, leading to a DOL Certificate of Completion while also offering structured learning and direct involvement in shipping high-quality, multiplayer titles.

You will work using Unity, Blender, and our own integrated development environment (engine) to contribute code and 3D assets to help define the gameplay experience for our MMO games, taking a generalist approach by tackling a range of tasks across both Unity engine development, 3D modelling, and tech art.

The apprenticeship continues for 12 months from the date of commencement, and thereafter an offer for a permanent, full-time role may be made solely at our discretion, creating a progression pathway from apprenticeship to full-time employment.

In tandem with the apprenticeship qualification, the successful applicant will also be prepared to receive a Unity Associate Certification at the completion of the apprenticeship, with the Associate certification exam provided by Realityjam and proctored by Pearson Vue. This adds an additional, internationally recognized qualification layer to the outcomes produced by this role.

If you’re not yet at the required experience level to apply, our pre-employment pathway offers a direct, mentored route into this role. You’ll gain core skills in asset creation, world-building and Unity dev alongside the Realityjam studio team in a commercial setting, with a direct step into the apprenticeship on completion. Find out more at realityjam.io/joinourmovement.

About 5th Dimension

Successful applicants will work as part of the production team for 5th Dimension, a multiplayer MMO game built in Unity, featuring rich world-building tools, interconnected gameplay systems and PVP / multiplayer functionality.

The project is being developed by Virtual Reality Jam Inc dba Realityjam in partnership with 5th Dimension Games.

Before applying, please play the free demo on Steam. Please note that our interview process references the demo.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform basic gameplay programming for story-driven visual content using existing gameplay systems and features, with work undertaken primarily using the Unity engine.
  • Create, optimize, and render 3D assets for use in-game principally using a library of existing assets and materials.
  • Implement, test, and debug core assets relating to gameplay/player experience and gameplay functionality, including 3d models and tech art-related assets and systems (pfx, interactions, etc).
  • Work with the senior dev team to integrate rendered assets and systems into the game pipeline.
  • Participate in code reviews and contribute to engineering best practices across the team.
  • Identify and resolve bugs, performance issues, and technical debt as directed.


Essential Requirements

  • Minimum 1 year of experience as a production team member at a commercial studio working on a published game title (this could be as an intern or trainee).
  • Experience using version control systems such as Git within a team environment.
  • Right to work in the USA; applicants must hold this at the time of application.
  • An intermediate understanding of the 3D pipeline in Unity, including animation, lighting, materials, rigging, etc.
  • Intermediate knowledge of the tech art / 3D art pipeline, including knowledge of 3D modelling applications in Blender.



Desirable Skills

  • Experience with Unity Netcode for GameObjects, Mirror, or an equivalent multiplayer networking framework.
  • Demonstrable experience working within a commercial Unity developer team or 3D art team.
  • Familiarity with .NET and server-side game logic.
  • Experience working with Edgegap, Photon, or similar multiplayer hosting and relay infrastructure.
  • Understanding of performance profiling and optimisation techniques in Unity.
  • Exposure to CI/CD pipelines or automated and unit testing in a games context.


Remuneration & Working Hours

  • Base wage: $20 per hour rising to $21.25 per hour after 6 months in line with the registered apprenticeship wage schedule, plus PTO and sick leave
  • Working hours: Monday to Wednesday, 11:00 am – 7:00 pm ET (including a 30-minute unpaid break - 22.5 hours per week)
  • Apprenticeship Training (Related Instruction): 13 hours per week on Thursday and Friday, 11:00 am – 6:00 pm ET (including a 30-minute break), scheduled outside working hours. As set out in the registered apprenticeship standard, related instruction is unpaid and is not counted as hours worked
  • Location: Fully remote
  • US Department of Labor Registered Apprenticeship (Game Developer - RAPIDS Program No. 2026-CA-140092) leading to a DOL Certificate of Completion, with a progression pathway to a permanent role on successful completion

How to Apply

To apply, submit a copy of your resume plus any of the following;

- a link to your GitHub profile

- a portfolio link showing commercial or published work

- a link to game credits for a project you contributed to, including your name.

Shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a technical programming task in the Unity engine. The task is designed to assess your practical Unity engine and 3D pipeline understanding, and should take approximately 3 hours to complete (NB. this work will not be used in production).

Please note: The opportunity to apply for this role is currently not available to residents of the following states: Delaware, Illinois, Michigan, Virginia, Colorado, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada, New Jersey, and Rhode Island.


Equal Opportunities

Virtual Reality Jam Inc is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and will consider all applications. We particularly encourage applications from groups historically under-represented in the games industry.

This role is only open to candidates with the right to work in the USA. Find out more about Realityjam at , and check out the official website for 5th Dimension at

title: Network Digital Media Professional
description:
Position / Title: Network Digital Media Professional
Bargaining Unit: NON-UNIONDepartment/Location: Communications & Community Relations
Work Days: 176Reports To: Senior Communications Specialist
JD Revision Date: 07/01/2025Supervises: N/A

Function / Position Summary

Each Network Digital Media Professional develops and updates content for the school websites and social media platforms within one of the five school networks. While each school remains primarily responsible for updating its individual school website and social media platforms, the Network Digital Media Professional aides those efforts throughout the network. This position provides training and troubleshooting support for websites and social media, as well as social media content review and creation and website review and layout changes. This position is designed to ensure equality for all schools within the network in regard to the quality and consistency of digital media, as directed by the Senior Communications Specialist who supervises the management of the digital media platforms. Digital content created by the Network Digital Media Professionals is done so in accordance with Communications & Community Relations Department posting guidelines. Network Digital Media Professionals will ensure that content positively features the district, its students, its employees, and/or its educational programming to bolster school pride and engagement among the school communities in the network.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

  • Ensure content featuring students abides by the district's publication guidelines and permissions for the posting of student names/images.
  • Attend regular digital media planning/training meetings as scheduled by the Digital Media Professionals' supervisor.
  • Other duties as assigned.

SOCIAL MEDIA

  • Develop a quarterly calendar to ensure the stories/activities of students of varying ages, abilities, and schools are sent to the district to highlight in district social posts and publications.
  • Collaborate with school-based employees within the network for ideas on engaging classroom activities and events to celebrate on social media.
  • Follow and monitor the social media platforms of the schools within the designated network to ensure equality in posting frequency and assist by adding a minimum of three posts per week of school-based classroom-related content (text and photo/video) to the social media accounts of schools that are lacking in content.
  • Collaborate closely with the Senior Communications Specialist to take advantage of social media cross-promotion opportunities and expand reach.
  • Regularly monitor trending social media comments for schools within the network and report any concerns to the digital media supervisor.

WEBSITE

  • Assist in training school-based employees within the network to perform regular maintenance updates of school website content, and help troubleshoot issues, as needed.
  • Perform school website page reviews and layout/content updates as directed by the Digital Media Professionals' supervisor.

Education

  • Communications, journalism, photography, website, media or writing experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of AP Style is a plus.

Experience / Knowledge

  • A solid understanding of the impact of online communications on the district and its publics.
  • Knowledge of district/school branding and digital media guidelines.
  • Ability to work with students of varying ages and abilities, ensuring their privacy and safety online.
  • Working knowledge of (or a strong desire and willingness to learn) Meta Business Suite and the district's website content management system.
  • Ability to capture and edit photos/video.
  • Strong attention to detail and active listening skills.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with an ability to work in a high-volume environment.
  • Ability to meet established deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently with limited supervision, as well as in a team setting.
  • Ability to use traditional, current, advanced, and emerging communication and technology tools.
  • Knowledge and understanding of public education goals and objectives.

Physical Demands

  • Ability to use district digital communication tools and office equipment and lift up to 30 lbs. with proper technique.
  • Ability to travel off-site to attend meetings, activities, or events.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

Terms of Employment

  • 184 work day stipend position.
  • One-time stipend processed in June 2026. If desired, the stipend can be split between two individuals.
  • Primary work completed outside of official school hours with some evening/weekend work likely.
  • Frequent offsite work; must be willing to travel.

title: VP, Operational Excellence
description:
Enterprise Wide -Relentless Continuous Improvement (RCI):

· Daily Management: Implement/support daily management at all business sites ensuring visual boards standards are in

place for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost (SQDC) and Inventory driving actions, KPI improvement and prioritization for the

business and related work centers. Visual boards including run the business and pacing boards drive actions for

operations, supply base, resource deployment, and key proactive decisions supporting customer requirements.


· Pipeline: Encourage a pipeline of active RCI and productivity cost improvement projects to drive hard and soft savings

that improve systems and processes with the operating units inclusive of VAVE operational and product dress down

efforts.


· Process Improvement: Develop and support continuous improvement strategies utilizing Lean, Six Sigma, and other

methodologies. Identify areas for process improvement within the businesses / operating unit and develop actionable

project plans using problem-solving tools like A3’s, 5S, etc. to address root causes and implement improvements.


· Best Practices: Develop and share best practices across the businesses / operating unit to increase adoption rates across

the supply chain operations network. Create a checklist forum to review and implement best practices as they are proposed

and approved.


· 80/20 Tool Set & KPIs: Implement the 80/20 tools to focus on the high impact activities. Use /enhance key performance

indicators (KPIs) to monitor and drive operational excellence for overall businesses, operating units, and overall JBT

Marel using the JBT Marel Business System.


Manufacturing Transformations:


· Site Consolidation & Expansion: In working with our operating units, develop and support execution plans and strategies for business site rooftop consolidation and or expansion to optimize the global footprint. Support the cross divisional focus for use of operations and migrate to lower cost operations for select products to support the overall footprint strategy. Navigate the key objective to implement an assembly, test, and ship model for food processing businesses as a type 3 operation.


· Product Transfers and Outsourcing: Establish business cases to transfer select products to other business sites and / or outsource manufacturing or assembly processes. Guide/Support the operating units in implementing these business cases to ensure minimal disruption driving overall cost, quality, and delivery efficiency in ever changing geopolitical environments with active tariffs.


· Site Center of Excellence (COE): Guide/support the profitable growth of targeted JBT Marel manufacturing and warehouse distribution facilities increasing business volume from multiple businesses/ operating unit targeting a 75% capacity utilization rate. Support COE’s for machining and fabrications for quick turn service components.


· Asset Management and Advanced manufacturing: Develop and implement asset management strategies to ensure optimal utilization and maintenance of equipment across the JBT Marel rooftop business footprint. This will also involve publishing JBT Marel equipment across the supply chain /operations network and dispositioning on the use of selected equipment and selling it for maximum value. Review and propose implementing or migrating to advanced manufacturing technologies and methodologies to enhance production efficiency, quality and begin the equipment standardization journey where applicable.


· Sales and Service Footprint: Drive key footprint changes based on a fact-pack of JBT Marel combined sales and service footprint to achieve yearly synergy targets inclusive of facility consolidation, better use of offices, selling of owned property, and reducing risk for facility leasing obligations and mitigating dilapidation challenges.


· Make Buy: Support Make Buy strategies with the sourcing teams to enable a core competency compliance model and business case justification. Drive outsourcing where there is less total cost value and invest in internal capability where there is strength and uniqueness driving customer satisfaction and competitive advantage. Utilize holistic assessments to these Make Buy decisions on a regional and global basis.


Strategic Planning as part of relentless continuous improvement (RCI) effort:


· Inventory Management Governance and Toolsets: Develop and implement governance policies for effective and standardized inventory management inclusive of inventory segmentation (nine Block), dashboards, E&O disposition focus, escalation processes and action plans. This governance will apply by business/operating unit/ division and holistically across JBT Marel with the target of improving turns, delivery, and service, and reducing working capital YOY. It is essential that this effort drives right-sizing inventory strategies, especially for service where an increased inventory improves service levels and provides immediate product availability to customers.


· Capacity Planning: Build and develop capacity planning tools to understand capacities and utilization across JBT Marel footprint. This will be a key tool for the manufacturing transformation team to build strategies and monitor progress.


· Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP): Organize and support standardized SIOP process to be deployed at each business or operating units to align internal and external supplier capacities, inventory, and production strategies to support the sales plans and market trends. Each SIOP session will have a standard cadence with a cross functional team to replan and update SIOP plans to ensure integrity and market relevancy inclusive of forecasting. This plan must be integrated into the procurement and planning teams to impact manufacturing and supply base schedules driving more pull than push for shorter lead-times.


· Master Data Management: Ensure accurate and consistent master data management across the supply chain inclusive of consistent data points, controlling additions on new parts, customer, and supplier additions. Implement a standard part normalization process to eliminate duplicate/redundant SKUs. Ensure master data includes the logistic requirements of HS/HTS codes, country or origin and applicable mill certification references.


· Inventory Pull Systems: Drive and support the mindset and key milestones to shift from push to pull environment for product manufacturing, assembly and procurement of components.


HSE Governance for Plants and Operations:


· Ensure health, safety, and environmental (HSE) standards are integrated into the plants, operations, and field service across operating units at JBT Marel. Define one global HSE framework to ensure clear minimum standards that align culture and behaviors providing insights into risk to bring value and improvements to JBT Marel.


· This one global HSE framework provides clear accountability at all levels and clear governance that supports improvement which is resilient by design for both operations and service safety.


· This role with operating unit support will drive adoption of safety standards, implement best practices and create HSE standards for PPE catalogs, safety, and health procedures.


· All plants and sites will comply with one global HSE framework in alignment ISO 45001/14001 system standards.


· This overall HSE strategy will help refresh our entire safety culture with value-add delivering measurable results in incident reduction, downtime, increased efficiency, boosting culture, enabling sustainable business growth and enhancing overall leadership and accountability.

title: Workshop Manager
description:
This will be an acting role for 6months after which we will determine if we recruit and if so open internally or externally.


The Workshop Manager provides leadership, planning, resourcing, and operational control for the Tennessee rock

drill and component rebuild workshops. The role develops safe, efficient, customer-focused repair and rebuild

capabilities; delivers projects on time and within budget; and improves utilization, capacity, quality, financial

performance, and customer satisfaction in support of the Sandvik USA business. The role is also the primary point of

responsibility for workshop repair and service quality and will become the primary ISO9001 responsible site person.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and develop rock drill and component rebuild operations, capabilities, service offerings, and resources in line with business strategy and customer requirements.
  • Plan workshop capacity, labor, inventory, tooling, and workflow to achieve utilization, production, delivery, cost, and quality targets.
  • Deliver repair and rebuild projects for internal and external customers safely, on time, within scope, and within budget. · Implement lean, standardized, and continuously improving workshop processes, supported by disciplined project management and appropriate financial controls.
  • Develop business plans for growth, additional projects, and expansion of workshop offerings based on customer needs, market research, and competitor activity.
  • Build productive relationships with customers and internal stakeholders, optimize service offerings, and maintain a strong focus on customer satisfaction.
  • Recruit, onboard, coach, motivate, develop, and evaluate workshop employees while aligning teams to clear goals and performance expectations.
  • Ensure compliance with Sandvik values, policies, EHS requirements, and applicable government, customer, and industry regulations; identify hazards and promote safer ways of working.
  • Utilize ISO9001 principles and other Quality Control processes to improve and sustain high quality standards for all repairs and services as well as physical workshop layout and tooling requirements.
  • Work with USA Quality and service excellence roles and prepare Tennessee for formal ISO9001 accreditation.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, or a related discipline. OR sufficient workshop management

experience in heavy machinery component shops


Experience: Minimum five years of workshop management experience, with significant senior-level management and

team leadership experience in an industrial, mining, repair, or rebuild environment.


Licenses & Certifications: Preferred certifications in OEM equipment components eg Dana, Kessler, Volvo or

equivalent.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong knowledge of mining-industry workshop, repair, and rebuild processes.
  • Demonstrated commercial and financial acumen, including capacity, utilization, inventory, and cost
  • management.
  • Experience applying lean methods and standardized work to improve safety, efficiency, quality, and delivery.
  • Strong leadership, planning, organizational, customer-service, and relationship-building capabilities. · High professional standards, integrity, drive, and the ability to communicate and listen effectively.

Primarily based at the Tennessee branch workshop, with regular exposure to industrial repair and rebuild operations.

The role requires compliance with applicable PPE and site-safety requirements and willingness to travel approximately

10% of the time. Physical demands, schedule, and other site-specific requirements are to be confirmed.

Job Details:

GENERAL NOTES

Dell Medical School is seeking a Transformational Gifts Writer, Development.

JOB SUMMARY
The Transformational Gifts Writer, Development position provides strategic communications consultation for donor-focused communications that directly support fundraising priorities and outcomes. Reporting to the Senior Director of Development Communications, this role serves as a lead editor and writer for external content and high-level internal communications. The position collaborates with faculty, institutional communications, and marketing teams to create compelling proposals, cases for support, campaign materials, and digital content. This role ensures alignment with brand standards, best practices, and donor engagement goals, strengthening relationships with donors and stakeholders through innovative storytelling and integrated communications.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Develops donor-focused communications strategy

  • Advises internal clients on communications needs across the cycle of giving, aligned with approved institutional fundraising priorities.
  • Partners with internal clients and communications and marketing teams to ensure message alignment.
  • Establishes annual communications goals and evaluates effectiveness through qualitative and quantitative measures.

Oversees content creation and campaign materials

  • Partners directly with faculty and physicians to build fundraising priority-specific cases for support, articulate gift concepts, and ensure brand-aligned language.
  • Translates complex academic, clinical, and research priorities into compelling donor-ready narratives.
  • Serves as a lead writer and strategist for a full range of externally facing content across the cycle of giving, under tight deadlines and evolving priorities.
  • Inputs content into designed templates and collaborates with graphic designers on custom pieces.
  • Guides scripting and messaging for donor-focused events, campaigns, and leadership presentations.

Proposal and case development

  • Leads development of fundraising priority-aligned cases for support and gift opportunities in collaboration with administrators, faculty, and development officers.
  • Maintains methods and standards for tracking proposals-in-process (proposal log) using development systems or new platforms as needed.
  • Serves as a project lead for transformational proposals and campaign-related materials.
  • Ensures consistency and adaptability of campaign messaging across audiences and timelines.

Collaborates with institutional partners

  • Works with communications and marketing teams to integrate donor messaging into broader campaigns.
  • Develops internal communications strategies.
  • Development community, keeping them informed of key related developments to inform their work and strengthen their outreach to donors and prospects.
  • Liaises with campus development teams for cohesive health communications.
  • Provides content and tools to support in-house and campus-wide fundraisers.
  • Participates in planning sessions for major campaigns and events.

Other duties as identified by department

  • Strategic communications, branding, and storytelling
  • Academic/healthcare environment concepts
  • Editorial standards and persuasive writing
  • Performance measurement and CRM tools
  • Strategic communications planning
  • Advanced writing and editing
  • Translating complex concepts into clear narratives
  • Project and proposal management

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Requires a Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field with at least 5 year(s) of experience in developing and leading fundraising or marketing communications strategy for a large institution of higher education, nonprofit or corporate office within the health sciences.

title: Head of Institutional Investments
description:
Let's Write Africa's Story Together!

Old Mutual is a firm believer in the African opportunity and our diverse talent reflects this.

Job Description

The Head of Institutional Investments is accountable for the investment leadership, portfolio construction and investment outcomes of Symmetry's institutional multi-managed solutions. The role leads the institutional portfolio management capability and acts as the senior investment representative of Symmetry to institutional clients, trustees, asset consultants and strategic partners.

This role brings together Symmetry's specialist capabilities in strategic and tactical asset allocation, manager research, responsible investing, private markets and portfolio management and translates these inputs into well-constructed, implementable and appropriately governed institutional portfolios.

The role works closely with Product and Distribution while retaining clear investment accountability for institutional multi-manager portfolio decisions and outcomes.

Working in close partnership with Product, Investment servicing and Distribution teams, the Head of Institutional Investments carries a dual mandate of investment excellence and commercial growth. In addition to sole accountability for investment outcomes, the Head of Institutional Investments shares accountability for originating and winning new institutional business and for retaining and growing existing institutional assets under management, while at all times safeguarding investment integrity, fiduciary duty and governance.

Key Responsibilities:


Institutional Investment Leadership and Accountability:

  • Provide investment leadership and clear accountability for Symmetry's institutional multi-managed portfolio range.
  • Own the investment positioning and investment outcomes of the institutional solutions, within approved mandates and governance frameworks.
  • Ensure the investment philosophy and process are consistently and rigorously applied to institutional portfolios and remain appropriate for evolving client needs and market conditions.
  • Contribute to the strategic development of Symmetry's institutional investment proposition and its competitiveness in the South African institutional market.

Portfolio Construction and Management:

  • Lead portfolio construction across institutional multi-manager solutions, including the combination of asset classes, investment strategies and underlying managers.
  • Translate strategic and tactical asset allocation research and views into portfolio positioning appropriate to each portfolio's objectives, risk budget and constraints.
  • Assess portfolio-level risks, diversification, liquidity, implementation considerations and unintended exposures, and take appropriate action where required.
  • Ensure effective risk management ensuring that risks are intentional, diversified, monitored, and aligned with strategic objectives
  • Oversee portfolio implementation, rebalancing and material portfolio changes to ensure investment decisions are executed efficiently and in line with approved mandates.

Manager Selection and Portfolio Integration:

  • Work closely with the Manager Research capability to translate manager research, due diligence and approved-manager views into portfolio decisions.
  • Be accountable for portfolio-level decisions on manager selection, combination, sizing and replacement through the appropriate investment governance processes.
  • Use the full investment opportunity set, including active and passive, local and global, traditional and alternative strategies, where appropriate to client objectives.
  • Monitor the contribution of underlying managers and strategies to portfolio outcomes and initiate changes where the investment case or portfolio role no longer remains appropriate.

Investment Performance, Risk and Governance:

  • Maintain clear accountability for institutional portfolio performance and risk outcomes against stated investment objectives and benchmarks.
  • Lead or participate in relevant investment governance forums and ensure material investment decisions are appropriately evidenced, challenged, documented and implemented.
  • Ensure portfolios are managed in accordance with client mandates, regulatory requirements, fiduciary obligations and Symmetry's governance standards.
  • Identify portfolios, strategies or underlying managers requiring intervention and ensure timely and appropriate corrective action.

Institutional Client and Market Leadership:

  • Act as a senior investment representative of Symmetry with institutional clients, boards of trustees, asset consultants and other key market stakeholders.
  • Present and defend investment philosophy, portfolio construction, positioning, performance and manager decisions with credibility and clarity.
  • Provide senior investment leadership in client report-backs, consultant engagements, tenders, pitches and other strategically important institutional engagements.
  • Build confidence in Symmetry's institutional investment capability through high-quality communication, thought leadership and consistent investment accountability.

Institutional Growth and Proposition Development:

  • Partner with Product, Distribution and Investment Consulting to develop institutional solutions that respond to client needs while maintaining investment integrity.
  • Provide investment leadership for new-business opportunities and the development or evolution of institutional propositions, including bespoke and multi-managed solutions.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen the institutional proposition across global investments, passive implementation, alternatives and other developing investment capabilities.

New Business Origination, Retention and Commercial Partnership (with Growth and Retention):

  • Partner with Product, Distribution and Investment Servicing & Consulting to originate and win institutional new business, actively working the pipeline and acting as investment lead on strategic pursuits against agreed new-business targets.
  • Build and sustain relationships with asset consultants, and centres of influence to generate deal flow and secure consultant ratings and help shape the go-to-market strategy and value proposition.
  • Share accountability with Product, Distribution and Investment Servicing for retaining and growing existing clients and assets, defending mandates at risk and pursuing cross-sell and share-of-wallet opportunities across the book.
  • Share accountability for agreed commercial outcomes, including net flows, new and retained assets and revenue growth, through a joint operating model that preserves the independence of the Head of Institutional Investments investment judgement.
  • Ensure that commercial and retention targets never override investment judgement, mandate discipline, fiduciary duty or governance.

Team Leadership and Development:

  • Lead and develop the institutional portfolio management capability, creating clear ownership and accountability for investment decisions and outcomes.
  • Build a high-performance investment culture characterised by intellectual rigor, constructive challenge, collaboration, client focus and strong fiduciary standards.
  • Develop investment talent and succession capability and contribute to strengthening the diversity and depth of Symmetry's investment leadership.

These responsibilities provide an overview of the role and are not exhaustive.


Qualification, Skills and Experience


  • A relevant postgraduate qualification in Investments, Finance, Economics, Actuarial Science, Mathematics or a related discipline.
  • A recognised professional investment qualification such as CFA, CAIA, actuarial qualification or CA(SA) is strongly preferred.
  • At least 15 years of relevant investment experience, with substantial experience in institutional investment management, multi-management, investment consulting or portfolio solutions.
  • Demonstrated responsibility for constructing and managing multi-asset and/or multi-manager portfolios and for the resulting investment decisions and outcomes.
  • Deep understanding of manager research, manager selection and portfolio integration across domestic and global asset classes.
  • Strong knowledge of the South African institutional and retirement-fund investment environment, including relevant regulatory and fiduciary requirements.
  • Demonstrated senior client-facing experience with boards of trustees, asset consultants and sophisticated institutional clients.
  • Experience leading senior investment professionals and operating within formal investment governance structures.
  • Experience across traditional and alternative investments, including the use of active and passive implementation approaches.
  • Must meet all applicable regulatory, fit-and-proper and governance requirements associated with the role.
  • Demonstrated track record of winning and originating institutional mandates, not only managing them.
  • Experience leading RFPs, tenders and consultant engagements, and working alongside distribution/sales.
  • An established network among South African asset consultants, trustees and institutional gatekeepers.

title: Analytics Engineer II
description:
Taxwell helps everyday Americans get every tax advantage they deserve by finding credits and deductions they never even knew existed. Our tax preparation software offers easy guidance and ensures your maximum tax refund. We strive to build a team of like-minded experts in both tax and technology who align with our brand purpose, are advocates for our customers and have a fresh, non-traditional approach to the tax industry.

Taxwell is a leading digital tax filing platform formed in 2022 from the combination of Drake Software® and TaxAct®. These two longstanding organizations offer customers professional and do-it-yourself digital and downloadable products that are easy-to-use, best-in-class technology, and provide unparalleled customer support. Taxwell brands are a trusted solution for all users including those with complex tax returns. We strive to attract and retain candidates who exemplify our values: performance, perseverance, progress and partnership. Taxwell is an organization of forward thinkers looking to add industry experts to our growing team.


Job Description

  • We are seeking a detail-oriented and results-driven Analytics Engineer II to join our Data Analytics Engineering team. You will build and maintain reliable, scalable, and well-documented data models that support reporting, self-service analytics, and business decision-making across the organization.
  • In this role, you’ll collaborate with data engineers, analysts, data scientists, and business stakeholders to transform raw data into clean, reusable datasets and consistent metrics. You will independently deliver well-defined analytics solutions within established architectural patterns while partnering with senior engineers on more complex technical decisions.
  • Our team uses modern cloud data technologies and AI-assisted development tools to improve efficiency and quality across development, testing, troubleshooting, and documentation.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain data models and transformation pipelines using dbt and Snowflake within established architectural patterns.
  • Develop and optimize SQL queries and transformations to support reporting, analytics, and operational needs.
  • Own assigned work from requirements gathering through development, validation, deployment, and ongoing support.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to clarify requirements and translate analytical needs into accurate, well-structured datasets and metrics.
  • Partner with data engineers to integrate new data sources and troubleshoot upstream dependencies.
  • Develop and maintain dbt models, macros, automated tests, and documentation using modular, reusable development practices.
  • Investigate and resolve data quality issues, troubleshoot transformation failures, and improve query and model performance.
  • Contribute to shared metric definitions and semantic layers to support consistent reporting across business units and analytics tools.
  • Maintain data definitions, documentation, and lineage to support governance and self-service analytics.
  • Participate in code reviews and knowledge-sharing, applying team standards and providing constructive feedback.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools to support SQL development, troubleshooting, testing, and documentation, validating generated code and results before use.
  • Communicate progress, dependencies, and risks clearly, seeking guidance when complexity or ambiguity requires additional support.

Qualifications

  • 3–5 years of experience in analytics engineering, data modeling, business intelligence, or a related data role.
  • Strong SQL skills, including complex joins, window functions, aggregations, and query troubleshooting and optimization.
  • Hands-on experience with dbt, including modular models, testing, documentation, and basic Jinja.
  • Experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse.
  • Working knowledge of dimensional modeling, dataset grain, and table relationships.
  • Experience using Git, pull requests, and collaborative code review workflows.
  • Understanding of data quality, automated testing, documentation, governance, and data lineage principles.
  • Ability to independently deliver well-defined work, clarify ambiguous requirements, and troubleshoot data issues.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar technologies.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Attention to detail, curiosity, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with semantic layers, shared metric definitions, or data contracts.
  • Experience with modern BI tools such as Sigma, Omni, Tableau, Power BI, or Looker.
  • Familiarity with data ingestion and integration tools such as Fivetran or Matia.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD workflows and automated deployment of analytics code.
  • Experience with Python for scripting or automation.
  • Familiarity with AWS services used for data integration and processing.

As such, Taxwell welcomes and celebrates diversity and inclusion and is committed to equal opportunity employment. title: School Site Coordinator
description:
Gary Community School Corporation is seeking professionals to implement the City Connects program within our school in partnership with Marian University. City Connects, a school-based collaboration among schools, community agencies, and Boston College, is reinvigorating a core function of schools by implementing an innovative model of systemic student support. City Connects assesses the strengths and needs of each student in the school and connects students with a tailored set of supports and resources from inside and outside the school.

The responsibilities of the School Site Coordinators are to:

• Establish and lead a Student Support team and process in the school that identifies and responds to the strengths and personal developmental needs of each and every child in the school.

• Connect students to a range of prevention, early intervention and intensive services programs

that address the physical, emotional, cognitive, and social development of each student.

• Develop and enhance community partnerships with varied community agencies to meet the

identified needs of students, families, and the school.

• Collaborate with school staff, including classroom teachers, to implement the City Connects

model.

• Promote the City Connects model of student support to the school community, families and

community agencies.

• Engage families and caregivers in understanding and supporting the education of their children

and the ways in which academic outcomes are enhanced by serving the social / emotional and

personal development needs of the child.

• Collect data on the implementation of the model and the delivery of services

Minimum Qualifications:

• Master's degree in School Counseling or Social Work

• Licensed School Counselor, Licensed Pupil Adjustment Counselor, or Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LCSW / LICSW) (IDOE Licensed is a plus.)

• Experience working in a school environment

• Evidence of culturally competent practices

• Ability to work collaboratively with a diverse staff, a diverse student body and families, as well as a team of professionals at both the school and the university.

The ideal candidate will possess the following experience and background:

• Experience and/or knowledge of elementary education;

• Communication skills via a second language, especially Spanish;

• Experience with an organization that uses data to guide practice.
