title: Associate Director, Hagler Institute for Advanced Study
description:
Job Title

Associate Director, Hagler Institute for Advanced Study

Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

Hagler Institute for Advanced Study

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.


Who We Are

The Hagler Institute for Advanced Study at Texas A&M University serves as a dynamic catalyst for enriching the intellectual climate and educational experiences at Texas A&M. Annually, we welcome distinguished scholars from around the world into our community, creating a vibrant atmosphere for pioneering research and advanced academic pursuits. By bringing together Texas A&M’s exceptional faculty and students with prestigious scholars from across the globe, we are committed to advancing research productivity and enhancing educational experiences. This collaboration deepens the university’s intellectual climate and contributes to multidisciplinary efforts aimed at solving some of humanity’s most challenging problems. To learn more, visit .


What We Want

The Hagler Institute for Advanced Study is seeking a strategic and collaborative leader to serve as Associate Director and help advance the Institute’s mission of attracting world-renowned scholars and fostering research excellence at Texas A&M University. The ideal candidate will bring strong leadership, financial and administrative expertise, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to build meaningful relationships with faculty, fellows, university leaders, and donors. This individual will play a key role in strategic planning, stakeholder engagement, fundraising efforts, financial oversight, and communicating the Institute’s impact to internal and external audiences.


What You Need To Know

Salary: Compensation will be commensurate to the selected hire’s experience.

A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended.


Other Requirements and Factors:

  • This position allows alternate work location per TAMU guidelines.
  • Work beyond normal office hours and/or on weekends.
  • Travel may be required.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience

  • Doctoral degree in a STEM field, Finance, or Economics.
  • Eight years of related experience in management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Doctoral degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) field, Finance, or Economics.
  • Record of peer-reviewed published scholarship.
  • 10 years or more of experience that includes service as a tenured professor with department head or higher-level administrative and leadership experience.
  • Experience in management and leadership of a significant organization, including responsibility for multimillion dollar budgets.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Commanding verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to effectively communicate with Texas A&M faculty, staff, students, Hagler Institute Fellows, and potential donors.
  • Knowledge of word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
  • Knowledge of management development programs and implementation, budget oversight, and strategic planning.
  • Effective analytical, interpersonal, and organizational skills.

Essential Duties/Tasks

Leadership and Strategic Planning

  • Assists in developing and implementing strategic plans and initiatives for the Hagler Institute.
  • Establishes performance goals and metrics to evaluate the Institute's progress and impact on Texas A&M University.
  • Assists the Director in all major activities of the Hagler Institute related to the recruitment of Fellows and Distinguished Lecturers.
  • Coordinates with departments regarding the terms and conditions of Fellow and Distinguished Lecturer appointments.
  • Negotiates with prospective Hagler Fellows and Distinguished Lecturers and prepares agreements.
  • Assists in the planning and execution of institute events, including developing scripts for the annual Hagler Institute Gala.

Institutional Outreach and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Facilitates relationships with internal and external collaborators, Hagler Fellows, Distinguished Lecturers, donors, and potential donors.
  • Coordinates and attends meetings, as necessary, with college deans, department heads, Texas A&M Foundation development officers, institute directors, potential donors, and other relevant faculty and staff stakeholders.
  • Communicates and assists with meetings involving potential donors and relevant Texas A&M personnel, including Texas A&M Foundation development officers, college deans, and other relevant faculty and staff.
  • Works to strengthen relationships between incoming Fellows and Distinguished Lecturers and the Hagler Institute by meeting with them personally; arranging opportunities for them to attend football games in the Board of Regents Suite; supporting seminars and symposia and providing leadership for the Rogers/Huang Research Collaboration Medal program.
  • Assists with endowment development efforts by identifying potential opportunities, generating ideas, and expanding the Institute's engagement with prospective donors.

Reporting and Analysis

  • Authors and oversees the development of the Institute’s newsletter and other public communications that highlight the work of the Institute.
  • Oversees content development and production of comprehensive annual reports for the Institute’s Administrative Council and External Advisory Board.
  • Assumes primary responsibility for the efficient and timely production of Cornerstone, the Hagler Institute’s annual report, in collaboration with Research Communications.
  • Produces the Hagler Institute’s annual Eminence brochure in collaboration with communications staff at the Texas A&M Foundation.
  • Updates and generates content for the Hagler Institute website, press releases, and other public communications that highlight the work of the Institute.

Budget and Financial Management

  • Provides leadership in evaluating the Hagler Institute’s financial sustainability and determining the availability of funding for new Hagler Fellows and related graduate student fellowships.
  • Leads and oversees the annual budgeting and expense-control processes for the Hagler Institute.
  • Assists with the preparation of budgets for the Hagler Institute.
  • Oversees the development of financial reports and budget analyses for the Director.

Policy and Program Oversight

  • Assists the Director in formulating and implementing policies and procedures related to administration of the Hagler Institute.
  • Ensures the workflow of staff continues at a high level of excellence, consistent with the excellence mission of the Institute.

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

  • Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts, and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums
  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays
  • Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month
  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas
  • Health and Wellness: Free exercise programs and release time
  • Professional Development: All employees have access to free LinkedIn Learning training, webinars, and limited financial support to attend conferences, workshops, and more
  • Educational release time and tuition assistance for completing a degree while a Texas A&M employee
  • Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

title: Maintenance Technologist
description:
Roquette is a family-owned global leader in plant-based ingredients and a leading provider of pharmaceutical excipients.

Want to help us make a difference?
Using plant-based resources, we collaborate with our customers and partners to imagine and offer ingredients to better feed people and treat patients.
Each of our ingredients responds to unique and essential needs, and they enable healthier lifestyles.

We are looking for our next Maintenance Technologist within our Health and Pharma Solutions (HPS) business. The Maintenance Technologist will support the METHOCEL™ manufacturing assets and be responsible for providing maintenance subject matter expertise to resolve plant issues and drive continuous improvement.

This position is located in Midland, MI.


Compensation:

The current salary range for this role is estimated to be $83,000-120,000. In addition, this position may also be eligible to earn performance-based incentive compensation. The specific compensation offered to a candidate will be influenced by a variety of factors including but not limited to skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

What You’ll Do:

· Provides technical expertise to plant personnel on troubleshooting failures, repairs, and evaluating whether equipment is designed to meet its intended or existing service conditions.

· During repairs ensure that repair details such as clearances, tolerances, materials of construction, rebuild procedures, etc. are provided and documented.

· Oversees and provides technical support for the rebuild of critical machinery

· Supports Root Cause Investigations by providing expertise on equipment failure analysis such as design specification, installation, and operational parameters.

· Develops or provides input for the creation of Standard Maintenance Procedures including repair techniques, repair procedures, recommended spares, and training requirements.

· Reviews spare parts list for existing equipment and works with MRO to ensure parts are identified, added, and stocked in the MRO system in support of the maintenance strategy.

· Provides maintainability input for capital projects and other improvement activities.

· Supports reliability in developing the equipment maintenance strategy by providing technical and historical information.

· Assists in specification of spare parts to maintain asset availability requirements.

· Serves as a technical resource to the planner on work packages.

· Supports the Turnaround Work Process with input on scope of work and field support during execution.

· Provides input to the Maintenance Leader in support of maintaining an accurate maintenance budget.

What You’ll Need:

Required Qualifications: · 3+ years of relevant experience in a manufacturing environment or related field

Experience / Skills:

· Experience analyzing equipment failures and providing technical expertise on repair techniques

· Knowledge of SAP Plant Maintenance module or equivalent Maintenance Management System

· Experience supporting planning and execution of maintenance turnarounds of moderate scale

· Experience developing (preferred) or knowledge of maintenance strategy elements including

MRO spare parts management, design for maintainability, and standard maintenance

procedures

· Strong written and communication skills across multiple work groups

· Highly motivated, results-driven, and a self-starter

· Ability to manage multiple projects / tasks at a time

· Skilled in the use of MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) preferred

Work Environment:

· This role spends approximately 50% of the time in an office environment and 50% of the time

in the plant environment. (manufacturing only)

Physical Demands:

· While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to speak or hear. The

employee is frequently required to stand; walk, climb stairs, use hands and fingers to handle or

feel; and reach with hands and arms; work in hot, cold and loud environments. Employee must

be able to wear a respirator. (manufacturing only)

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:

· This is a full-time position. Days and flexible hours of work are required to meet facility

demands.

title: TSD Manager, HPC SEA
description:
Technical Service & Development Manager, Hygiene & Personal Care (HPC), SEA

Arxada is a global leader in innovative solutions that protect our world. Our groundbreaking technologies, in-depth regulatory know-how, manufacturing and process development help our customers to safeguard nutrition, health and infrastructure efficiently through chemistry and biotechnology that enhance sustainability. We offer a broad portfolio of ingredients and services for multiple end-markets that include Human Health & Nutrition, Home & Personal Care, Professional Hygiene, Paints & Coatings and Wood Protection.

With customers in more than 100 countries, the company achieved sales of CHF 2 billion in 2024. Headquartered in Basel (Switzerland), Arxada employs 3,200 associates across 24 production sites and 14 R&D centers, all committed to our customers’ success.

As a Technical Service & Development Manager, Hygiene & Personal Care (HPC), SEA, you will provide application-oriented solution development, technical service and customer support to drive growth across Southeast Asia hygiene and personal care markets. The role partners closely with Business Development, Marketing, Sales, R&D, Regulatory and Product Management to solve customer technical challenges, develop practical solutions and enable successful adoption of Arxada products. Acting as a key technical interface with customers and distribution partners, you will translate customer needs and market insights into value-creating application and growth opportunities. This is an individual contributor role with regional customer project leadership and technical influence responsibilities.

Essential Job Functions:

· Partner with Business Development, Marketing and Sales teams to develop new solutions and support growth initiatives across Southeast Asia hygiene and personal care markets.

· Provide technical support to customers and distribution partners, including product recommendations, formulation guidance, performance evaluation, troubleshooting and application optimization.

· Develop and execute customer-focused technical projects that support new business opportunities, product adoption, customer qualification and market expansion.

· Build strong technical relationships with key customers and distribution partners and act as a trusted technical interface for application and product-related needs.

· Identify customer needs, technical and regulatory trends, and competitive insights, and translate them into technical value propositions, application development opportunities and growth projects.

· Collaborate with Regional and Global R&D, Regulatory, Product Management, Quality and Supply Chain teams to support new product launches, product approvals, customer qualifications and commercialization activities.

· Plan and conduct laboratory work, application testing and performance evaluation, and interpret results to provide practical customer recommendations.

· Prepare technical reports, laboratory data, product application guidance, presentations, training materials and customer-facing technical documentation.

· Deliver technical training, seminars, workshops and customer presentations to strengthen customer capability and position Arxada as a trusted technical partner.

· Manage multiple customer and application projects with clear priorities, ownership and follow-through to business-relevant outcomes.

· Support regional portfolio development, product positioning and commercialization through technical expertise, customer insights and market knowledge.


Business Travel:

  • Regional business travel across Southeast Asia of approximately 30-40% may be required.
  • Regular customer visits, distributor engagement and technical support at customer sites are required.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Microbiology, Biology, Formulation Science, Cosmetic Science or a related discipline; a master's degree is preferred
  • 5-10 years of experience in Technical Service, Application Development, Formulation Development or R&D within Hygiene, Personal Care, Home Care, microbial control, specialty chemicals or related industries
  • Experience in customer-facing technical support, project management and cross-functional collaboration across Southeast Asia
  • Hands-on laboratory capability in experimental design, application testing, data analysis and technical reporting
  • Strong knowledge of personal care and hygiene applications, formulation principles, microbial control solutions and performance requirements
  • Fluency in English is required; proficiency in Thai, Bahasa Malaysia, Bahasa Indonesia, Vietnamese or Mandarin Chinese would be an advantage

Arxada has world class offerings in two distinct areas:

Microbial Control Solutions (MCS) focuses on threats posed by microorganisms to people and planet through five distinct business lines including Professional Hygiene, Home & Personal Care, Wood Protection, Paints & Coatings and Material Protection.

Nutrition, Care & Environmental (NCE), meanwhile, provides materials used to manufacture composites for electronics, aerospace and other markets, as well as vitamins and nutritional ingredients, chemicals and performance intermediates, and raw materials for a wide range of high-performance applications.

Arxada is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a qualified individual with disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

  • Significant experience leading integrated project controls within complex programmes or portfolios.
  • Strong knowledge of planning, cost control, risk management, reporting and assurance disciplines.
  • Deep understanding of programme, portfolio and project management frameworks, governance and controls.
  • Experience leading, developing and coaching high-performing teams.

title: Director, Braftovi/Mektovi Melanoma Strategy & Indication Lead
location: United States - New York - New York City
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Pfizer Commercial Oncology is introducing the world to the next era of cancer care. With a growing portfolio of novel therapies, industry-leading R&D, and a goal of delivering eight breakthroughs by 2030 across major cancer types, we're translating cutting-edge science into market-shaping impact. Here, you'll partner with exceptional colleagues across scientific, medical, and manufacturing teams, backed by advanced digital and AI-enabled infrastructure and the authority to accelerate medicines from discovery to delivery. Guided by our values of courage, excellence, equity, and joy, you'll have the opportunity to stretch your skills and build a career that evolves with you—across teams, roles, and the Pfizer enterprise. Join us to make history — for patients, for their families, for the future.


BRAFTOVI + MEKTOVI is an established cornerstone of Pfizer Oncology’s Precision Medicine & Thoracic Franchise in BRAF V600E/K-mutant metastatic melanoma. The advanced melanoma treatment landscape is complex and dynamic, with many innovative therapies recently launched and more expected to arrive in the near future. In this environment, the melanoma business is focused on defending its position and growing strategically — maintaining the confidence of high-share prescribers, converting new HCPs, protecting access, growing net revenue and market share while the brand moves through the next stage of its lifecycle. For BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma patients who need a targeted therapy combination, ensuring BRAFTOVI + MEKTOVI remains a well-understood and accessible option matters. This role bears significant responsibility for HCP intent and therapy uptake.


This is the senior commercial seat for the melanoma indication and the owner of the melanoma-specific goals. You are expected to set and adapt the overall melanoma strategy, own commercial strategy and execution directly, and carry the indication P&L end-to-end — topline, GTN, NPS, forecasting, latest estimates, and the KPI framework the franchise steers by. You drive the melanoma plan by drawing on shared franchise marketing resources and leading through influence across a broad cross-functional matrix. Within that mandate, the role leads 2027 melanoma Strategic Imperatives - (1) focusing on 2L+ targeted therapy patients to maintain high-share prescribers and grow through HCP conversion, and (2) defending access and managing GTN. This role is also responsible for leading MEKTOVI loss-of-exclusivity strategy and planning. The role also serves as the franchise Competitive Intelligence captain across indications.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead the melanoma strategy and execution

  • Define, adapt, and drive the overall melanoma commercial strategy for BRAFTOVI + MEKTOVI, positioning the brand to defend and strategically grow in a complex and evolving treatment landscape
  • Own melanoma tactical planning and execution end-to-end, drawing on shared franchise marketing resources and ensuring tactics ladder to the melanoma strategic imperatives
  • Lead the melanoma field-based strategy team (FBST), translating brand strategy into field priorities and pull-through
  • Lead cross-functional and leadership updates for the indication; represent melanoma in franchise strategic planning, OP, and LE

Deliver melanoma performance

  • Responsible for melanoma revenue, TRx, NPS, and GTN as the accountable indication lead
  • Lead the melanoma KPI Measurement Framework, instrumenting on prescriber retention, new-HCP conversion, and leading indicators
  • Support melanoma forecasting, latest estimates, and phasing

Strategic Imperative and LOE ownership

  • Lead SI#1 — focus on the 2L+ targeted therapy patient to maintain high-share prescribers and grow through HCP conversion
  • Finalize and implement melanoma lab alerts to drive timely, actionable HCP engagement at key treatment decision points
  • Lead SI#2 — defend access and manage GTN, partnering with the Team Lead on pricing and GTN trade-offs
  • Lead MEKTOVI LOE strategy and planning, owning the go-to-market strategy and associated tactics through the loss-of-exclusivity transition
  • Coordinate with Payer Marketing, Pricing, Contracting, and Account Marketing to ensure access, contracting, and channel strategies support melanoma goals

Lead competitive intelligence and cross-functional partnership

  • Serve as franchise Competitive Intelligence captain across indications, managing the CI vendor partnership; lead melanoma CI strategy and execution, translating insights into brand implications
  • Coordinate and collaborate with melanoma cross-functional partners — field sales, TLELs, Medical, Patient Services, RC, Legal, Regulatory, analytics, and agencies — to meet our goals for patients
  • Serve as Melanoma RBD & Training liaison
  • Develop and coach others, including mentoring junior marketing colleagues

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

  • Bachelor’s degree with 7+ years, MBA/MS with 7+ years, or PhD with 5+ years of marketing, commercial, or related experience
  • US marketing / commercial experience
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, adapt, and execute brand strategy that drives measurable growth
  • Ownership of a commercial P&L, forecast, or KPI framework, with strong analytical and business acumen
  • Strong project leadership across multiple simultaneous priorities, stakeholders, and timelines
  • Proven ability to lead and influence cross-functionally without direct authority
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, including with senior leadership

OTHER JOB DETAILS

Last Date to Apply for Job: October 30, 2026

Eligible for Relocation Package: No

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $176,600.00 to $294,300.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. title: Speech-Language Pathology Assistant
description:
PURPOSE STATEMENT

Under supervision of Language, Speech, and Hearing Therapists, completes a variety of tasks such as activities designed to develop pre-language and language skills, oral-motor control for speech production, vocalization, and use of assistive technology devices for communication; works with students who have identified speech and language disorders as well as other disabilities; performs related duties as assigned.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The list of duties and responsibilities is illustrative only, and is not a comprehensive listing of all the duties and responsibilities performed by this position.
  • Conducts speech and language screenings, without interpretation, and uses screening protocols developed by the Language, Speech, and Hearing Therapists;
  • Provides direct treatment assistance to students at various school sites; follows and implements documented treatment plans or protocols; documents student progress toward meeting established objectives and reports the information to therapists; assists the therapists during assessments by assisting with documentation and completing billing for students receiving direct therapy;
  • Prepares therapy materials such as visual boards, word walls, communication boards, and/or equipment for use in therapy activities;
  • Programs and troubleshoots Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) devices; adapts or modifies instructional materials and/or equipment as determined by student needs and abilities; assists in maintaining student records, tallying data, preparing charts, records, graphs and reports;
  • Observes and reports significant behavioral patterns or other problems to the therapists;
  • Assists in maintaining appropriate behavior between activities;
  • Prepares various teaching materials such as charts, pictures, word lists, and other related items.
  • Collaborates with Supervising Speech Pathologist
  • Attends Case Conferences
  • Attends to other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Associate of arts degree in speech-language pathology or communication disorders, or graduation from a speech- language pathology assistant program; current registration as a Speech-Language Pathology Assistant (SLPA) issued by the State of Indiana and prior SLPA experience in educational or clinical settings is preferred.
  • Knowledge of Speech and language pathology equipment, materials, and procedures; normal speech, language, and hearing development; language disorders and rehabilitation; articulation disorders and rehabilitation; acquired disorders and rehabilitation; terminology related to communicative disorders; learning patterns in children; student behavior management techniques and strategies; learning difficulties of children with special education needs; AAC devices and other assistive technology; English usage, punctuation, spelling, and grammar; basic math skills; routine office procedures and recordkeeping; standard software applications including IPad applications.
  • Skill and Ability to deal effectively with attitudes and behaviors of students; use a variety of screening tools and protocols; appropriately administer and score screening tools; provide effective implementation of therapy objectives; interact and communicate effectively with children and adults from different cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds; work independently with minimal supervision; maintain and troubleshoot assistive equipment; communicate effectively in oral and written form; operate a computer and IPad using standard software applications; react with flexibility and sensitivity to changing situations and needs; organize and prioritize work; effectively carry out written and oral instructions; maintain cooperative work relationships.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  • Ability to speak in a clear and concise manner;
  • Ability to interpret data;
  • Ability to organize and maintain efficiency;
  • Ability to work independently and effectively;
  • Ability to meet daily attendance requirements


EVALUATION:
Performance of this position will be evaluated by the Director or Associate Director of Special Education




PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Sedentary Work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

description:

Position Overview

As a Shift Lead, you will ensure that the vision, culture, and core values of Dutch Bros are upheld on every shift. Schedule:

  • This role requires that you have availability to work a minimum of 32 hours per week.

  • Available to work a flexible, ever-changing schedule that may include early mornings, evenings, and weekends.

Key Result Area (KRA):

Lead the experience for every Broista on shift that ensures a mind-blowing experience for every customer:

  • Cultivate the Dutch Bros atmosphere and standards on shift ensuring that Broistas are meeting all expectations; help solve problems on shift

  • Manage the shift - responsible for ensuring Broistas are prepared for any specials or promotions and have the right energy and attitude for the customer

Be an expert on drink and operational fundamentals to execute Broista training:

  • Primary responsibility is to model and meet all expectations of the Broista role

  • Train new Broistas operationally and culturally while providing a fun-loving, mind-blowing environment

  • Set Broistas up for success by covering all aspects of the Manifesto during training

Aid your Shop Manager and Shop Lead in shop inventory management, support, and other delegated duties:

  • Set up the next shift for success in all areas: counting tills, bank deposits, restocking products, putting inventory away, meeting cleanliness standards, etc.

  • Communicate with your manager and share wins and opportunities for improvement with your shop leaders

  • Be a good role model. Attend mandatory meetings, know your resources, and adhere to all company policies and procedures as laid out in the Shift Lead Field Guide and Employee Handbook

  • Aid the Shop Manager and Shop Leads in Inventory

  • Aid the Shop Lead and Shop Manager in ensuring shop setup and cleanliness standards are met

  • Work with the Shop Lead and Shop Manager in following up with Quality Assurance inspections and accountability process

Levels of Leadership Expectations

Anchor Points

  • Excellent Communicator: Communicate appropriate information up to your leaders, and communicate expectations to the crew while on shift.

  • Available: You must be able to work shift lead shifts and be present at shop meetings and culture building events.

Level-Up Arrow:

Effort + Skill x Attitude = Performance

  • Effort: Giving it your all! Wanting more for yourself and for others. Going above and beyond your own perceived capabilities.

  • Skill: Being a master at the craft. Having high emotional intelligence and a great understanding of people. Keeping a mindset and heart to be a student of the game.

  • Attitude: Have an attitude that is unshakeable. Be resilient and optimistic. “To be so strong that nothing can disturb your peace of mind.

  • Free Dutch Bros swag

  • Free coffee per Employee Drink Policy

Full-time shift lead also receives:

  • Employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Sick time, as applicable by state law

  • Paid time off

  • Paid holidays (6 per year)

*More details on all benefits provided after onboarding

Physical Requirements

  • Constant standing/walking, up to 10 hours at a time

  • Occasional stooping, kneeling, or crawling

  • Occasional pushing, pulling, lifting, or carrying up to 65 lbs

  • Possible exposure to extreme heat and/or cold temperatures

  • Occasional ascending or descending on ladders and ramps

  • Frequent, continual, intermittent flexing, or rotation of the wrist(s) and spine

  • Constantly receiving detailed information through oral communication

  • Constant clarity of vision at near and/or far distances

  • Constant cash handling requiring mental math

  • Constant talking, expressing, or exchanging ideas by means of verbal communication

*Qualifying candidates may be eligible to receive relocation compensation upon acceptance of a job offer that requires them to move. The amount of relocation compensation varies and is based on the total distance of the relocation (among other variables).

Compensation:

$16.50 per hour base pay + an average of $6.00 per hour in tips


What we strive for: a fun environment, great co-workers, and a chance to make a difference in your community. What we don't guarantee: tip averages. Actual tips may vary based on a variety of factors including location, position, hours, and quality of service. Average hourly tips are based on 2025 reporting.

If you like wild growth and working in a unique and fun environment, surrounded by positive community, you'll enjoy your career with us!

  • Knowledge of characteristics of specific health and social concerns and disabilities particularly within the post-secondary context;
  • Solid computer competency including word processing, spreadsheet, database and web-based applications;

title: Program Assistant - Bilingual Preferred
description:
San Diego Youth ServicesJOB ANNOUNCEMENTProgram Assistant - Bilingual Preferred

San Diego Youth Services seeks a Program Assistant in the Community Assessment Team program to be based in San Diego. This is a full-time & non-exempt position reporting to the Program Manager.


San Diego Youth Services: Who we are


San Diego Youth Services has helped improve the lives of more than 834,000 homeless, runaway and vulnerable youth since its beginning in 1970. We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing to more than 16,000 youth every year at 100+ community and school locations. Through prevention, early intervention and treatment, we also help youth before they need higher levels of care or become homeless.


We aim to:

  1. Meet the basic needs of youth. Hunger, poverty and youth homelessness are on the rise for many youth and their families today. We help meet these basic needs for youth. What could be more vital than food and shelter? We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing.
  2. Create positive connection. We help youth focus on positive life changes and healthy relationships as part of providing needed resources and services. San Diego Youth Services has long provided foster homes and adoption support services for families considering adopting a youth in the foster care system.
  3. Help youth develop life skills. In addition to a range of safe and stable housing options, we offer support to help youth develop the independent living skills necessary to become self-sufficient and keep off the streets.
  4. Promote overall health and well-being. Early intervention and care for the whole child are critical. We provide a broad continuum of services to help youth overcome trauma and challenges that put them at risk, including case management, counseling, mental health treatment and educational support and resources.

SDYS has a staff of approximately 200 employees and 90 volunteers working across San Diego County and an annual budget of approximately $24 million.


You can learn more about us at .


CONTEXT OF THE POSITION:


Accountable to Spring Valley & East Communities Campus (SVECC) Program Managers to provide comprehensive trauma-informed services as related to the day-to-day operations of the Community Assessment Team (CAT) program. Responsible for assisting with the general administrative duties including, but not limited to, preparing check requests, data entry, word processing, file and form maintenance, and assistance with data collection and tracking per contract requirements. The goal of the CAT program is to prevent East County youth ages 6-18 from entering or continuing in the juvenile justice system by providing prevention and intervention services for identified at-risk youth and their families. The CAT Program provides services in the home, on school campuses and in the community. Program Assistant is responsible for screening possible intakes, providing intake assessments, crisis management, facilitating appropriate referrals, as well as, community outreach. In addition, responsible for providing prevention and intervention facilitated groups on a variety of topics, including: alcohol and other drug use, teen pregnancy prevention, self-esteem, positive choices, and anger management.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. The development, implementation, and evaluation of an integrated treatment approach for youth with co-occurring psychiatric and substance disorders and quality trauma informed youth programs that adhere to and uphold the rigorous standards of San Diego Youth Services as mandated by its mission, purpose, guiding principles and standards of quality.
  2. Participate in appropriate agency-wide committees as applicable.
  3. Attend and actively participate in all required agency and contract trainings and meetings
  4. Welcome and support volunteers in the organization and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  5. Assist in updating policies and procedures for all above named programs.
  6. Maintain data collection and contract compliance of records as required.
  7. Maintain timely distribution of all incoming and internal mail for the above name programs.
  8. Maintain and order all program office supplies.
  9. Develop forms to standardized operations, replenish all forms as needed and proofread forms, and correspondence.
  10. Operate and maintain office equipment—i.e. computer, copy/fax machine, and coordinate office equipment.
  11. Responsible for filing, copying, scanning and faxing as needed.
  12. Organize timesheets and mileage for the above named programs.
  13. Create flyers for trainings, special events, and activities for the above name programs.
  14. Maintain confidentiality and privacy standards of service partner protected health information and other applicable information and material in accordance to agency policies, applicable regulations and law, including HIPAA.
  15. Work collaboratively and cooperatively with staff and volunteers within the program, the center, the agency, and the community.
  16. Identify eligible families and children residing or receiving schooling within the East Region through outreach to community-based organizations, government agencies, schools, street outreach including other outreach methods as identified during the program period.
  17. Maintain warm, welcoming office grounds and facilities.
  18. Assist in planning, coordination, development, monitoring, and evaluation of services for youth and family.
  19. Provide initial screening, assessment, short-term crisis intervention services and referrals.
  20. Maintain current knowledge of resources and treatment providers within the community to support youth and family needs especially regarding substance abuse treatment programs.
  21. Provide public insurance eligibility screening referrals for families who are uninsured and may be eligible for coverage.
  22. Facilitate trauma informed and strength-based groups on a variety of topics including substance abuse prevention and tobacco use prevention and/or cessation in various settings, such as community-based organizations, schools, and law enforcement facilities.
  23. Maintain program’s space and vehicle cleanliness and safety. Report and coordinate any necessary facility or equipment repairs with Program Manager as needed. With other staff, participate in the maintenance of the day-to-day cleanliness and order of the physical facility and grounds.
  24. Other duties as assigned.
  25. Perform other Duties as assigned or required

SDYS EXPECTATIONS:

  • Adhere to and uphold the rigorous standards of SDYS as mandated by its mission, purpose, guiding principles and standards of quality.
  • Maintain confidentiality and privacy standards of service partner protected health information and other applicable information and material in accordance to agency and center policies, and applicable regulations and laws including HIPAA.
  • Welcome and support SDYS volunteers and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  • Effectively communicate with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Recognize, nurture, and learn from strengths in co-workers.
  • Maintain warm, welcoming and safe work environments.
  • Possess flexibility to accomplish job responsibilities in several work environments, whether it be from home, on the road, or in an office.

PREFERRED EDUCATION, YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS:


Bilingual (Spanish/English) is preferred. Bachelor's Degree in Psychology, Sociology, Criminal Justice, Social Work, or closely related social-service field. Experience with office support and crisis hotline strongly preferred.


Familiar with the Juvenile Justice/Probation and social services systems preferred. Some home-based services experience and knowledge of East County resources is a plus. Ability to de-escalate and respond to crises appropriately. Must be willing to develop or possess working knowledge of trauma-informed care and dual diagnosis treatment; experience working in trauma-informed and dual diagnosis programs preferred. Strong professional oral and written communications skills is a must, as well as, ability to work with minimum supervision and frequent interruptions, while maintaining a professional demeanor at all times. Able to work with multi-disciplinary team in a very diverse setting that serves people of all backgrounds, culture and sexual orientation. Must be computer literate in Microsoft Outlook, Word and Access. Ability to obtain and maintain certification in CPR and First Aid. Must be available to work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends.


Must have reliable vehicle, relevant auto insurance, a clean driving record, and willing to drive (mileage reimbursement available). Employment offer will be subject to clearances, which include fingerprinting, background checks, TB and drug testing.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • The ability to bend at the waist, kneel, or crouch to assist youth.
  • The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand, to exchange accurate information and make presentations.
  • The ability to lift and carry 20 pounds-lifting books, materials, and equipment to execute lessons and presentations.
  • Able to observe details at a close range and interpret the information (such as reading), prepare, and review a variety of documents related to activities of the youth and to be able to monitor youth activities.
  • Sitting or standing (stationary position) for extended periods of time.
  • Traversing extended lengths to move around campuses.
  • Potential exposure to physical injury from aggressive behavior.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.


Hourly Wage Range: $22-$24


FULL-TIME STAFF BENEFITS:

  • PTO: 18 days PTO + 2 floating holidays + 12.5 paid holidays (32.5 paid days off)
  • 403b with 2% employer match
  • Medical, dental, vision, pet insurance
  • Mileage reimbursement
  • $2,000 annual bonus for staff who are fully bilingual in Spanish
  • $1,500 annual bonus for staff with proficiency in Spanish

To apply, please send resume and cover letter through job posting on SDYS website.


SDYS offers a comprehensive benefits package to full time employees that includes generous PTO, personal holidays, health, vision, dental, life insurance, parental leave and a 403(b)-retirement plan with matching contribution. SDYS is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) employer.


All are welcome at San Diego Youth Services.


As an organization working to meet the basic needs of youth, create positive connections, help youth develop life skills, and promote overall health and well-being, SDYS believes its practices and actions must reflect the highest level of commitment to access, equity, and social justice.


The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, innovation, self-expression, and talent that our members invest in their work represents not only part of the SDYS’ culture, but the SDYS’ reputation and achievements as well. SDYS remains open to feedback from all communities it touches and knows that input from those with direct experience of issues will make the SDYS more effective in achieving its goals.


SDYS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. AECOM is seeking an experienced and driven Electrical Lead Project Manager to lead the planning, coordination, and execution of mechanical systems in data center construction projects. The ideal candidate will bring expertise, leadership, and a commitment to excellence to deliver projects that meet and exceed client expectations. This position will be on site in McGregor, TX.

description:
Introduction

The ASML Business Information team in the Netherlands helps transform complex data into meaningful insights that support business decisions across the organization. As a Data Science | Engineering intern: optimizing business processes, you will work in a dynamic environment where priorities evolve based on business needs and operational challenges. This internship offers the opportunity to improve processes, enhance data solutions, and contribute to projects that create measurable impact. You will collaborate with experienced professionals while developing both your technical and professional skills. To achieve this, we leverage a range of technologies and programming languages, including Power BI, Spotfire, Azure Databricks, SQL, and the Azure Cloud. If you enjoy solving problems, exploring data, and taking initiative, this internship could be the right opportunity for you.

Your assignment

As a Data Science | Engineering intern: optimizing business processes, you will support initiatives that improve efficiency, reliability, and scalability of business processes and data solutions. You will work on a variety of assignments rather than a single predefined project, giving you the opportunity to apply your analytical and technical skills across different business challenges. You will investigate problems, identify improvement opportunities, and help deliver solutions that create value for stakeholders.


Your main responsibilities will be:

  • Analyze large datasets and translate findings into actionable business insights.
  • Investigate process inefficiencies and perform root cause analyses.
  • Improve data pipelines, data quality, and process automation solutions.
  • Develop tools and solutions that simplify workflows and increase efficiency.
  • Design, build, and maintain scalable data models and databases.
  • Conduct qualitative and quantitative research to support improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to identify business needs and recommend data-driven solutions.

This is a bachelor/master non-thesis internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 4 days per week (2 days on-site). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027.


Your profile

To be suitable for the internship, you:

  • Are pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, data science, engineering, business information technology, or a related field.
  • Have experience with programming and data analysis using tools such as SQL, Python, Power BI, Mendix or similar technologies.
  • Are analytical and able to investigate complex problems using a structured approach.
  • Demonstrate initiative, ownership, and the ability to work independently.
  • Communicate effectively in English and collaborate with a variety of stakeholders.
  • Are curious, proactive, and eager to contribute ideas that improve business outcomes.

Additional requirements:

  • You are enrolled at an educational institution throughout the entire internship period.
  • You are located in the Netherlands during the internship, or you are willing to relocate before the start date.
  • If you are a non-EU citizen studying in the Netherlands, your educational institution must be able to support the internship documentation requirements.

Join ASML through this internship and gain hands-on experience in a data-driven environment where your contributions can directly influence business performance. This internship offers exposure to real business challenges, collaboration with experienced professionals, and opportunities to develop valuable technical and stakeholder management skills.

This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the United States Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. title: GenAI Fullstack Engineer
description:
Marlabs, a global AI and Digital Solutions Consulting firm, delivers intelligent solutions across AI, data, analytics, and product engineering. Since 2000, we have partnered with some of the largest healthcare, life sciences, financial services, and government organizations worldwide. As we continue to expand our global footprint, we have an exciting opportunity for a highly skilled GenAI Fullstack Engineer to join our innovative and dynamic team.

This position requires onsite 5 days/week

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | About the Role

As a GenAI Fullstack Engineer, you will design and build scalable enterprise applications that combine robust Java-based backend engineering with modern Generative AI capabilities. You will work across Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Python, FastAPI, LLMs, RAG, and Vector Databases to develop production-ready AI services and integrate them with enterprise applications. The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer who has expanded into hands-on GenAI engineering and can develop secure, scalable solutions spanning traditional backend services, AI orchestration, enterprise knowledge retrieval, and LLM-powered applications.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Day-to-Day

  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend applications and REST APIs using Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Spring Security, and Spring Data/JPA.
  • Build and integrate production-grade GenAI and LLM applications, connecting AI services with existing Java/Spring Boot enterprise applications and business systems.
  • Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, indexing, semantic search, context retrieval, reranking, and response generation.
  • Develop AI services and orchestration components using Python and FastAPI, leveraging frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or Hugging Face to support reusable enterprise AI capabilities.
  • Implement and optimize Vector Databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, FAISS, or ChromaDB to enable enterprise knowledge retrieval and semantic search.
  • Integrate LLM platforms such as Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Claude, Gemini, or Llama, applying prompt engineering, response evaluation, guardrails, and optimization techniques to improve solution accuracy and reliability.
  • Build secure and observable AI/backend services by implementing authentication, authorization, exception handling, logging, monitoring, API security, and production-grade engineering standards.
  • Containerize and deploy applications using Docker and CI/CD pipelines, collaborating with architects, data engineers, developers, and business teams to deliver reliable and scalable GenAI solutions.

GenAI Fullstack Engineer | Skills & Experience

  • Strong software engineering 3+ years experience with Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, and REST APIs, including hands-on experience designing scalable and distributed enterprise backend applications.
  • Hands-on experience developing production GenAI/LLM applications, including LLM integration, prompt engineering, response evaluation, and enterprise AI use cases.
  • Strong production experience with RAG architectures, including embeddings, document ingestion, chunking, semantic retrieval, reranking, context construction, and RAG quality optimization.
  • Strong working knowledge of Python and FastAPI, with experience building AI/ML services and integrating Python-based AI components with Java/Spring Boot applications.
  • Hands-on experience with Vector Databases and GenAI frameworks, such as Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch, FAISS, ChromaDB, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or Hugging Face.
  • Experience with cloud and modern deployment practices, including AWS, Azure, or GCP, Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, observability, and production deployment of AI services.
  • Additional exposure to Agentic AI, MCP (Model Context Protocol), AI guardrails, LLMOps, Kubernetes, knowledge graphs, multimodal AI, and event-driven microservices is advantageous.

title: Thin Films Module Engineering - PhD Intern
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

The Role and Impact


As a Module Engineering PhD Intern, you will play a key role in developing and sustaining semiconductor manufacturing processes for a specific module. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include supporting equipment troubleshooting, performing maintenance and qualification activities, and collaborating with engineering teams to optimize process control methodologies. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in semiconductor manufacturing while building essential skills for a future career in engineering.

Business group


You will join the Intel Foundry team, a dynamic and innovative group dedicated to delivering cutting-edge manufacturing solutions that drive Intel's technology forward. The team focuses on advancing semiconductor fabrication processes in areas such as Diffusion, Dielectrics, Implant, EPI, and FE Metals. As part of this group, you will contribute to Intel's mission of creating world-changing technology that enables global progress and enriches lives.


What We Do

As members of the Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) team, we are responsible for improving process capability for multiple technology nodes (Intel 18A, Intel 3, Intel 12nm and upcoming technologies) from initial product qualification through high volume manufacturing. The focus will be on delivering yield improvement, performance enhancement, variation and cost reduction.

Key Responsibilities



  • Assist with the development and implementation of thin film manufacturing processes for a specific module within Intel's semiconductor production.
  • Support troubleshooting and maintenance activities for manufacturing equipment to ensure optimal performance.
  • Participate in equipment qualification processes, ensuring compliance with quality and functional standards.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to optimize process control methodologies and achieve production targets.
  • Establish strong working relationships and partner closely with technology development, high volume manufacturing and cross-functional stakeholders to achieve common goals.
  • Analyze data trends, identify solutions for process improvement and drive automation improvements (using AI where applicable)
  • Contribute to sustaining and improving manufacturing tools and processes while gaining hands-on experience in semiconductor engineering.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


  • Currently pursuing a PhD degree in a relevant STEM discipline (e.g. Physics, Applied Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, etc.).
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience writing software code for application in above majors
  • Excellent communication skills - both written and verbal.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a diverse, high-performing team.
  • Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and disciplined approach to procedures.
  • Data analysis skills with demonstrated ability to construct clear data-based problem statements, design of experiment.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience with data analysis tools and software (e.g. JMP, Python, Excel, and AI tools).
  • Ability to summarize data for technical and non-technical audiences.


Please note, the ideal candidate will be open to work a 6-month internship schedule beginning the Spring of 2027 through December 2027.


This is your chance to join a global leader in semiconductor manufacturing, gain real-world experience, and contribute to innovative solutions that shape the future of technology. If you are ready to learn, grow, and make an impact, we encourage you to apply today.

If you are safety driven, physically capable, experienced in power line construction or eager to develop in the trade, join our Utilities team in Alberta today!

The Hub Project is accepting applications for an internship on the abortion campaign to support the campaign’s efforts to fight back against attacks on our reproductive freedoms and rights. title: Senior Manager - Real Estate Strategy and Planning
description:
Position Overview:

The Cigna Group is seeking an experienced transformational leader to serve as Senior Manager, Portfolio Strategy & Planning within Global Workplace Programs (GWP). This leader will align the company's workplace portfolio, workforce requirements, technology, and business priorities to improve employee experience, portfolio performance, and real estate efficiency.


The Senior Manager will lead workplace and occupancy strategies, including space planning, utilization analytics, workplace solutions, and change leadership. Working across GWP, Human Resources, Enterprise Technology, Finance, and business leadership, this role will translate enterprise priorities into scalable workplace strategies, consistent standards, and actionable portfolio decisions across offices and other workplace environments.


The ideal candidate combines strategic judgment, analytical problem-solving, broad functional knowledge, and strong execution discipline. The role requires an enterprise mindset, excellent communication skills, and the emotional intelligence to build alignment across diverse stakeholders while leading teams through complex change.


Key Responsibilities:

· Develop and maintain a 5- to 10-year workplace and real estate portfolio strategy aligned with enterprise, workforce, talent, and financial priorities.

· Collaborate on the global occupancy and space planning capability, establishing consistent demand-planning processes, space standards, governance, and service delivery expectations.

· Evaluate portfolio, workforce, and utilization data to recommend optimal square footage, employee-to-desk ratios, collaboration capacity, adjacencies, workplace zoning, and site-level solutions.

· Translate business growth, organizational change, workforce forecasts, and attendance expectations into actionable occupancy plans and real estate requirements.

· Advise senior leaders on portfolio utilization, workplace investments, sequencing decisions, trade-offs, risks, and actions required to align the physical footprint with enterprise strategy.

· Facilitate cross-functional planning and prioritization across GWP functions, including portfolio strategy, transactions, design, workplace experience, facilities operations, capital project delivery, analytics, governance, and change leadership.

· Establish enterprise workplace principles and standards that balance employee experience, business purpose, operational resilience, cost, and flexibility.

· Build change leadership and stakeholder-engagement roadmaps that prepare leaders and employees for workplace, occupancy, and portfolio changes and support successful adoption.

· Identify and implement leading practices, tools, benchmarks, and process improvements that strengthen workplace strategy and occupancy management performance.

· Measure outcomes through clearly defined portfolio, utilization, employee experience, financial, and delivery metrics, and communicate progress to senior leadership.


Minimum Qualifications:

· Bachelor's degree in business, real estate, architecture, planning, operations management, analytics, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

· Demonstrated experience leading workplace strategy, occupancy planning, space planning, portfolio planning, or a closely related corporate real estate function.

· Experience translating business and workforce requirements into long-range portfolio and workplace strategies.

· Strong analytical capability and demonstrated success using data to solve complex problems, evaluate alternatives, and support executive decisions.

· Proven ability to build trusted relationships and collaborate across business, HR, Technology, Finance, and real estate stakeholders.

· Strong executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex concepts clear, concise, and actionable.

· Ability to lead challenging conversations calmly, objectively, and with a solutions-oriented approach.

· Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills, with the ability to move between strategic direction and execution detail.


Preferred Qualifications:

· Master's degree in business, real estate, architecture, planning, organizational change, or a related discipline.

· Experience leading enterprise-wide business integration, workplace transformation, portfolio optimization, or technology-enabled operating model initiatives.

· Experience with workplace and portfolio technology platforms, utilization analytics, scenario modeling, and performance reporting.

· Demonstrated ability to lead and influence within a highly collaborative, multidisciplinary, and matrixed organization.

· Results-oriented leadership style with the ability to engage deeply in critical details while motivating teams and maintaining an enterprise perspective.

· Broad understanding of corporate real estate, workplace experience, change leadership, design, project delivery, facilities operations, finance, and the interdependencies among these functions.

· Exceptional written, verbal, and listening skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences.

The Long-Term Substitute Teacher is responsible for providing classroom coverage for a teacher/counselor who is absent for an extended period of time. The long-term substitute works the regular hours of the absent classroom teacher/ counselor during his/her absence. Guides the learning process toward the achievement of the District curriculum and goals in an effective manner, ensuring a safe classroom environment, proper classroom management, and maintaining reasonable rules of conduct encouraging self-discipline and responsibility. Serves as a positive role model for students, demonstrating professionalism that includes a positive attitude, positive and respectful communication, and professional appearance.

  • Deliver lesson plans as instructed by the regular classroom teacher and/or school administrators, including taking daily attendance.
  • Ensure safety and wellbeing of all students within the assigned classroom and appropriately respond to all emergency situations following all necessary and reasonable safety precautions to protect students, equipment, material, and facilities.
  • Maintains a professional and positive rapport with all students, staff, administration and others.
  • Maintains order and discipline in the classroom conductive to effective learning.
  • Clearly communicates expectations and adapts to individual learning needs, providing individual and small group instruction.
  • Strive to implement assistive technology in instruction and meet individual student needs.
  • Actively participate in professional development sessions.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

  • The daily rate for this position is $300.15 ($329.83 w/ TRS) effective after 15 days of continuous employment in the same assignment; retroactive to 1st day of assignment.

title: Paraeducator - MAC
description:
Position / Title: Paraeducator MultiAbilities Classroom (including multilingual classrooms)
Bargaining Unit: DUEADepartment/Location: Specialized Student Services
Calendar Days: 192Reports To: Building Principal
JD Revision Date: 12/1/2025Supervises: N/A

Function / Position Summary

The Multi Abilities Classroom (MAC) paraeducator supports the classroom by assisting in the implementation of structured instructional, behavioral, social and communication supports aligned to the MAC curriculum and practices. Provide direct support to students with significant academic learning, communication and behavioral needs, including assistance with personal care, feeding and toileting as required. Perform duties under the direct supervision of a certified staff member, contribute to a consistent, hands on and supportive learning environment while maintaining confidentiality of student, staff and department information.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

  • Implement individual or small group instructional activities under the direction of the MAC teacher, using established routines, visual supports and structured practices.
  • Familiarize yourself with student IEP goals, objectives, accommodations and behavior supports to assist with consistent implementation across the school day.
  • Support the use of communication systems, visual schedules, reinforcement systems and other structured supports that align with MAC expectations and individual student needs.
  • Follow through on defined behavioral intervention plans and procedures, including implementation of proactive strategies, reinforcement systems and de-escalation supports as directed by the teacher.
  • Assist with data collection, including academic, behavioral, social and communication data, and document information as requested by the teacher.
  • Support a structured classroom environment by preparing, organizing and maintaining materials and assisting with environmental setup as directed by the teacher.
  • Supervise students during lunch, recess, arrival, departure and community-based activities.
  • Escort students within the building, including transitions to specials/electives, therapies and other instructional spaces.
  • Assist with the loading and unloading of student buses during assigned work hours.
  • Work cooperatively with the teacher by assisting with any activity aligned to student IEP needs, including instructional tasks, communication supports, social skills and behavior routines.
  • Provide personal care support to students, including lifting, transferring, positioning, feeding, toileting and hygiene needs, consistent with special skills expectations.
  • Support students in building independence, communication, self-regulation and engagement throughout the school day.
  • Provide input to the teacher regarding student responses, communication attempts, behavior patterns and other needs.
  • Attend staff meetings and professional development activities as assigned
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, staff and department information within the school and community.
  • Be willing to complete and maintain certification in CPI and Ukeru to support safe, proactive approaches to behavior support.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education

  • Para Educator, Substitute, Professional Educator or Provisional Educator License required.
  • Minimum education requirement for a Para Educator license is completion of at least 60 semester hours of college course work or a passing score on the ETS Para Pro exam or two specific Work Keys exams.
  • Bilingual – Spanish/English (written/verbal) preferred.
  • Assignments in multi-lingual or bilingual classrooms require Bilingual-Spanish/English

Experience / Knowledge

  • 3 years of Para Educator experience or classroom assistant for students with disabilities preferred
  • Experience with students who have behavioral needs preferred
  • Experience as a Behavior technician or Registered Behavior Technician strongly preferred
  • Ability to collaborate with staff and students in a way that is collaborative, student friendly and productive
  • Familiarity with data collection preferred

Physical Demands

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work through many interruptions throughout the school day
  • Required prolonged standing, bending, start/stop and sitting
  • Lifting may be required to manually move, carry, pull or push heavy objects or materials
  • Assisting with toileting needs may be required as needed
  • Ability to perform CPI approved restraint once trained
  • Excellent physical agility and quick response time

Terms of Employment

  • This is a 9-month position.
  • Salary and benefits are established by the Board of Education and set forth in the collective bargaining agreement as applicable.
  • The starting rate for this role is $23.38/hr.

Have a front row seat at the human side of insurance

As a Commercial Property Loss Adjuster, you'll manage a caseload of commercial property damage claims across the Midlands region from visiting customer sites, co-ordinating visits from contractors, to finally settling each claim.


Imagine yourself stepping into people's lives during some of their most unsettling moments: a burst pipe that flooded the shop, a fire that scorched restaurant kitchen, trees fallen through the roof from storm damage. description:
Our customers can find fresh food, healthy snack choices, and helpful employees. We strive to serve our local communities through kind and clean in-store service and community involvement. Enmarket is passionate about bringing healthy options to our customers and promoting healthy initiatives.

We have 128 locations across Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina and we are continuing to grow, which means new career opportunities!

Enmarket is looking for fresh and friendly faces to help us enrich life. If you are customer service oriented and highly motivated with a positive attitude, we hope you’ll consider joining our team.

If you have a good attitude, like working with people and are ready to work hard, you have come to the right place. We are committed to hiring quality people and taking good care of them so they will take good care of our customers. Customers visit our stores for much more than a good value on gasoline and products, they come for the value of a warm smile and courteous welcome.

GENERAL SUMMARY

The Store Manager has an ultimate responsibility for the day-to-day store operations including and not limited to car wash and food service operation, store profitability, budget, expense control, inventory levels, shortage control, customer service and safety scheduling, training and supervising employees.

PRINCIPLE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Workforce Management and Development

  • Recruit, interview, hire, train, and develop all store staff

  • Demonstrate leadership and promote teamwork

  • Motivate staff to continually improve performance

  • Effectively address employee relations issues

  • Provide performance feedback and coaching to store employees

  • Conduct regular performance evaluations, coaching, and counseling of store employees

  • Require personal grooming and appearance at all times

  • Exhibit personal accountability for every action

  • Ensure that all store employees know and follow all company policies and procedures

  • Supervise all hourly employees to clock in and clock out and assure their time properly reported to payroll

  • Post work schedule as per Company policy

Financials and Sales

  • Develop and execute site level operating budget

  • Responsible and accountable for the steady improvement of store profitability and the delivery of budgeted financial objectives.

  • Responsible for maximizing store sales and gasoline volume at the location in accordance with company guidelines and objectives.

  • Monitor retail gasoline prices to stay on strategy.

  • Ensure product mix and inventory levels are properly maintained in order to increase sales volume and control inventory

  • Stock shelves and refrigerated coolers

  • Accountable for minimizing the loss of cash and inventory and operating within assigned shrink targets.

  • Ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal laws within the scope of the convenience/food store operation

  • Be directly responsible for all fund reconciliation and inventory audits

  • Prepare or supervise preparation of all required paperwork

Customer Service

  • Provide the best customer experience to every customer

  • Greet every customer with a smile and sincere greeting

  • Suggest possible purchases to the customers and promote specials

  • Assume full responsibility for the execution of our customer service program at the site level

Safety & Station Appearance

  • Responsible for doing what is necessary to minimize the safety risks to employees, customers and suppliers. Assure that all site employees are adequately trained on safety policies and procedures and maintains adequate controls to verify compliance to these

  • Assure all environmental and hazardous material regulations are strictly enforced

  • Maintain safety and security of the store and document any accidents or incidents that occur

  • Manage the maintenance of the customer environment inside and around the perimeter of the store

  • Operate all assigned equipment safely and efficiently

  • support implementation of our Safety and Health program

  • Promptly Report and investigate workplace accidents, injuries, incidents, or illnesses involving employees within the location

  • Complete the new employee safety orientation procedure with all new or transferred employees working at the store

  • Regularly inspect stores in your area of responsibility for workplace hazards and initiate corrective action immediately

  • Encourage employees to report unsafe conditions or work practices and initiate corrective action

  • Promote a quick return to work for employees under your supervision

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 1-3 years of management experience in convenience store, retail, fast food, or restaurant operations

  • Budget and P&L understanding

  • Ability to effectively perform in a fast-paced work environment

  • Strong leadership and interpersonal skills

  • State of Maine Applicants Only: UST Class A/B Certification is a MUST or ability to become certified within the first 30 days of employment

  • Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization

  • Must be able to provide any level of coverage if needed, including nights, weekends, and/or holidays

  • Ability to bend down, stoop low, and also stand for at least 8 hours

  • Ability to properly lift, pull and/or push up to 30 lbs.

  • Successful completion of certification testing as needed

  • MS Outlook, Word, and Excel skills

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ensures physical maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and attractiveness of all store facilities

  • Performs other related duties as required

  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times

  • Must be able to traverse and access all areas of the store

  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer

  • Prolonged periods of standing and working at a cash register
