When we put our heads together, we can do brilliant work. And when we do brilliant work, we can achieve remarkable things for patients as we positively transform healthcare. Our Trial Vendor Senior Managers have direct impact on the success of our clinical trials and the management of our critical vendors.


Job Description

As a core member of the Clinical Trial Team (CTT), the Trial Vendor Manager (TVM) serves as the CTT vendor sub-team lead, providing direct operational management and oversight of clinical trial vendors to deliver study outcomes in accordance with schedule, budget, quality, compliance, and performance standards. The TVM is accountable for vendor service delivery at the study level and collaborates closely with the Vendor Start-up Manager (VSM) across major clinical vendor categories, including central labs, eCOA/ePRO, IRT, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, patient recruitment and retention (PR&R), and imaging. During study start-up, the TVM applies technical and operational expertise to translate protocol requirements into clear vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs), helping to ensure timely study initiation.


You will proactively manage vendor-related risks and potential issues and implement global vendor strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the single point of contact for vendor service delivery at the study level, partnering with vendors and cross-functional teams within the Clinical Trial Team (CTT)
  • Provide direct, end-to-end operational oversight of clinical trial vendor deliverables, ensuring alignment with study timelines, scope, quality, and compliance expectations across major vendor categories, including central labs, IRT, eCOA/ePRO, imaging, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, and PR&R.
  • Review vendor-related protocol sections during protocol development and partner with the Vendor Start-up Manager to translate protocol requirements into accurate vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs).
  • Oversee vendor financials, including forecasting, budget tracking, validation of work performed, service confirmations, invoice reconciliation, and purchase order management and close-out.
  • In collaboration with vendors, study start up leads and vendor start up managers, ensure that all key vendor deliverables and documentation are in place to support submission during study start-up
  • Lead UAT activities for vendor systems (e.g., eCOA, IRT), and contribute to vendor system validation
  • Drive site activation from a vendor perspective, compile vendor related central documents, and address risks/issues during site activation and throughout the life-cycle of a site
  • Manage vendor performance against agreed KPIs, proactively identify risks and issues, drive corrective actions and mitigation plans with vendors and study teams, and maintain complete, inspection-ready oversight documentation.

Essential Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences or equivalent; advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years’ clinical operations experience, including direct operational management and oversight of clinical trial vendors across one or more major service categories such as central labs, IRT, eCOA/ePRO, or imaging.
  • Strong knowledge of GxP and ICH regulations, clinical trial design, and supplier service specifications.
  • Proficiency in vendor management, contracting, and site-related collaborations, including UAT for eCOA and IRT systems.
  • Results-driven with proven ability to complete projects within timelines.
  • Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, problem-solving, and communication skills in a matrixed environment.
  • Demonstrated networking abilities, team collaboration, and decision-making capabilities.
  • Strong scientific curiosity and good knowledge of working on Clinical Trials with an Oncology focus, would be highly beneficial

title: General Manager - Store CAN6844
description:
Job Description

A General Manager must be committed to inspiring our team, as well as helping our Customers succeed and growing our business with integrity. Professional level sales and management position capable of supporting functions on both sides of the business. The role requires understanding of store systems, automotive systems, parts knowledge and has the ability to identify, troubleshoot and project assist for DIY. Responsible for developing and maintaining Professional Customer relationships and program growth. Is accountable for achieving financial metrics and maintaining service and appearance standards. Position is exempt and requires a minimum of 50-55 hours per week (excluding meal break periods). The average schedule is 5-6 days a week, 11 hour shifts, including rotating nights and weekends, with an hour for lunch. Additional hours may be required based on staffing, store conditions, sales to target, and other business demands. General Managers are required to work a schedule based on the needs of the business.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Achieve overall store sales goals and service objectives
  • Manage and grow Professional Customer relationships/sales, including building and holding team accountable to executing Customer action plans
  • Selection, hiring, development, performance mgmt., coaching, scheduling and engagement of store Team Members
  • Ensure execution of all inventory and operational standards
  • Coach all Team Members to deliver on Customer expectations (DIY and Professional)
  • Manager on duty responsibilities (touch base/coaching, floor/phone mgmt., task assignment and completion, safety, open/close duties)
  • Ability to lead change management
  • Embrace diversity and foster a respectful environment for both Customers and Team Members

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Provide DIY service including battery installation, testing, wiper install, etc.
  • Assist District/Region in other functions upon request

Success Factors

  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Ability to become ASE P2 certified or ASE ready equivalent
  • Ability to execute and train project and product quality recommendations
  • Advanced parts lookup and sourcing
  • Ability to source from numerous places including special order, FDO, second source, etc.
  • Ability to execute and train all store operational processes and procedures, and testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY services
  • Ability to execute and train inventory systems and store equipment
  • Ability to execute and train POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Ability to review and analyze P&L statement
  • Ability to recruit, select, hire and develop quality Team Members
  • Ability to build and grow relationships with Professional Customers

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a General Manager

  • Working knowledge of automotive systems preferred
  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with Customers, peers and upper management
  • Use Microsoft software effectively (Word, Excel required; PowerPoint preferred)
  • Calculate figures and amounts such as discounts, percentages, sales increases, and gross profit percent
  • Ability to review and analyze business reports, such as profit and loss statement (P&L)
  • Hold others accountable, inspect work quality and give feedback in a way that is inspiring
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a General Manager up for Success

  • 2-3 years of experience managing a team of 10 - 20 Team Members in a fast-paced and highly dynamic retail environment
  • Successful experience managing profitability; proven financial and business acumen

Education, Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

High school diploma or general education degree (GED), Bachelor’s degree in business or a related area preferred.

Must have a valid driver's license

ASE certification preferred, but not required

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: Safety & Security Specialist - Transit
description:
AECOM's Transportation, Boston Area Business Line is actively seeking a creative, highly talented Safety & Security Specialist - Transit for immediate employment in the Boston region. The selected individual will lead risk management tasks for transit projects across the U.S., applying FTA processes and APTA standards. The role drives SMS-based hazard management, safety risk assessment, corrective action oversight, and regulatory compliance to strengthen safety performance and culture.

This role is intended for a talented Safety Specialist who is looking to expand their technical capabilities while developing skills in the delivery of projects. This is a hybrid position, combining office and remote work.

The successful candidate will bring strong technical fundamentals, intellectual curiosity, and a proactive mindset, with the ability to take ownership of defined tasks and progressively grow into leading small scopes and teams.

The job responsibilities of the position will include but are not limited to:

  • Lead hazard identification, risk evaluation, and mitigation (e.g., PHAs/TVAs), track corrective actions, and validate effectiveness.
  • Develop and manage CEL/CIL and DCCC/CSCC documents to ensure thorough technical closure of findings with design disciplines.
  • Conduct hazard analysis, facilitate multi-disciplinary workshops, collaborate with cross functional teams to identify, assess and mitigate safety risk and document findings.
  • Prepare SSC plans, documents, and reports; conduct peer reviews and assist with SSC training.
  • Support System Safety & Security Certification and SSPP compliance; produce monthly safety/security progress reports.
  • Track and monitor hazards; align CDRLs with the PMP and related project documents.
  • Support State Safety Oversight of rail transit agencies through compliance reviews, annual report development, data verification, hazard-management, event-investigation review, and CAP monitoring.
  • Engage directly with agency clients SSO’s and project managers.
  • Provide field safety oversight for construction, maintenance, and transit facility projects
  • Under minimal direction supervises personnel engaged in the ES&H functions within the company or on the same project.
  • Provides technical leadership and functional guidance to ensure regulatory standards are being enforced.
  • Ensures that quality control procedures are executed to monitor all aspects of regulations.
  • Drafts all necessary reports to Federal, State and local agencies.
  • Communicates programs to enhance employee awareness of prevention and compliance.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • BA/BS in Construction Management, Industrial Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Safety Studies or related field + 10 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
  • Proven experience applying FTA processes and APTA standards
  • 10 years of related experience of driving SMS-based hazard management, safety risk assessment, corrective action oversight, and regulatory compliance to strengthen safety performance and culture

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Masters Degree in Construction Management, Industrial Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Safety Studies or related field
  • Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Construction Health and Safety Technician (CHST)
  • OSHA 10-hour Construction Health and Safety Course
  • Initial and Annual Refresher OSHA 29 CFR 1910.120/1926.65 HAZWOPER
  • Knowledgeable in OSHA 29 CFR 1926 and 1910 Regulations
  • Knowledgeable in use of eBuilder
  • Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
  • Relocation assistance is not available.

Function / Position Summary

The Multi Abilities Classroom (MAC) paraeducator supports the classroom by assisting in the implementation of structured instructional, behavioral, social and communication supports aligned to the MAC curriculum and practices. Provide direct support to students with significant academic learning, communication and behavioral needs, including assistance with personal care, feeding and toileting as required. Perform duties under the direct supervision of a certified staff member, contribute to a consistent, hands on and supportive learning environment while maintaining confidentiality of student, staff and department information.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

  • Implement individual or small group instructional activities under the direction of the MAC teacher, using established routines, visual supports and structured practices.
  • Familiarize yourself with student IEP goals, objectives, accommodations and behavior supports to assist with consistent implementation across the school day.
  • Support the use of communication systems, visual schedules, reinforcement systems and other structured supports that align with MAC expectations and individual student needs.
  • Follow through on defined behavioral intervention plans and procedures, including implementation of proactive strategies, reinforcement systems and de-escalation supports as directed by the teacher.
  • Assist with data collection, including academic, behavioral, social and communication data, and document information as requested by the teacher.
  • Support a structured classroom environment by preparing, organizing and maintaining materials and assisting with environmental setup as directed by the teacher.
  • Supervise students during lunch, recess, arrival, departure and community-based activities.
  • Escort students within the building, including transitions to specials/electives, therapies and other instructional spaces.
  • Assist with the loading and unloading of student buses during assigned work hours.
  • Work cooperatively with the teacher by assisting with any activity aligned to student IEP needs, including instructional tasks, communication supports, social skills and behavior routines.
  • Provide personal care support to students, including lifting, transferring, positioning, feeding, toileting and hygiene needs, consistent with special skills expectations.
  • Support students in building independence, communication, self-regulation and engagement throughout the school day.
  • Provide input to the teacher regarding student responses, communication attempts, behavior patterns and other needs.
  • Attend staff meetings and professional development activities as assigned
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, staff and department information within the school and community.
  • Be willing to complete and maintain certification in CPI and Ukeru to support safe, proactive approaches to behavior support.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education

  • Bilingual – Spanish/English (written/verbal) preferred.

Experience / Knowledge

  • 3 years of Para Educator experience or classroom assistant for students with disabilities preferred
  • Experience with students who have behavioral needs preferred
  • Experience as a Behavior technician or Registered Behavior Technician strongly preferred
  • Ability to collaborate with staff and students in a way that is collaborative, student friendly and productive
  • Familiarity with data collection preferred

Physical Demands

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work through many interruptions throughout the school day

  • Lifting may be required to manually move, carry, pull or push heavy objects or materials
  • Assisting with toileting needs may be required as needed

Terms of Employment

  • Salary and benefits are established by the Board of Education and set forth in the collective bargaining agreement as applicable.

title: Build Quality Principal
description:
PBM Build Quality Principal

In-Factory Quality Engineering, Automation & Release Evidence

Job Description

PBM Build Quality Principal will lead execution of the program’s quality strategy across platform and product engineering builds. Working within the standards established by the PBM Test Architect Principal, this role is accountable for unit, contract, regression, evaluation, and automation testing, as well as the evidence required to demonstrate that releases meet agreed entry and exit criteria. The Principal will establish a consistent quality bar across New PBM Platform engineering teams and drive quality earlier into design and development.

This role partners closely with Product and Platform Engineering, Delivery, DevSecOps, Architecture, Test Data Engineering, the PBM Test Lead, and the PBS test organization. The Principal provides deep quality-engineering expertise, leads contractors or matrixed contributors where required, identifies systemic risks, and advances automation and responsible AI-enabled testing practices to improve release confidence, speed, and reliability.

Core Responsibilities Include

Build Quality Strategy Execution

  • Operationalize the program test strategy within the New PBM Platform software factory and ensure engineering teams consistently meet the defined quality standards.
  • Define build-level test plans, coverage expectations, automation requirements, evidence packages, and quality checkpoints for platform and product releases.
  • Lead unit, contract, component, regression, evaluation, and other in-factory testing required before integration and end-to-end stages.
  • Ensure defects, risks, exceptions, and unresolved quality concerns are transparent and appropriately escalated.
  • Partner with the PBM Test Architect Principal to evolve standards based on delivery experience, defects, incidents, and emerging risks.

Automation & Quality Engineering

  • Drive automation across the development and release pipeline, prioritizing repeatability, coverage, speed, and reliable evidence.
  • Embed quality engineering into design, coding, pull-request, build, and deployment practices rather than relying on downstream detection.
  • Partner with DevSecOps and engineering teams to integrate automated quality controls into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Use AI to accelerate the quality lifecycle, including generation of unit, contract, and regression tests, synthetic test data, defect triage, root-cause analysis, and evidence assembly, judged on measured gains in cycle time and escape rate rather than tool adoption.
  • Set the review bar for AI-generated test assets, covering what must be human-reviewed before it is trusted, how coverage claims are verified, and how traceability back to requirements is preserved.
  • Advance service virtualization, testability, observability, synthetic data, and other techniques that reduce testing constraints.

Release Quality & Evidence

  • Own compilation and validation of build-quality evidence against agreed entry and exit criteria.
  • Provide clear quality assessments and recommendations for releases moving to integration and end-to-end testing.
  • Establish scorecards for coverage, defect trends, escape rates, automation, stability, and quality risk.
  • Lead root-cause analysis and systemic corrective action for recurring defects and quality failures.
  • Partner with engineering leaders to ensure technical debt and quality risks are understood, prioritized, and addressed.

Technical Leadership & Partnership

  • Serve as the senior quality-engineering advisor to platform and product engineering leaders.
  • Mentor quality engineers, developers, and technical contributors in modern testing and defect-prevention practices.
  • Coordinate with Test Data Engineering to ensure reliable, secure, representative, and reusable test data is available.
  • Partner with the PBS Test Lead so build evidence, known risks, and open defects transfer cleanly into integration, end-to-end, and client-wave testing across the existing estate.
  • Partner with the PBM Test Lead to keep coverage, automation, and evidence consistent across the platform and product build teams, and to resolve overlaps where the same capability is tested twice or falls between teams.
  • Operate within the test architecture and quality standards set by the PBM Test Architect Principal, raising exceptions through that route rather than diverging locally.
  • Lead matrixed or contracted quality resources and maintain consistent standards across delivery teams.

Critical Leadership Competencies

  • Drives Vision and Purpose: Connects the role’s work to the broader PBM transformation objectives and communicates a clear path forward.
  • Delivers Results: Creates accountability, removes barriers, and drives measurable outcomes under demanding timelines.
  • Manages Complexity: Synthesizes complex and sometimes conflicting information to establish practical solutions.
  • Decision Quality: Makes sound, timely decisions using technical, delivery, risk, and business considerations.
  • Collaborates: Builds effective partnerships across engineering, architecture, product, delivery, and business teams.
  • Communicates Effectively: Provides clear, concise, and audience-appropriate communications, recommendations, and escalations.
  • Manages Ambiguity: Establishes direction and momentum where requirements, solutions, or precedents are still emerging.
  • Instills Trust: Builds credibility through transparency, expertise, follow-through, and sound judgment.
  • Innovation: Identifies and applies better ways to improve quality, automation, evidence, and engineering productivity.
  • Technical Influence: Shapes engineering behavior and quality decisions through expertise, credibility, and practical partnership.

Critical Technology Competencies

  • Deep expertise in modern quality engineering, test automation, regression strategy, contract testing, and continuous testing.
  • Experience with cloud-native platforms, APIs, distributed systems, event-driven architectures, data services, and complex integration environments.
  • Hands-on knowledge of automated testing frameworks, CI/CD integration, environment and test-data dependencies, defect tooling, and quality analytics.
  • Experience applying performance, resilience, security, accessibility, and other non-functional testing practices in partnership with specialists.
  • Knowledge of AI-enabled testing approaches, including appropriate validation, privacy, security, and governance considerations.
  • Hands-on experience testing cloud-native workloads on AWS, including containerized and serverless services, managed data and messaging services, and the observability tooling used to diagnose build and pipeline failures such as CloudWatch and X-Ray.
  • Depth in automation tooling across the build layers, such as JUnit, TestNG, or pytest at unit and component level, Pact or WireMock for contract testing and service virtualization, and Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress where interface coverage is required.
  • Experience embedding quality and security gates into CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Harness, alongside scanning tools such as SonarQube, Snyk, or Checkmarx and defect and test management tooling such as Jira with Xray or Zephyr.
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted engineering tooling such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q Developer, or Cursor, and with AI-enabled quality capabilities including generated unit and contract tests, synthetic test data, self-healing automation, and defect triage assistance.
  • Products named above are illustrative of the depth expected in each category rather than individually required.
  • Ability to convert quality data and technical findings into concise recommendations for engineering and leadership audiences.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent related experience required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in quality assurance, software testing, test automation, quality engineering, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience leading quality practices across multiple engineering teams or a complex technology platform.
  • Proven expertise designing and scaling automated testing and integrating quality controls into software-delivery pipelines.
  • Experience working within an AI-assisted software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC), including the validation, security, and traceability controls required to rely on generated code and tests in a regulated environment.
  • Experience directing matrixed contributors, contractors, or technical workstreams and influencing engineering leaders without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, written communication, and presentation skills.
  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy benefit management, regulated technology, or high-volume transaction-processing environments preferred.

Success in this position requires fostering disciplined execution among your team members; supporting talent development; coordinating transparent reporting for senior management; and maintaining open lines of communication with stakeholders across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Lead the EMEA regional oversight model for compliance monitoring, testing, and issues management across multiple compliance disciplines including Financial Crimes Compliance, Core Compliance, and Markets Compliance.

  • Provide senior-level regional oversight by challenging execution risks, identifying control gaps, managing overdue deliverables, and addressing quality concerns in compliance activities.
  • Oversee the annual Compliance Test Plan for EMEA by managing scoping processes, ensuring execution quality, developing comprehensive reports, validating results, identifying issues, and escalating as necessary.
  • Ensure testing coverage accurately reflects regional regulatory obligations, business activities, risk assessments, and global priorities to maintain robust compliance.
  • Supervise regional execution of monitoring routines established by the global compliance monitoring programme to assess control effectiveness and emerging risks.
  • Review monitoring results, trends, exceptions, and thematic observations to identify root cause themes and control weaknesses within the compliance framework.
  • Provide regional oversight of issue identification including documentation, severity assessment, ownership assignment, action planning, validation processes, and closure protocols.
  • Challenge the adequacy of action plans by evaluating milestone discipline, evidence quality, closure readiness while overseeing reporting on issue status for senior management.
  • Coordinate with global function owners as well as regional compliance leadership and local teams to ensure consistency in execution while promoting transparency and accountability.

What you bring:

To excel as Director of Compliance Oversight – Testing, Monitoring and Issues Management at MUFG you will bring extensive experience from global organisations—ideally spanning over fifteen years—with significant exposure to managerial roles leading high-performing teams. Your expertise should encompass financial sector regulations including banking laws as well as supervisory guidance relevant to compliance or risk management disciplines. You will have demonstrated success implementing global operating models across diverse jurisdictions while maintaining sensitivity to local legal frameworks. Your interpersonal skills must enable you to build cooperative partnerships across regions—facilitating transparency between stakeholders at all levels. Experience with governance forums is essential along with proficiency in regulatory remediation programmes or transformation initiatives. Advanced communication capabilities are required for executive-level reporting alongside technical competence using GRC platforms or data analytics tools. Your proven ability to nurture talent within your team—combined with strategic thinking—will ensure disciplined execution of compliance functions under your leadership.


  • Extensive experience working within a global organisation plus managerial experience leading teams in complex environments.
  • Significant background in financial services with deep knowledge of banking laws; regulations; supervisory guidance; compliance; risk management or related control functions.
  • Proven track record overseeing risk-based compliance testing; monitoring routines; issue remediation; or control assurance activities within large financial institutions.

The organisation’s supportive leadership culture prioritises talent development through inclusive engagement practices that foster growth at every level. MUFG’s dedication to disciplined execution ensures that every team member has access to training opportunities designed for professional advancement while generous pension contributions support long-term security. The company’s flexible working arrangements further enhance work-life balance—making it possible for employees to thrive both personally and professionally. As part of MUFG’s EMEA operations you will enjoy being part of a network that values responsible stewardship over aggressive competition—where nurturing relationships is central to achieving organisational goals.

title: General Manager II - Store 4400 - Albemarle, NC
description:
Job Description

What is a General Manager?

A General Manager must be committed to inspiring our team, helping our Customers succeed and growing our business with integrity. Professional level sales and management position capable of supporting functions on both sides of the business. The role requires understanding of store systems, automotive systems, parts knowledge and has the ability to identify, troubleshoot and project assist for DIY. Responsible for developing and maintaining Professional Customer relationships and program growth. Is accountable for achieving financial metrics and maintaining service and appearance standards. Position is exempt and requires a minimum of 50-55 hours per week (excluding meal break periods). The average schedule is 5-6 days a week, 11 hour shifts, including rotating nights and weekends, with an hour for lunch. Additional hours may be required based on staffing, store conditions, sales to target, and other business demands. General Managers are required to work a schedule based on the needs of the business.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Achieve overall store sales goals and service objectives
  • Manage and grow Professional Customer relationships/sales, including building and holding team accountable to executing Customer action plans
  • Selection, hiring, development, performance mgmt., coaching, scheduling and engagement of store Team Members
  • Ensure execution of all inventory and operational standards
  • Coach all Team Members to deliver on Customer expectations (DIY and Professional)
  • Manager on duty responsibilities (touch base/coaching, floor/phone mgmt., task assignment and completion, safety, open/close duties)
  • Ability to lead change management
  • Embrace diversity and foster a respectful environment for both Customers and Team Members

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Provide DIY service including battery installation, testing, wiper install, etc.
  • Assist District/Region in other functions upon request

Success Factors

  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Ability to become ASE P2 certified or ASE ready equivalent
  • Ability to execute and train project and product quality recommendations
  • Advanced parts lookup and sourcing
  • Ability to source from numerous places including special order, FDO, second source, etc.
  • Ability to execute and train all store operational processes and procedures, and testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY services
  • Ability to execute and train inventory systems and store equipment
  • Ability to execute and train POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Ability to review and analyze P&L statement
  • Ability to recruit, select, hire and develop quality Team Members
  • Ability to build and grow relationships with Professional Customers

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a General Manager

  • Working knowledge of automotive systems preferred
  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with Customers, peers and upper management
  • Use Microsoft software effectively (Word, Excel required; PowerPoint preferred)
  • Calculate figures and amounts such as discounts, percentages, sales increases, and gross profit percent
  • Ability to review and analyze business reports, such as profit and loss statement (P&L)
  • Hold others accountable, inspect work quality and give feedback in a way that is inspiring
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings and weekends as needed
  • Prior Experience that Sets a General Manager up for Success
  • 2-3 years of experience managing a team of 10 - 20 Team Members in a fast-paced and highly dynamic retail environment
  • Successful experience managing profitability; proven financial and business acumen

Education

  • High school diploma or general education degree (GED), Bachelor’s degree in business or a related area preferred.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

  • Must have a valid driver's license
  • ASE certification preferred, but not required

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Position is eligible for sales commission based on individual or store performance.

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

title: Senior Snowflake & BI Developer – Treasury Finance
description:
Join Mizuho as Senior Snowflake & BI Developer – Treasury Finance!



The Senior Snowflake & BI Developer designs, develops, and supports enterprise data, analytics, and reporting solutions across Treasury and Finance, partnering with business, Data Architecture, and Engineering teams to translate requirements into scalable, production-quality solutions.

The role requires strong hands-on Snowflake, SQL, data engineering, data modeling, and Power BI expertise, with Treasury and Finance experience supporting areas such as Liquidity Management, Cash Positioning, Funding, Intraday Liquidity, Reconciliation, Bank Statements, and financial reporting, while ensuring appropriate data quality, lineage, performance, security, and governance.



PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a technical liaison with Treasury, Finance, Data Architecture, Engineering, Operations, Risk, and dependent technology teams.
  • Partner directly with Treasury and Finance users to understand reporting requirements, financial calculations, business rules, and data dependencies.
  • Communicate development progress, data-quality issues, risks, dependencies, and technical recommendations.
  • Work collaboratively with Solution Architects, Data Architects, Business Analysts, and application teams.
  • Support analysis and resolution of data and reporting discrepancies.



Snowflake Data Development

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain scalable Snowflake data solutions, including advanced SQL transformations, dimensional models, financial data marts, and reusable data components.
  • Build and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest, transform, aggregate, and publish Treasury and Finance data from multiple source systems.
  • Design and develop Power BI dashboards, semantic models, KPIs, calculations, and DAX measures supporting Treasury and Finance reporting and analytics.
  • Optimize Snowflake queries, data structures, and processing patterns for performance, scalability, and efficient resource utilization, while troubleshooting data issues across upstream and downstream layers.
  • Implement data-quality, reconciliation, and reporting controls to ensure Power BI outputs reconcile to approved source data and financial control totals.

Requirements & Data Solution Design

  • Partner with Treasury and Finance users to translate business requirements into data requirements, reporting specifications, transformation rules, and source-to-target mappings.
  • Collaborate with Data and Solution Architects to design target-state data models and flows, maintaining traceability from source systems through Snowflake to Power BI.
  • Maintain required data models, mappings, and technical documentation.
  • Data Quality, Governance & Controls
  • Implement data-quality, validation, and reconciliation controls across source systems, Snowflake, and reporting layers.
  • Maintain data lineage, governance, security, and access controls for Treasury and Finance data.
  • Support the full development lifecycle, including testing, UAT, code review, deployment, and production support.

________________________________________


MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS OR EXPERIENCE


Business & Domain Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in data engineering, BI development, data warehousing, analytics engineering, or financial-services technology.
  • Hands-on expertise in Snowflake, advanced SQL development, and Power BI, supported by strong knowledge of dimensional data modeling, enterprise data warehousing, data marts, data aggregation and transformation, data-quality controls, and end-to-end data lineage.
  • Experience working directly with Finance/Treasury stakeholders to understand financial data and reporting requirements.
  • Experience working within Agile delivery environments.



EDUCATION AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS

  • Batchlors in Engineering, Information Systems or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to translate business concepts into technical data solutions.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership of development deliverables.
  • Comfortable working across business, technology, risk, operations, and data organizations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • High attention to data accuracy, reconciliation, and financial controls.



The expected base salary ranges from $112k-$190k. Salary offers are based on a wide range of factors including relevant skills, training, experience, education, and, where applicable, certifications and licenses obtained. Market and organizational factors are also considered. In addition to salary and a generous employee benefits package, successful candidates are eligible to receive a discretionary bonus.


#LI-Hybrid

Other requirements

In office attendance is an essential function of this role. There is currently a requirement to be in the office a minimum 50% of the time, or five out of every 10 business days. Specific information about the requirements for your role will be communicated during the recruitment process.


Company Overview

Mizuho Financial Group, Inc. is the 15th largest bank in the world as measured by total assets of ~$2 trillion. Mizuho's 60,000 employees worldwide offer comprehensive financial services to clients in 35 countries and 800 offices throughout the Americas, EMEA and Asia. Mizuho Americas is a leading provider of corporate and investment banking services to clients in the US, Canada, and Latin America. Through its acquisition of Greenhill​, Mizuho provides M&A, restructuring and private capital advisory capabilities across Americas, Europe and Asia. Mizuho Americas employs approximately 3,500 professionals, and its capabilities span corporate and investment banking, capital markets, equity and fixed income sales & trading, derivatives, FX, custody and research. Visit www.mizuhoamericas.com.​​

Mizuho Americas offers a competitive total rewards package.

title: Associate Director, Research Development Services
description:
Job Title

Associate Director, Research Development Services

Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

Research Development Services

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.


Who We Are

Research Development Services (RDS) is a unit within Texas A&M University's Division of Research dedicated to advancing research capacity and competitiveness across the university. We partner with faculty, researchers, and stakeholders to support strategic research initiatives, secure external funding, and develop high-impact proposals. Through collaborative expertise, professional development, proposal support, and innovative research services, we help transform ideas into successful research programs that advance scholarship, innovation, and discovery.


What We Want

We are seeking an experienced and collaborative professional to serve as Associate Director of Research Development Services (RDS). In this leadership role, you will advance the university’s research mission by developing and delivering faculty training and proposal development programs, providing strategic guidance on research funding opportunities, leading outreach and engagement efforts across campus, and overseeing key RDS programs and staff. The successful candidate will partner with faculty, academic leaders, and research stakeholders to strengthen grant competitiveness, foster interdisciplinary collaborations, support professional development initiatives, and drive strategic research development efforts that enhance institutional research success.


What You Need to Know

Salary: Commensurate with experience.

A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Master's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Eight years of related experience in research development, professional development, grant writing, or research administration in a higher education.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certified Research Administrator (CRA) credential or active involvement in NORDP.
  • Direct experience establishing faculty development programsand team science facilitation initiatives.
  • Experience using research intelligence and analytics tools (e.g., Academic Analytics, Elsevier SciVal, Clarivate Web of Science).
  • Demonstrated track record of designing, delivering, and evaluating long-term faculty grant-writing cohort programs (e.g., NSF CAREER, NIH Early-Stage Investigator initiatives).
  • Active participation in national research development organizations (e.g., NORDP committee leadership, conference presentations, or formal mentoring programs).

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.

Essential Duties/Tasks

Training and Development

  • Organizes and hosts professional and proposal development training programs for faculty and other users.
  • Provides guidance and support to researchers in proposal development.
  • Develops and coordinates documentation provided to customers.
  • Participates in training and professional development focusing on leadership.

Leadership and Strategic Development

  • Serves as part of departmental leadership team and assists in developing departmental strategies for research development.
  • Develops strategic plans and sets goals for assigned programs in collaboration with administration.
  • Establishes performance goals and measures to evaluate the success of areas of responsibility.
  • Assists in formulating and implementing policies and procedures.
  • Provides leadership for the department in specific areas of expertise.
  • Monitors national trends and seeks new information for faculty professional development.
  • Participates in planning, directing, and coordinating operational matters related to programs.

Program Management and Support

  • Develops, implements, and oversees programming for various services.
  • Manages and directs HelpDesk and user support with a mission to provide robust support services.
  • Collects data and analyzes for reporting and tracking progress.
  • Maintains program activity records and provides progress reports to leadership.
  • Oversees and manages personnel issues of employees supervised.
  • Develops program budgets based on needs and availability of funding.
  • Supervises and directs staff and activities of project teams.

Campus Outreach and Engagement

  • Develops and executes a proactive, campus-wide outreach strategy, including departmental presentations, digital toolkits, and targeted communications, to maximize awareness of Research Development Services (RDS) across all academic disciplines.
  • Cultivates strong partnerships with Deans, department chairs, and faculty leaders to ensure equitable access to proposal development resources.
  • Facilitates interdisciplinary networking and ideation sessions to connect faculty across disparate departments for large-scale, multi-investigator funding opportunities.
  • Integrates RDS resources into new faculty onboarding programs and establishes continuous feedback mechanisms to adapt service offerings to evolving campus research needs.

Compliance and Standards

  • Ensures compliance with unit, department, and government standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Enforces ethical, regulatory, and performance standards.

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

  • Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts, and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums
  • 12-15 days of annual paid holidays
  • Up to eight hours of paid sick leave and at least eight hours of paid vacation each month
  • Automatic enrollment in the Teacher Retirement System of Texas
  • Health and Wellness: Free exercise programs and release time
  • Professional Development: All employees have access to free LinkedIn Learning training, webinars, and limited financial support to attend conferences, workshops, and more
  • Educational release time and tuition assistance for completing a degree while a Texas A&M employee
  • Living Well, a program at Texas A&M that has been built by employees, for employees

The Mechanical Plant Design team (TPM) is part of engineering at HVDC, with the mechanical responsibilities for our HVDC Projects on a global scale. We are currently around 160 employees operating from 5 countries.


We engineer the mechanical systems of HVDC converter stations, defining how high-voltage equipment is integrated into the overall plant design. The Senior Scientific Engagement & Program Manager, part of the International Medical Affairs, Center of Excellence (IMACE) Scientific Operations team. Responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing high quality medical and scientific engagement activities across assigned programs, brands, and therapeutic areas (Oncology, Cardiovascular Disease, Renal, Neuroscience, and Immunology).

Working closely with International Medical Affairs (IMA) (TAs, IMACE) and cross functional partners, the role translates engagement strategy into clear operational plans and ensures seamless delivery of advisory boards, congress activities, standalone meetings, and medical education programs. This position plays a key role in enhancing ways of working, improving processes and tools, and fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement in how scientific engagements are executed.

The position is reporting to the Scientific Engagement Lead.


Job Description

Key Responsibilities:


Scientific Engagement Planning & Execution

  • Coordinate and execute medical and scientific engagement activities including advisory boards, congress activities (e.g., symposia), external expert engagements (EEEs), standalone meetings, and medical education programs, ensuring high‑quality delivery aligned with engagement objectives.
  • Translate engagement strategies into detailed operational plans, timelines, and deliverables across assigned programs, projects, brands, and therapeutic areas.
  • Lead day‑to‑day project planning by managing milestones, logistics, materials, and overall readiness for scientific events.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with IMA (TAs, IMACE) and cross‑functional stakeholders to clarify objectives, align expectations, and drive coordinated execution.
  • Maintain strong communication channels with internal teams and external partners to share updates, flag risks, resolve issues, and ensure smooth handoffs.

Operational Excellence & Standardization

  • Apply and reinforce standardized ways of working - including processes, templates, tools, documentation practices, and governance frameworks - across scientific engagements.
  • Ensure compliant, audit‑ready execution of activities by following SOPs, guidance documents, and established approval pathways.

Vendor & Logistics Coordination

  • Manage relationships with external vendors, agencies, and logistics partners, overseeing deliverables, timelines, budgets, and the overall quality of execution.

Risk, Issue & Quality Management

  • Identify risks, issues, or delays affecting timelines or quality, escalating or resolving them in collaboration with project teams to maintain momentum and compliance.

Tracking, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Track program progress, outputs, and performance metrics, supporting reporting needs and contributing to continuous improvement of tools, templates, processes, and operational efficiency.

Essential Requirements:

  • Education: BSc or equivalent. MSc, PhD, PharmD, or MD are desirable.
  • Significant experience in scientific engagement delivery and program/project management in pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences. Including min 5 years of coordinating medical or scientific engagement activities, such as advisory boards, medical congresses (including symposia), standalone medical meetings, external expert engagements (EEEs) or medical education programs.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent projects, with strong organizational skills and the ability to deliver against timelines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Background in operational planning and execution, including managing logistics, vendors, materials, and event related deliverables.
  • Experience working in a matrixed, cross functional setting, collaborating with teams such as IMA, Scientific Operations, Medical Affairs, or similar scientific/medical functions.
  • Familiarity with compliance, SOPs, and approval processes within medical or scientific environments, ensuring activities are delivered to quality and audit ready standards.
  • Experience maintaining documentation, tracking progress, and supporting project reporting, ideally using standard project management tools or systems. Exposure to process improvement activities, including contributing ideas to streamline workflows, enhance documentation, or improve engagement execution.
  • Fluent oral and written English; additional languages desirable.

Desirable Requirements:

  • Experience working in one or more of the following therapeutic areas Oncology, Cardiovascular, Renal, Neuroscience, or Immunology is an advantage.

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

What We Want

We're looking for a detail-oriented and hands-on professional who is passionate about preserving library collections and mentoring student workers. In this role, you’ll be responsible for training and supervising student employees, as well as coordinating the organization and upkeep of all Preservation Lab spaces. You will assess library general collection items and recommend appropriate preservation services and treatments for damaged or fragile materials. You will maintain the equipment within the listed lab areas, ensuring their proper function, accessibility, and safe use. The ideal candidate is organized, dependable, and comfortable balancing routine tasks with specialized preservation work. If you enjoy behind-the-scenes work that directly supports the long-term stewardship of collections, we'd love to hear from you.

What You Need to Know

Salary: $17.25/hourly.

Cover Letter/Resume: A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended and will help in our review. You can also attach a portfolio of previous projects to demonstrate your hand skills and attention to detail. You may upload them on the application under the CV/Resume section.

Other Requirements and Factors:

  • Must be able to work Monday through Friday, daytime hours (8am to 5pm).

Essential Duties/Tasks

  • Student Employee Supervision and Training - Hires, trains, coaches, supervises, and evaluates student employees in the lab who are engaged in repairing books, creating enclosures, and transferring materials. Directs related workflows, provides immediate feedback and guidance, and approves work schedules and timesheets. Serves as the unit liaison to AskUs personnel for damaged materials, documenting. Patron Damage to report to the Business Office.
  • Preservation Lab Coordination - Coordinates the organization and upkeep of all Preservation Lab spaces, outside of the Conservation Lab, including the book repair/enclosures work area, flex space, intake and storage areas, as well as the anteroom and adjacent portions of the office suite. Maintains all equipment within the listed lab areas, ensuring their proper function, accessibility, and safe use. Ensures accessibility of all necessary materials and supplies for lab workers. Assists the Preservation Librarian with facilitating the use of the flex space and adjacent areas by personnel external to the Preservation Unit for instructional purposes or donor-related events.
  • Preservation Repair and Enclosures - Assesses the condition of library general collection items and recommends appropriate preservation services and treatments for damaged or fragile materials. Uses Preservation and Conservation knowledge to perform repairs and treatments on said materials, such as tear repair, hinge tightening, new cases, spine repairs/Rebacks, tip-ins, pockets, velo binding, surface cleaning, pamphlet stitching, sewing signatures, as well as others determined by the Preservation Librarian. Constructs boxes, four-flaps, mylar and colibri covers, and other protective enclosures for library collections items. Documents statistics of all work performed within the lab and reports it monthly to the Preservation Librarian.
  • Order Materials, Supplies, and Services - Submits purchase orders to maintain plentiful stock of regular Preservation Unit materials and supplies. Coordinates with Heads of each Preservation Section, as well as the Preservation Director, to research, select, and order specialized unit materials, supplies, and some outside services. Maintains forms for supply requests from members of the Preservation Unit and spreadsheets for tracking the Unit’s expenditures throughout the Fiscal Year. Provides regular supply, shipping, and budget status updates to the Preservation Librarian, Preservation Director, and the Preservation Unit as a whole.
  • Team Participation - Collaborates with Preservation employees to provide the best service possible to donors and library users through participatory decision-making and implementation of operations and guidelines. Participates and attends special events, library and unit meetings, and training as needed.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Three years of related library experience. Three years experience in a public, academic, or a specialized library, museum, or archive.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • One year as TAMU experience as a Library Specialist I.
  • Experience in an academic or archival library setting.
  • Knowledge of basic book binding, repairs, and preservation treatments.
  • Knowledge of archival enclosures and materials.
  • Knowledge of basic collections handling practices.
  • Ability to operate laboratory equipment such as, Gunnar mat cutter, board shear, guillotine
  • Supervisory experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Ability to multi-task and work cooperatively with others.
  • General knowledge of library services and functions.
  • Knowledge of email, word processing, spreadsheet applications and library online research database searches and/or processing.
  • Excellent problem solving and critical thinking skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Good manual dexterity and attention to detail.
  • Reliable attendance.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to move medium weight (~50lb) boxes, books, heavy book carts, lab equipment, or similar items
  • Ability to handle material which can contain dust or microscopic mold spores.
  • Ability to climb step ladders up to 10 feet high while holding library materials

Who We Are

The Libraries are the indispensable hub of discovery, learning and creativity with the teaching and research that goes on in the colleges and academic departments. We offer rich and extraordinary collections at the University Libraries. The Libraries resources and services enable and support the University missions of teaching, research, and service. We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration. Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

title: Overnight Residential Counselor
description:
San Diego Youth ServicesJOB ANNOUNCEMENTOvernight Residential Counselor

San Diego Youth Services seeks an Overnight Residential Counselor in the Youth Emergency Shelter program to be based in San Diego. This is a full-time & non-exempt position reporting to the Program Manager.


San Diego Youth Services: Who we are


San Diego Youth Services has helped improve the lives of more than 834,000 homeless, runaway and vulnerable youth since its beginning in 1970. We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing to more than 16,000 youth every year at 100+ community and school locations. Through prevention, early intervention and treatment, we also help youth before they need higher levels of care or become homeless.


We aim to:

  1. Meet the basic needs of youth. Hunger, poverty and youth homelessness are on the rise for many youth and their families today. We help meet these basic needs for youth. What could be more vital than food and shelter? We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing.
  2. Create positive connection. We help youth focus on positive life changes and healthy relationships as part of providing needed resources and services. San Diego Youth Services has long provided foster homes and adoption support services for families considering adopting a youth in the foster care system.
  3. Help youth develop life skills. In addition to a range of safe and stable housing options, we offer support to help youth develop the independent living skills necessary to become self-sufficient and keep off the streets.
  4. Promote overall health and well-being. Early intervention and care for the whole child are critical. We provide a broad continuum of services to help youth overcome trauma and challenges that put them at risk, including case management, counseling, mental health treatment and educational support and resources.

SDYS has a staff of approximately 250 employees and 80 volunteers working across San Diego County and an annual budget of approximately $24 million.


You can learn more about us at www.sdyouthservices.org.


CONTEXT OF THE POSITION:


Supervise residential service partners in milieu. Provide crisis intervention, group facilitation and intake counseling and mediation. Maintain relief coverage.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. Maintain shelter schedule, rules, and consequences.
  2. Maintain program structure through supervision of residents.
  3. Ensure completion of chores by residents.
  4. Conduct intakes, assist in development of life plans.
  5. Teach and model skills through individuals and groups including youth leadership. Assist in teaching life skills, healthy coping skills, and standards of quality.
  6. Maintain data collection and contact compliance of records as required. Communicate necessary information and events through utilization of communication logs or direct contact.
  7. Maintain shelter cleanliness and safety.
  8. Attend any mandatory trainings/meetings
  9. Maintain a working knowledge of MIS equipment.
  10. Welcome and support volunteers in the organization and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  11. Maintain positive relationship with community and donors.
  12. Have Weekday Availability for Overnight shifts.
  13. Other Duties as required.

SDYS EXPECTATIONS:

  • Adhere to and uphold the rigorous standards of SDYS as mandated by its mission, purpose, guiding principles and standards of quality.
  • Maintain confidentiality and privacy standards of service partner protected health information and other applicable information and material in accordance to agency and center policies, and applicable regulations and laws including HIPAA.
  • Welcome and support SDYS volunteers and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  • Effectively communicate with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Receive and give supportive feedback to foster equity and inclusion in working relationships.
  • Recognize, nurture, and learn from strengths in co-workers.
  • Maintain warm, welcoming and safe work environments.
  • Possess flexibility to accomplish job responsibilities in several work environments, whether it be from home, on the road, or in an office.

PREFERRED EDUCATION, YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS:

Able to work with homeless runaway youth in a shelter setting. Be available to cover shift in case of illness or vacations on short notice. Be available to stay overtime to complete crises intervention or necessary crises documentation. Experience working in a residential setting preferred with youth development experience. Bilingual Spanish-English speaking helpful. Able to work in a very diverse setting with people of all backgrounds, culture and orientation. Must be available to work a minimum of one shift per quarter in evenings, overnight, weekends and holidays. Must be able to obtain/maintain CPR and First Aid Certification. Hire subject to background check, TB test, and drug test.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:


Able to lift and carry 25 lbs. Able to be cleared to drive own vehicle & agency vehicle (if applicable) and have valid driver’s license.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.


Hourly Pay Range: $19-$21

FULL-TIME STAFF BENEFITS:

  • PTO: 18 days PTO + 2 floating holidays + 12.5 paid holidays (32.5 paid days off)
  • 1.5x overtime pay
  • 403b with 2% employer match
  • Medical, dental, vision, pet insurance
  • Mileage reimbursement
  • $2,000 bonus for staff who are fully bilingual in Spanish
  • $1,500 bonus for staff with proficiency in Spanish

To apply, please send resume and cover letter through job posting on SDYS website.


SDYS offers a comprehensive benefits package to full time employees that includes generous PTO, personal holidays, health, vision, dental, life insurance, parental leave and a 403(b)-retirement plan with matching contribution. SDYS is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) employer.


All are welcome at San Diego Youth Services.


As an organization working to meet the basic needs of youth, create positive connections, help youth develop life skills, and promote overall health and well-being, SDYS believes its practices and actions must reflect the highest level of commitment to access, equity, and social justice.


The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, innovation, self-expression, and talent that our members invest in their work represents not only part of the SDYS’ culture, but the SDYS’ reputation and achievements as well. SDYS remains open to feedback from all communities it touches and knows that input from those with direct experience of issues will make the SDYS more effective in achieving its goals.


SDYS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. In compliance with the Immigration and Nationality Act as amended, all new employees must verify their eligibility to work in the United States.


SDYS is proud to be a kindness certified company.

Under the direction of Project Management, performs work involving the day-to-day operation and maintenance of the wastewater facility including all related infrastructure, equipment, buildings and grounds.

  • Conducts Wastewater sampling and laboratory monitoring per Project and Regulatory requirements.

  • Performs cleanup/housekeeping activities at all facilities, buildings and grounds.

  • Ability to operate complex controls, processes, and equipment.

  • Knowledge of wastewater treatment systems, processes and equipment.

  • Must be able to work as a team in a teamwork-oriented environment.
  • Must be safety conscious and at times be able to work independently with little/no supervision.
  • Must be able to work closely with local contractors.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

  • Valid MN Grade IIA or higher Wastewater Treatment Operator License.
  • Valid MN Driver’s license and the ability to meet risk management guidelines.

Physical Requirements:

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear.

description:

Every day, our unwavering commitment to quality ensures the delivery of safe and effective products to patients. Our flexible, innovative, and customer-oriented culture is rooted in science and risk-based compliance. Whether you are engaged in development, maintenance, compliance, or research analysis, your contributions have a direct impact on patient care. By being part of our team, you help uphold a quality culture that adapts and evolves to meet the needs of patients, ensuring that every product we deliver is of the highest standard.



What You Will Achieve

In this role, you will:

  • Assist in the preparation and maintenance of media stocks, including sterilization of accessories by autoclave cycles.
  • Manage receipt, storage, and handling of Bio ball cultures, and assist in the maintenance of Master cultures and preparation of Cryo vials.
  • Perform various microbiological tests such as water analysis, Microbial Limit Test, Sterility tests, Bacterial Endotoxin Test, CCIT, and micro challenge studies.
  • Ensure training records are updated and correctly filed to reflect current testing capabilities.
  • Perform sampling and labeling of materials as per defined procedures and verify all equipment and instruments.
  • Interpret and evaluate data for accuracy, precision, trends, and potential cGMP impact, recommending appropriate corrective actions.
  • Ensure all documentation and quality records comply with Good Manufacturing Practices and Good Laboratory Practices and are filed according to existing policies.
  • Review and revise Standard Operating Procedures, analytical methods, and related documents to keep them current.
  • Conduct analyses on finished products, raw materials, and components, including data entry, review, and approval in a computerized database, and generate EMS reports.
  • Contribute to the completion of complex projects, manage time effectively to meet targets, and develop plans for work activities within a team, while exercising judgment with reliance on supervisor and working under their direction.



Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements)

  • Bachelor's degree with any years of experience, or an Associate's degree with 4 years of relevant experience, or a high school diploma (or equivalent) and 6 years of relevant experience
  • Demonstrated technical skills in method validation and testing
  • Ability to read and understand applicable compendial methods, Standard Operating Procedures, technical procedures, and governmental regulations
  • Knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices and its application standards, processes, and policies.
  • Excellent organizational skills and strong ability to multi-task
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency with unique Quality Control instruments to meet accuracy specifications for sample management, retains management, interpretation, and evaluation



Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements)

  • Experience with laboratory work, particularly using analytical HPLC (High Pressure Liquid Chromatography) techniques
  • Proven track record in leading continuous improvement projects
  • Strong knowledge of lean manufacturing principles, six sigma methodologies, and statistical analysis
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with colleagues at all levels
  • Adaptability and willingness to learn new techniques and procedures
  • Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use



PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Lifting up to 50-100 pounds daily. 5 to 8 hours walking, lifting, moving materials in the warehouse. Position is first shift Monday through Friday. Some off hour (night/weekend/holiday) support may be required to support staff and operations.



NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS

Position is first shift Monday through Friday. Some off hour (night/weekend/holiday) support may be required to support staff and operations.

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. Function / Position Summary

The Multi Abilities Classroom (MAC) paraeducator supports the classroom by assisting in the implementation of structured instructional, behavioral, social and communication supports aligned to the MAC curriculum and practices. Provide direct support to students with significant academic learning, communication and behavioral needs, including assistance with personal care, feeding and toileting as required. Perform duties under the direct supervision of a certified staff member, contribute to a consistent, hands on and supportive learning environment while maintaining confidentiality of student, staff and department information.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

  • Implement individual or small group instructional activities under the direction of the MAC teacher, using established routines, visual supports and structured practices.
  • Familiarize yourself with student IEP goals, objectives, accommodations and behavior supports to assist with consistent implementation across the school day.
  • Support the use of communication systems, visual schedules, reinforcement systems and other structured supports that align with MAC expectations and individual student needs.
  • Follow through on defined behavioral intervention plans and procedures, including implementation of proactive strategies, reinforcement systems and de-escalation supports as directed by the teacher.
  • Assist with data collection, including academic, behavioral, social and communication data, and document information as requested by the teacher.
  • Support a structured classroom environment by preparing, organizing and maintaining materials and assisting with environmental setup as directed by the teacher.

  • Escort students within the building, including transitions to specials/electives, therapies and other instructional spaces.
  • Assist with the loading and unloading of student buses during assigned work hours.
  • Work cooperatively with the teacher by assisting with any activity aligned to student IEP needs, including instructional tasks, communication supports, social skills and behavior routines.
  • Provide personal care support to students, including lifting, transferring, positioning, feeding, toileting and hygiene needs, consistent with special skills expectations.
  • Support students in building independence, communication, self-regulation and engagement throughout the school day.
  • Provide input to the teacher regarding student responses, communication attempts, behavior patterns and other needs.
  • Attend staff meetings and professional development activities as assigned
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, staff and department information within the school and community.

Education

  • Para Educator, Substitute, Professional Educator or Provisional Educator License required.

Experience / Knowledge

  • 3 years of Para Educator experience or classroom assistant for students with disabilities preferred
  • Experience with students who have behavioral needs preferred
  • Experience as a Behavior technician or Registered Behavior Technician strongly preferred
  • Ability to collaborate with staff and students in a way that is collaborative, student friendly and productive
  • Familiarity with data collection preferred

Physical Demands

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work through many interruptions throughout the school day
  • Required prolonged standing, bending, start/stop and sitting
  • Lifting may be required to manually move, carry, pull or push heavy objects or materials
  • Assisting with toileting needs may be required as needed
  • Ability to perform CPI approved restraint once trained

Terms of Employment
