Job Description Summary

#LI-Hybrid

Location: Westworks, London, UK
We are unable offer relocation for this position. Please only apply of this location is accessible for you.

This is a hybrid position with an expectation of 12 days a month onsite working from our Westworks, White City offices.

Home worker contracts can be discussed and offered depending on eligibility criteria being met. This can be discussed at interview stage if applicable.

When we put our heads together, we can do brilliant work. And when we do brilliant work, we can achieve remarkable things for patients as we positively transform healthcare. Our Trial Vendor Senior Managers have direct impact on the success of our clinical trials and the management of our critical vendors.


Job Description

As a core member of the Clinical Trial Team (CTT), the Trial Vendor Manager (TVM) serves as the CTT vendor sub-team lead, providing direct operational management and oversight of clinical trial vendors to deliver study outcomes in accordance with schedule, budget, quality, compliance, and performance standards. The TVM is accountable for vendor service delivery at the study level and collaborates closely with the Vendor Start-up Manager (VSM) across major clinical vendor categories, including central labs, eCOA/ePRO, IRT, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, patient recruitment and retention (PR&R), and imaging. During study start-up, the TVM applies technical and operational expertise to translate protocol requirements into clear vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs), helping to ensure timely study initiation.


You will proactively manage vendor-related risks and potential issues and implement global vendor strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the single point of contact for vendor service delivery at the study level, partnering with vendors and cross-functional teams within the Clinical Trial Team (CTT)
  • Provide direct, end-to-end operational oversight of clinical trial vendor deliverables, ensuring alignment with study timelines, scope, quality, and compliance expectations across major vendor categories, including central labs, IRT, eCOA/ePRO, imaging, cardiac and respiratory diagnostics, and PR&R.
  • Review vendor-related protocol sections during protocol development and partner with the Vendor Start-up Manager to translate protocol requirements into accurate vendor specifications and Statements of Work (SOWs).
  • Oversee vendor financials, including forecasting, budget tracking, validation of work performed, service confirmations, invoice reconciliation, and purchase order management and close-out.
  • In collaboration with vendors, study start up leads and vendor start up managers, ensure that all key vendor deliverables and documentation are in place to support submission during study start-up
  • Lead UAT activities for vendor systems (e.g., eCOA, IRT), and contribute to vendor system validation
  • Drive site activation from a vendor perspective, compile vendor related central documents, and address risks/issues during site activation and throughout the life-cycle of a site
  • Manage vendor performance against agreed KPIs, proactively identify risks and issues, drive corrective actions and mitigation plans with vendors and study teams, and maintain complete, inspection-ready oversight documentation.

Essential Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences or equivalent; advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years’ clinical operations experience, including direct operational management and oversight of clinical trial vendors across one or more major service categories such as central labs, IRT, eCOA/ePRO, or imaging.
  • Strong knowledge of GxP and ICH regulations, clinical trial design, and supplier service specifications.
  • Proficiency in vendor management, contracting, and site-related collaborations, including UAT for eCOA and IRT systems.
  • Results-driven with proven ability to complete projects within timelines.

description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

MUFG, one of the world’s most respected financial groups, is seeking a Director Technology Analytics and Innovation Lead to join their London office. This pivotal role offers you the opportunity to shape the future of compliance technology and analytics across EMEA, leading a multidisciplinary team in a globally renowned organisation with over 350 years of history. MUFG is committed to nurturing talent, fostering shared growth, and building long-term relationships with clients and employees alike. As Director TAI Lead, you will be at the forefront of integrating advanced technology, data sourcing, analytics, tuning, and AI enablement to support core compliance and financial crime systems. You will benefit from a supportive leadership environment that values integrity, transparency, and responsibility, while enjoying flexible working opportunities and access to generous pension contributions. If you are passionate about driving positive change in financial crime compliance through technology and innovation, this is your chance to make a meaningful impact within an inclusive and collaborative global network.

What you'll do:

As Director Technology Analytics and Innovation Lead at MUFG in London you will play a central role in advancing the organisation’s compliance technology landscape. You will drive strategic direction for AML and sanctions platforms by overseeing project delivery from inception through post-implementation validation. Your day-to-day responsibilities include managing cross-functional teams across Compliance Operations Technology Data Model Risk functions as well as external partners. You will facilitate forums that review system changes ensuring robust governance practices are followed while representing MUFG during regulatory reviews audits model validations. Your expertise in detection capabilities will be crucial as you optimise transaction monitoring sanctions screening customer risk rating KYC surveillance systems within your regional scope. By leading data sourcing analytics AI enablement initiatives you will ensure that all solutions meet rigorous standards for accuracy reliability regulatory compliance. Success in this role requires strong interpersonal skills collaborative mindset ability to build consensus among stakeholders disciplined approach to governance meticulous attention to documentation executive reporting.

  • Own the regional roadmap and execution for all technology-related work supporting Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Sanctions, Core Compliance, and Data Platforms such as AIRIS.

  • Lead requirements gathering, design processes, testing phases, implementation strategies, release readiness assessments, production support activities, and post-implementation validation for applications and enhancements.
  • Manage scope, budget, schedule, risks, dependencies, and benefits of technology initiatives while reporting/escalating issues to regional and global heads as needed.

  • Oversee effectiveness of Transaction Monitoring systems, Sanctions Screening tools, Customer Risk Rating models, Know Your Customer (KYC) processes; manage regulatory-ready systems through coverage assessments and optimisation activities.
  • Direct material detection configuration decisions including logic design choices; document rationale for governance reviews; ensure proper controls are implemented for watchlist management.
  • Lead data sourcing efforts for systems/models/analytics/AI use cases; assess impact of data defects or feed failures on detection logic/model performance/alert generation/regulatory reporting.

What you bring:

Your proven track record in financial crime compliance technology delivery makes you an ideal candidate for the Director Technology Analytics and Innovation Lead position at MUFG. You bring deep expertise in managing multidisciplinary teams responsible for large-scale transformation programs spanning multiple regions legal entities lines business. Your hands-on experience with detection capabilities transaction monitoring sanctions screening customer risk rating KYC surveillance ensures you can oversee critical systems optimising their effectiveness regulatory readiness. You have demonstrated ability influence senior IT leaders align priorities drive outcomes even when incentives timelines differ leveraging structured governance escalation executive sponsorship. Your skill translating analytical needs into actionable requirements mapping data sources designing transformation rules ensures robust solutions meet operational regulatory demands. You excel communicating complex concepts clearly tailoring messages diverse audiences from regulators executives technical specialists operational staff. Your strategic vision leadership style motivates high-performing teams fosters collaborative inclusive environment supports talent development execution excellence.


  • Extensive experience across financial crime compliance technology data analytics model ownership or major technology delivery within regulated environments.
  • Experience in leading managers technical professionals business unit system owners quantitative analysts data analysts or multidisciplinary teams focused on technology analytics transformation.
  • Proven ability to lead large-scale programs with approved budgets exceeding US$5 million including accountability for scope budget schedule risk business outcomes using both waterfall agile methods.
  • Experience chairing system/model change governance forums with authority to challenge proposals require evidence escalate unresolved risks drive decisions closure across multiple legal entities branches countries lines business.
  • Direct experience owning materially leading detection capabilities in at least two financial crime domains such as Transaction Monitoring Sanctions Screening Customer Risk Rating KYC Surveillance.
  • Hands-on experience sourcing data translating analytical needs into field-level requirements source-to-target mappings transformation rules test conditions acceptance criteria conducting completeness reconciliation profiling gap analysis assessing effect defects models systems alerts reporting.
  • Demonstrated success influencing senior IT leaders system-division partners where priorities incentives delivery timelines not aligned using governance escalation executive sponsorship achieve program outcomes without direct reporting authority.
  • Experience acting trusted advisor execution partner business/system owner translating control responsibilities into technology analytical requirements driving implementation accountable delivery teams developing resource capacity plans addressing priorities skills role mix location strategy employees contractors.
  • Ability communicate complex technical analytical model data control matters clear business language tailoring messages regulators executive committees senior technology leaders operational teams delivery resources demonstrating executive judgment under pressure distinguishing facts assumptions elevating material risks early setting clear asks driving decisions closure stakeholders competing objectives delivery constraints.
  • Bachelor’s degree equivalent relevant professional experience advanced degree industry certification preferred excellent managerial leadership experience strategic approach articulate implement vision strategy department lead motivate high performing team provide clear direction.

What sets MUFG apart:

MUFG stands out as one of the world’s largest most trusted financial groups with a rich heritage spanning over three centuries global presence more than 2 300 offices 150 000 employees worldwide. The organisation is deeply committed to integrity responsibility transparency fairness creating an environment where every employee can thrive contribute meaningfully. At MUFG you will find supportive leadership dedicated nurturing talent providing flexible working opportunities generous pension contributions ongoing training development resources empowering you grow professionally personally. Working at MUFG means joining community values inclusivity dependability empathy teamwork offering unparalleled platform advance your career make lasting impact financial services industry.

title: Case Manager
description:
San Diego Youth ServicesJOB ANNOUNCEMENTCase Manager

San Diego Youth Services seeks a Case Manager in the Victim and Survivor Services program with lived experience to be based in San Diego. This is a full-time & non-exempt position reporting to the Program Manager.


San Diego Youth Services: Who we are


San Diego Youth Services has helped improve the lives of more than 834,000 homeless, runaway and vulnerable youth since its beginning in 1970. We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing to more than 16,000 youth every year at 100+ community and school locations. Through prevention, early intervention and treatment, we also help youth before they need higher levels of care or become homeless.


We aim to:

  1. Meet the basic needs of youth. Hunger, poverty and youth homelessness are on the rise for many youth and their families today. We help meet these basic needs for youth. What could be more vital than food and shelter? We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing.
  2. Create positive connection. We help youth focus on positive life changes and healthy relationships as part of providing needed resources and services. San Diego Youth Services has long provided foster homes and adoption support services for families considering adopting a youth in the foster care system.
  3. Help youth develop life skills. In addition to a range of safe and stable housing options, we offer support to help youth develop the independent living skills necessary to become self-sufficient and keep off the streets.
  4. Promote overall health and well-being. Early intervention and care for the whole child are critical. We provide a broad continuum of services to help youth overcome trauma and challenges that put them at risk, including case management, counseling, mental health treatment and educational support and resources.
  5. SDYS has a staff of approximately 250 employees and 80 volunteers working across San Diego County and an annual budget of approximately $24 million.

You can learn more about us at www.sdyouthservices.org


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Provide support services that include accompanying youth to meetings/appointments/court; case management services around stabilization (i.e., housing, employment, education, health, etc.); outreach activities, crisis intervention, and referrals as applicable. Provide transportation when needed.
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation, data collection and contract compliance of records including file reviews.
  • Conduct emergency and/or immediate outreach in collaboration with Child and Family Wellbeing to prospective service partners in a variety of community settings (Polinsky, Group Homes, Juvenile Hall, In-home, Community Partners, etc.); screen prospective service partners for eligibility to enter program. Triage with CSEC Response Team Coordinator for needed services.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of group curriculum and facilitate groups.
  • Ensure coordination of care by communicating with Probation Officer, CWS Social Workers, Health Care Providers, Therapist, Natural Support Systems, Parents/Families, etc. to gain knowledge of service-partners and how to best ensure their success.
  • Ability to be on-call. A typical on-call rotation is 1 week every 5-6 weeks and is subject to change.
  • Provide intensive 24hr follow-up on all referrals.
  • Engage youth in services for up to 90 days or longer, depending on client need and linkage to long-term resources, of intensive short-term case management.
  • Provide outreach and training to increase community awareness.
  • Knowledgeable or willing to be trained in tenant-landlord laws, Fair Housing Laws, and the Transitional Housing Misconduct Act.
  • Seek out new partnerships with low-income housing providers.
  • Provide transportation when needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

SDYS EXPECTATIONS:

  • Adhere to and uphold the rigorous standards of SDYS as mandated by its mission, purpose, guiding principles and standards of quality.
  • Maintain confidentiality and privacy standards of service partner protected health information and other applicable information and material in accordance with agency and center policies, and applicable regulations and laws including HIPAA.
  • Welcome and support SDYS volunteers and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  • Effectively communicate with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Recognize, nurture, and learn from strengths in co-workers.
  • Maintain warm, welcoming and safe work environments.
  • Possess flexibility to accomplish job responsibilities in several work environments, whether it be from home, on the road, or in an office.

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in social work or related field preferred. 2-5 years’ experience working with high-risk clients preferably adolescents and Transitional Aged Youth who have experienced commercial sexual exploitation or human trafficking will be considered in leu of education.
  • Lived experience of commercial sexual exploitation or human trafficking required (personal experience or personal impacts due to experience of family, a close friend, etc.).
  • Bi-lingual in Spanish preferred.
  • Experience in crisis intervention, group facilitation, documentation, and case management preferred.
  • Must possess excellent oral and written skills.
  • Work well autonomously and with multi-disciplinary team.
  • Willingness to develop or possess working knowledge of trauma-informed care.
  • Must have or be willing to be trained 40-hour Domestic Violence counselor training, Campbell Danger Assessment, Mental Health First Aid, Seeking Safety, and Motivational Interviewing (MI) trainings.
  • Must be computer literate in Microsoft Outlooks, Word and Excel.
  • Valid CA driver’s license, good driving record and willingness to use own properly insured vehicle on the job (mileage reimbursed).
  • Maintain certification in CPR and First Aid.
  • Employment is subject to required clearances which include tuberculosis test, fingerprinting, background checks (FBI, DOJ, CACI), and drug testing.
  • Available to work on-call hours Monday through Sunday 24/7.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: This position does not have supervisory responsibilities.


Hourly Pay Range: $22-$24

FULL-TIME STAFF BENEFITS:

  • PTO: 18 days PTO + 2 floating holidays + 12.5 paid holidays (32.5 paid days off)
  • 403b with 2% employer match
  • Medical, dental, vision, pet insurance
  • Mileage reimbursement
  • $2,000 annual bonus for staff who are fully bilingual in Spanish
  • $1,500 annual bonus for staff with proficiency in Spanish

To apply, please send resume and cover letter through job posting on SDYS website.


SDYS offers a comprehensive benefits package to full time employees that includes generous PTO, personal holidays, health, vision, dental, life insurance, parental leave and a 403(b)-retirement plan with matching contribution. SDYS is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) employer.


All are welcome at San Diego Youth Services.


As an organization working to meet the basic needs of youth, create positive connections, help youth develop life skills, and promote overall health and well-being, SDYS believes its practices and actions must reflect the highest level of commitment to access, equity, and social justice.


The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, innovation, self-expression, and talent that our members invest in their work represents not only part of the SDYS’ culture, but the SDYS’ reputation and achievements as well. SDYS remains open to feedback from all communities it touches and knows that input from those with direct experience of issues will make the SDYS more effective in achieving its goals.


SDYS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. In compliance with the Immigration and Nationality Act as amended, all new employees must verify their eligibility to work in the United States.


SDYS is proud to be a kindness certified company.

title: Manager, Brand Strategy
description:
As part of the dynamic, results-oriented Corporate Marketing organization, the Manager, Brand Strategy plays a critical role within WD’s Brand Strategy & Experience team. This role is responsible for defining WD’s brand strategy and narrative, ensuring clarity, consistency, and scalability across enterprise and consumer portfolios.

The primary objective of this role is to develop and operationalize WD’s brand positioning, messaging architecture, and narrative frameworks, enabling consistent brand expression across a decentralized global organization. This individual serves as a strategic and hands-on leader who connects business priorities to compelling brand platforms and scalable execution systems.

WD is the storage foundation of the AI-driven data economy, powering innovation across enterprise infrastructure and consumer technology. As WD expands its visibility across enterprise and consumer markets, strong brand leadership is essential to unify storytelling, elevate category leadership, and ensure consistent execution across regions, products, and channels.

Working closely with Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Creative, Communications, Channel, Regional Marketing, and agency partners, this role ensures WD’s brand shows up with clarity, credibility, and cohesion across all strategic initiatives.

What You’ll Achieve

  • A clearly defined enterprise and consumer brand strategy and narrative that strengthens WD’s leadership across key markets
  • Standardized messaging frameworks that enable consistent storytelling across campaigns, launches, and executive communications
  • Scalable brand systems that empower decentralized teams while maintaining consistency
  • Integrated workflows connecting internal creative teams and external agency partners
  • Strong brand adoption across product, regional, partner, and customer-facing initiatives
  • Increased brand clarity and differentiation across enterprise and consumer portfolios

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Brand Strategy & Positioning

  • Lead development of WD’s global brand positioning across enterprise and consumer portfolios
  • Translate business strategy into clear brand platforms that guide campaigns, launches, and storytelling
  • Define category positioning that strengthens WD’s leadership across AI infrastructure, data innovation, and consumer technology
  • Partner with executive leadership to align brand strategy with business priorities
  • Drive quarterly brand platform development cycles aligned to key market moments

Narrative & Messaging Architecture

  • Define WD’s enterprise and consumer brand narratives, ensuring clarity and differentiation
  • Develop messaging architectures that connect corporate positioning to product storytelling
  • Translate complex technical capabilities into clear, compelling messaging
  • Support executive communications and thought leadership narratives
  • Ensure consistent language across product, campaign, and corporate messaging

Scalable Brand Systems

  • Build scalable brand playbooks, templates, and messaging frameworks
  • Create standardized tools that enable decentralized teams to execute consistently
  • Identify inconsistencies and outliers across brand expression and provide solutions
  • Develop systems that support both governance and usability across global teams
  • Establish repeatable processes that improve speed and consistency of brand execution

Agency & Creative Integration

  • Brief and manage brand and creative agencies supporting strategic initiatives
  • Partner with internal design teams to ensure brand consistency across deliverables
  • Connect internal and external creative workflows into a unified operating model
  • Guide development of brand-level creative programs and storytelling assets
  • Ensure agency and in-house teams align to shared strategy and execution standards

Collaborative Brand Governance

  • Provide brand guidance through partnership, not enforcement
  • Enable teams across product, regional, and channel marketing to align through clarity and tools
  • Support co-branding, partner branding, and MDF-driven initiatives
  • Establish scalable governance models that maintain flexibility across regions
  • Drive adoption of brand tools and frameworks across the organization

Campaign Platform Development

  • Develop strategic brand platforms that support recurring campaign cycles
  • Guide top-line brand storytelling initiatives across enterprise and consumer audiences
  • Support launch readiness across key product and corporate initiatives
  • Align messaging across campaign, product, and corporate channels
  • Ensure brand platforms remain adaptable across evolving market needs

Required:

  • 8–12+ years of experience in brand strategy, brand management, or strategic marketing
  • Proven experience developing brand positioning and messaging frameworks at scale
  • Strong background managing creative agencies and integrated marketing programs
  • Experience operating within decentralized or global marketing organizations
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex technology into compelling messaging
  • Experience building scalable brand systems, playbooks, or governance frameworks
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across marketing, communications, and product teams
  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or related field

Preferred Experience:

  • Experience in enterprise technology, infrastructure, storage, or AI-related industries
  • Experience supporting both B2B and consumer portfolios
  • Familiarity with brand architecture development and messaging systems
  • Experience managing integrated internal and external creative teams
  • Experience leading brand transformation or repositioning initiatives
  • Experience working across both enterprise technology and consumer-facing brands preferred
  • MBA preferred

title: Senior Scientist, Translational Preclinical Models, MPS Automated Cell Culture & Innovation
description:
Band

Level 3


Job Description Summary

Join the Discovery Sciences team at Novartis BioMedical Research to advance the next generation of translational preclinical models for drug discovery. In this highly collaborative, hands-on role, you will integrate stem cell biology, microphysiological systems (MPS), automated tissue culture, advanced imaging, and innovative technologies to build scalable, human-relevant models that can transform how biological insights are generated and translated.

You will work across disciplines to translate complex biological protocols into reproducible, automation-ready processes, generate high-quality cellular models at scale, and enable project teams with reliable data and fit-for-purpose model systems. This opportunity is well suited to a collaborative scientist who enjoys troubleshooting, managing multiple workflows, and improving laboratory systems through innovation.


Job Description


Internal Job Title: Senior Scientist I/II

Position Location: Cambridge, MA, onsite


Location statement: This role is based in Cambridge, MA. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role; please only apply if this location is accessible for you.


Job Description:


The Discovery Sciences department at Novartis BioMedical Research is seeking a Senior Scientist I/II to support manual and large-scale automated tissue culture and advanced human model systems. The successful candidate will operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and develop scalable workflows across automated tissue culture platforms while partnering with scientists to deliver consistent, well-characterized cell models. The role requires practical expertise spanning cell biology, laboratory automation and scheduling software, microscopy, image analysis, and experimental data interpretation.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Maintain, expand, cryopreserve, and characterize human pluripotent stem cell lines, including iPSC and hESC cultures.
  • Execute multiple stem cell differentiation protocols in parallel while maintaining experimental schedules, traceable documentation, and quality standards.
  • Perform large-scale iPSC culture in a controlled laboratory environment using automated liquid-handling platforms and high-throughput robotic systems.
  • Program, operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot automated tissue culture platforms, including flask-based CellTrio systems and plate-based HighRes Biosolutions systems.
  • Develop and apply microscopy and image-analysis workflows to monitor cell health and enable data-driven, real-time decisions on automated platforms.
  • Establish, maintain, and operate microphysiological systems, organ-on-chip models, and advanced 3D tissue culture platforms, including routine monitoring, functional assessment, and data documentation.
  • Design, execute, and optimize MPS-based studies with cross-functional scientists to improve experimental quality, reproducibility, and translational relevance.
  • Perform imaging, functional characterization, and data analysis to evaluate model performance and support drug discovery and translational research programs.
  • Create and improve SOPs, maintenance manuals, and start-up procedures; train users; prepare required media and reagents; and coordinate cell-production needs with project teams.

Essential Requirements:


  • B.S. or M.S. in Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Bioengineering, or a related discipline, with 4+ years of relevant post-graduate experience. We will also consider recent PhD graduates, within the last 2 years, with relevant experience.
  • Hands-on experience maintaining mammalian cell cultures, including human cancer cell lines and/or iPSCs, with strong aseptic technique and cell-quality practices.
  • Experience executing cell culture or differentiation workflows with attention to reproducibility, scheduling, documentation, and experimental quality.
  • Experience designing, building, deploying, operating, or troubleshooting automated laboratory workflows in life science or clinical laboratory settings.
  • Working knowledge of microscopy, image-based monitoring, and quantitative data analysis for cellular models.
  • Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, troubleshoot effectively, and collaborate across project teams and stakeholders.

Desirable Requirements:


  • Familiarity with HighRes BioSolutions/Cellario robotic platforms, CellTrio RoboCell, Sartorius CompacT, liquid handlers, bulk dispensers, and associated laboratory automation software.
  • Experience with phenotypic screening, advanced microscopy, image-analysis tools, and data platforms such as Genedata Screener or Spotfire; exposure to AI-enabled analysis tools is a plus.

Compensation and Benefits:


The salary for this position is expected to range between $93,800 and $174,200 per year for Senior Scientist I, and $98,700 and $183,300 for Senior Scientist II. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors.


Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.


US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

title: Mechatronics Engineer
description:
Introduction to the job

ASML is seeking a Mechatronics / Robotics Design Engineer to join the Wilton, CT development location as we break new ground in the emerging field of photolithography. As a Mechatronics Engineer, you will specify, design, develop, realize, integrate, and test modules and tools in a multi-disciplined team, collaborating closely with cross-functional partners and suppliers. You will deliver within system specifications, cost targets, and project schedules, ensuring timely realization of solutions that contribute to competitive, achievable, and serviceable products. The mechatronics engineer provides discipline specific expertise throughout the entire product life cycle. This Includes concept feasibility, new product introduction, existing product sustainment and customer facing problem resolution. The position requires highly motivated, extremely organized, and self-driven individuals.

The mechatronics engineer will work on mechatronics, precision handling of delicate parts, product and system integration and software functionality, all specific to ASML products. The main focus will be mechatronics and control systems on advanced modules in lithography tools. Candidate should have direct experience in the design and test of mechatronic systems and control systems, preferably in the area industrial robotics integration.

This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). As a condition of employment, qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.

Scope:

Perform defined mechatronics engineering work with increasing independence and guidance from senior engineers. Contribute to component and sub-module design, analysis, integration, testing, and troubleshooting while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and suppliers.

  • Design and develop custom mechatronics systems with a cross sector team, including translating stages, rotary motion, multi-link positioners, sensors, servos, actuators, etc.
  • Design path optimization algorithms and associated controls for end product.
  • Analyze and improve dynamic disturbance response of robotic systems
  • Responsible for “sustaining engineering” tasks, resolving equipment design issues in a timely fashion as they arise at customer sites.
  • Participate in concept designs and experiments for future equipment and subsystems.
  • Design quality products using six sigma and lean process techniques for robust designs.
  • Work with external suppliers to define and develop certain aspects of new product design while collaborating with internal cross discipline teams.
  • Perform Root Cause Analysis: Troubleshooting from System to Component Level
  • Technical Writing: Define and Document Specifications, Design Decisions and
  • and Operations to be used in a clean manufacturing environment.
  • Develop and Implement the Product Validation and Verification (V&V) Strategy
  • Integrate control systems for industrial robotics into capital equipment, including all aspects such as dynamics, end-effector design, controls, etc.
  • Troubleshoot designs to determine potential risks, failure modes, and corrective actions.
  • Run complex mechatronic systems for test and qualification of design changes.
  • Design, Develop and Build Product Specific Test Tooling
  • Test Validation and Verification (V&V) of Product Requirements
  • Define and document technical specifications, design decisions, procedures, and operational instructions for use in a clean manufacturing environment.

Role and responsibilities

In this role, you will execute engineering tasks, contribute to mechatronic design solutions, perform analysis and testing, support system integration, troubleshoot technical issues, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality engineering solutions.

  • Identify, analyze, document, and manage requirements with traceability, and coordinate verification criteria to confirm deliverables meet intent.
  • Conduct research and feasibility studies, document findings, and translate results into recommendations, tradeoffs, and decision inputs.
  • Develop engineering concepts and solutions, make technical choices, and resolve issues to meet functionality, performance, cost, and compliance needs.
  • Define and communicate specifications and high-level designs, align interfaces, and support reviews and approvals to enable quality execution.
  • Support system or product integration by coordinating dependencies, applying configuration management, and enabling smooth project execution.
  • Define and execute validation and test approaches, improve methods and procedures, and ensure qualification evidence supports release readiness.
  • Estimate effort, plan and track work, manage risks and dependencies, and deliver assigned work packages or projects to agreed quality and timelines.
  • Maintain accurate technical documentation, share knowledge through coaching and mentoring as applicable, and follow EHS policies while identifying and mitigating safety risks.

Education and experience

Bachelor's degree (BS/BE) in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field required. Internship, academic, or professional experience with mechatronics, robotics, controls, or related systems preferred.


Skills

Technical & Functional Skills

  • Requirements management, technical specifications, and interface definition.
  • Engineering design, problem solving, and technical trade-off analysis.
  • System integration, verification & validation (V&V), and product qualification.
  • Mechatronics, robotics, motion control, and dynamic systems.
  • PID control, calibration, and flexible dynamics.
  • Design of complex electromechanical mechanisms.
  • MATLAB/Simulink modeling and simulation.
  • Classical and digital control theory, stability analysis, and real-time controls.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, and communication skills.
  • Experience in semiconductor, lithography, optics, or other multidisciplinary high-tech environments is a plus.

Behavioral & Leadership Skills

  • Drives Results: Takes ownership and delivers high-quality outcomes.
  • Self-Awareness: Seeks feedback and continuously improves.
  • Values Differences: Fosters inclusion and leverages diverse perspectives.
  • Builds Effective Teams: Collaborates effectively and builds trust.
  • Drives Vision & Purpose: Aligns work with team goals and priorities.

Other information

  • Job posting end date: 3/30/2027
  • This position is located on-site. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. A flexible workplace arrangement is available for remote work up to two days a week.
  • Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.
  • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds.
  • May require travel (domestic and/or international) dependent on business needs.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Additional Responsibilities: There is potential for exposure to strong magnetic fields, high voltage and currents.

What you will be doing

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Program Coordination & Alignment

  • Serve as the enterprise point of contact for Community Benefit programming, maintaining a current roster of HSS community programs, program leads, and partner organizations across all departments and regions.
  • Engage departments to identify HSS-funded community programs not yet captured in Community Benefit reporting, learning what each program does, who it serves, and how it is funded.

Regional & Department Partnerships

  • Partner with program leads and Regional Ambassadors across the enterprise, including regional sites, to identify gaps, reduce duplication, and align offerings with CSP priorities and Community Benefit requirements.
  • Develop and sustain relationships with community-based organizations and expand partnerships that reach populations with the greatest health need.

Mission Impact Committee & Governance Support

  • Coordinate logistics for Mission Impact Committee meetings, including scheduling, communications, materials preparation, minutes, and tracking of follow-up actions.
  • Lead development and production of the annual Community Benefit report, coordinating content and timelines.
  • Support development of committee presentations, briefing materials, and Community Benefit updates for the Committee, executive sponsors, and institutional leadership.
  • Coordinate leadership convenings and cross-departmental working sessions that advance the Committee’s multi-year roadmap and priorities.

Project Management & Collaboration

  • Manage the annual Community Benefit project calendar, including CHNA, CSP, and Schedule H milestones, ensuring departments and program leads meet submission deadlines.
  • Serve as the operational liaison to the Senior Coordinator, Outcomes, Data Analytics & Scholarly Activity, connecting program leads for accountability.
  • Coordinate with HSS Finance, Marketing, and other internal partners to keep Community Benefit timelines, communications, and deliverables on track.

title: Rare Disease – Rare Cardiac, Senior Health & Science Specialist - Kansas
description:
Pfizer US/PR Commercial Sales

Founded in 1849, Pfizer Inc. began as a small chemistry enterprise built on the belief that scientific ingenuity can improve—and protect—human life. Today, as one of the world’s leading biopharmaceutical companies, Pfizer’s purpose is Breakthroughs that change patients’ lives: discovering, developing, and delivering medicines and vaccines that address unmet need, earn trust through quality and integrity, and reach patients through strong partnerships across the healthcare system. In a complex and rapidly evolving pharmaceutical landscape, our work is measured by one outcome - helping patients live longer, healthier lives.


Rare Disease Sales Organization Mission & Impact

Pfizer’s Rare Disease – Rare Cardiac Sales organization exists to help improve the lives of people living with serious rare cardiac conditions by connecting scientific innovation to the clinicians and systems that deliver care. We lead with integrity and patient need—advancing disease and product education grounded in robust clinical evidence, promoting Pfizer Rare Cardiac therapies compliantly, and supporting healthcare professionals’ understanding of appropriate patient identification and use based on approved indications.


Through evidence‑based scientific exchange, we help reduce access, diagnostic, and workflow barriers so more patients can start and stay on the right therapy. Our impact is more informed clinical decision‑making, improved consistency of care, and better outcomes for patients, contributing to a higher standard of care across the rare cardiac community.


Role Summary

The Rare Disease – Rare Cardiac, Senior Health & Science Specialist is a field-based specialty sales role responsible for driving the growth of Rare Cardiac products through compliant, strategic relationships within assigned accounts. This role partners with Therapeutic Area Specialists and Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to execute effective promotional strategies, support appropriate access, and deliver high-impact customer engagement. The Rare Disease – Rare Cardiac Health & Science Specialist leverages strong sales acumen, product and disease-state expertise, and a structured approach to in-person engagement while collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve business objectives.


Role Responsibilities

  • Drive customer engagement and sales performance through effective in-person interactions across rare cardiac accounts.
  • Build strong, compliant relationships with cardiology HCPs, multidisciplinary care teams, and office staff across assigned accounts.
  • Deliver approved promotional and disease-state messaging to support appropriate Rare Cardiac product use.
  • Leverage product, disease, and market knowledge to identify opportunities, prioritize accounts, and support patient finding and referral pathways.
  • Support patient access by providing information on prior authorization requirements, reimbursement support, hubs, and co-pay resources as applicable.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners to address customer needs, remove access barriers, and advance Rare Cardiac business objectives.
  • Use digital tools and insights to plan, execute, and optimize Rare Cardiac territory activities.

Basic Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree

  • OR an associate’s degree with 8+ years of work experience
  • OR a high school diploma (or equivalent) with 10+ years of work experience.

Work Experience: Minimum of 3 years in one or more of the following:

  • Pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical device sales
  • Pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical device marketing
  • Aligned therapeutic specific healthcare provider experience

Driver’s Licensing Requirement: Valid US driver’s license and driving record in compliance with company standards.

description:

Job Description Summary

#LI-Hybrid
Location: Mengeš, Slovenija

Iščemo izkušenega strokovnjaka, ki želi prevzeti pomembno vlogo pri zagotavljanju zanesljivih in skladnih proizvodnih procesov na področju downstream procesov (DSP) in čiščenja. Kot Tehnolog proizvodnih procesov specialist (m/ž/d) boste vodili in spremljali proizvodne procese, skrbeli za pripravo in strokovni pregled dokumentacije po izvedenih procesih ter koordinirali reševanje zahtevnejših odstopov. Samostojno boste vodili projekte, povezovali različne strokovne oddelke ter usklajevali skupno delo pri kompleksnih procesnih in proizvodnih izzivih. Pomemben del vaše vloge bo tudi strokovno zagovarjanje področja med inšpekcijami, kjer boste prevzemali vodilno vlogo. Iščemo komunikativno in sodelovalno osebo, ki zna povezati strokovno znanje, različne deležnike in zahteve reguliranega proizvodnega okolja ter jih učinkovito usmerjati k skupnemu cilju.


Job Description

Vaše ključne odgovornosti:

  • Vodenje in spremljanje proizvodnih procesov na področju downstream procesov (DSP) in čiščenja skladno z zahtevami GMP.
  • Priprava, pregled in pravočasno zagotavljanje proizvodne dokumentacije ter dokumentacije po izvedenih proizvodnih procesih.
  • Koordiniranje in vodenje preiskav zahtevnejših odstopov, določanje ključnih vzrokov ter zagotavljanje ustreznih korektivnih in preventivnih ukrepov.
  • Samostojno vodenje kompleksnejših projektov ter usklajevanje aktivnosti za njihovo kakovostno in pravočasno izvedbo.
  • Prevzemanje vodilne strokovne vloge pri inšpekcijskih pregledih in presojah ter zagovarjanje področja odgovornosti.
  • Koordiniranje medfunkcijskega sodelovanja pri reševanju kompleksnih procesnih, proizvodnih in kakovostnih izzivov.
  • Zagotavljanje strokovne podpore proizvodnji ter vodenje izboljšav, sprememb in aktivnosti za zagotavljanje robustnih proizvodnih procesov.

Vaš doprinos k delovnem mestu:

  • Univerzitetna izobrazba s področja inženirstva, farmacevtske tehnologije, kemije, farmacije ali druge ustrezne znanstvene smeri.
  • Najmanj 5 let izkušenj s podporo procesom v proizvodnji in/ali kakovosti.
  • Poznavanje farmacevtskih proizvodnih procesov, dobre proizvodne prakse (GMP) in regulatornih zahtev.
  • Samoiniciativnost in sposobnost samostojnega prevzemanja odgovornosti za zahtevnejše naloge in aktivnosti.
  • Odlične komunikacijske in koordinacijske sposobnosti ter sposobnost povezovanja in usklajevanja različnih ekip.
  • Aktivno znanje angleškega in slovenskega jezika.

Zaželene izkušnje:

  • Izkušnje na področju downstream procesov (DSP).
  • Poznavanje principov izolacije in čiščenja proteinov.

Z izbranim kandidatom bomo sklenili delovno razmerje za nedoločen čas s poskusno dobo 6 mesecev. Prijavo oddajte z življenjepisom v slovenskem in angleškem jeziku.

Nagrajevanje:

V Novartisu smo zavezani k soustvarjanju prihodnosti medicine ter priznavanju in nagrajevanju ljudi, ki to omogočajo.


Pričakovani letni osnovni razpon plače za delovno mesto:

32.060,00 - 59.540,00 EUR


Osnovna plača se določa na podlagi vnaprej opredeljenih in transparentnih kriterijev, kot so relevantne veščine, kompetence in izkušnje, ne glede na spol, ter v skladu z Novartisovo politiko določanja plač. Po zaposlitvi v Novartisu se plača periodično pregleda v skladu z internimi akti in postopki.


Plačna enakost je temeljno načelo naše kadrovske politike in odraža našo zavezo k ustvarjanju raznolikega, pravičnega in vključujočega okolja, ki vse zaposlene obravnava dostojanstveno in spoštljivo, kot je opredeljeno v našem Kodeksu etike.


Poleg osnovne letne bruto plače so zaposleni upravičeni tudi do spodaj navedenih ugodnosti:

  • Letni bonus, ki pripada vsakemu zaposlenemu: 12% letne plače.
  • Regres za dopust: Leta 2025 je znašal 2.496 € (neto). Za leto 2026 znaša 2.678,28 € (neto).
  • Nagrada za poslovno uspešnost: Leta 2025 je znašala 2.538,64 € (bruto), skupaj z zimskim regresom.
  • Prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje: Novartis v Sloveniji zagotavlja prostovoljno dodatno pokojninsko zavarovanje (5,844 % bruto izplačila, letno omejeno na 3.224,18 €).
  • Zavarovanje: Dodatno nezgodno zavarovanje: V času zaposlitve pri Novartisu je zaposleni 24/7 zavarovan za primer smrti ali invalidnosti, ki bi bila posledica nezgode. Zavarovanje – Specialisti: Kolektivno zdravstveno zavarovanje, ki omogoča hitrejši dostop do specialističnih zdravstvenih storitev pri Zavarovalnici Triglav d.d. za vas in vaše družinske člane.
  • Care Connect: Program, ki ponuja zaupno, osebno podporo za vaše duševno zdravje in dobro počutje s pomočjo terapij, svetovanj, orodij in še mnogo več.
  • Ostale ugodnosti v skladu z zakonom in kolektivno pogodbo: Prevoz, prehrana ter ostali dodatki.

Preberite brošuro in izvedite več o našem sistemu nagrajevanja:


Opomba: Ugodnosti se lahko razlikujejo glede na državo ter so skladni z lokalno zakonodajo, vključno z določili kolektivnih pogodb. Celovit pregled vašega paketa prejemkov, vključno z morebitnimi relevantnimi določbami kolektivne pogodbe, ki veljajo za vašo delovno mesto glede na lokacijo zaposlitve in delodajalca Novartis, vam bo posredovan v okviru nadaljnjih korakov zaposlitvenega postopka.


Predani smo raznolikosti in vključenosti: Novartis si prizadeva ustvariti izjemno, vključujoče delovno okolje in oblikovanje raznolikih timov, saj ti predstavljajo naše bolnike in skupnosti, ki jih oskrbujemo.


Zakaj Novartis: Pomagati bolnikom in njihovim družinam zahteva več kot le inovativno znanost. Potrebna je skupnost zavzetih ljudi, kot ste vi. V Novartisu cenimo sodelovanje, podporo in navdihovanje drug drugega za razvoj prebojnih terapij, ki spreminjajo življenja pacientov. Ste pripravljeni ustvariti svetlejšo prihodnost skupaj z nami?

At Babcock we’re working to create a safe and secure world, together, and if you join us, you can play your part as a Caisson Operativeat our Devonport Royal Dockyard site.

The role

As a Caisson Operative, you’ll be part of a specialist team responsible for the operation and maintenance of critical dockyard infrastructure that enables vessels to safely enter, leave and operate within the dockyard. This is a unique opportunity to develop highly specialised operational skills while working within the defence, engineering and maritime sectors.

Day-to-day, you’ll directly support naval operations, dockyard activities and national defence capabilities. No two days are the same, and you'll gain exposure to a wide range of technical activities, equipment and environments while building a rewarding long-term career with excellent training and development opportunities.

  • Operating pump houses, penstocks, caissons and control systems to support docking and undocking activities.
  • Monitoring dock and basin water levels, dock conditions and safety systems to ensure safe operations.
  • Leading and supporting ship, caisson and gate movements across the dockyard infrastructure.
  • Assisting with structural surveys, dock preparations, maintenance activities and refurbishment work on dockyard assets.
  • Working safely in confined spaces, at height, around water and in operational dockyard environments.

This role is full time, 35 hours per week and is based on site at Devonport Royal Dockyard.

Essential experience of the Caisson Operative

  • Working within operational, industrial, maritime, engineering or maintenance environments.
  • Using hand tools, battery-powered tools or mechanical equipment safely and effectively.
  • Following safe systems of work and health and safety procedures.
  • Working collaboratively within a team environment whilst also taking responsibility for tasks when required.
  • Operating in physically active roles, including outdoor working and challenging environments.

Qualifications for the Caisson Operative

Essential

  • A willingness and ability to successfully complete all required role-specific training.

Desirable

  • Slinging or lifting operations experience.
  • Forklift Truck Operator certification.
  • Powerboat qualifications.

Security Clearance

The successful candidate must be a sole UK National who is able to achieve and maintain Security Check (SC) security clearance for this role.

Many of the positions within our company are subject to national security clearance and Trade Control restrictions. This means that your eligibility for certain roles may be affected by your place of birth, nationality, current or former citizenship, and any residency you hold or have held. Further details are available at United Kingdom Security Vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk).

title: Memory Signal Integrity Engineer
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

As a Signal Integrity Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in delivering high-speed signal integrity solutions for complex platforms, boards, and packages. You will perform simulations, define signal integrity rules, and guide physical implementations to optimize design margins and ensure the integrity of next-generation interfaces. Your work on electrical specifications and interconnect designs will directly support Intel's cutting-edge products, ensuring they meet rigorous standards for performance and quality.

You will be joining the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), which drives innovation by developing foundational technologies for Intel's products. This team focuses on designing and optimizing advanced silicon and platform solutions to deliver high-performance, scalable, and reliable technology. As part of this group, you will contribute to shaping the future of Intel's hardware and platform offerings.

The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:

  • Develop and deliver signal integrity solutions for high-speed interconnects in complex platforms, boards, and packages.
  • Perform 2D and 3D modeling and simulations to evaluate electrical structures for die-to-die interconnects.
  • Define signal integrity rules, guide their implementation, and optimize design margins to enhance product performance.
  • Design, simulate, and characterize test structures to correlate simulations with real-world measurements using high-speed equipment.
  • Collaborate with IP design and silicon integration teams to align designs with platform-level requirements, minimizing signal degradation and costs.
  • Generate electrical specifications and industry-standard interconnect guidelines to support next-generation interface development.
  • Document characterization reports and implementation guidelines for platform design improvements.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 0-1 years of hands-on experience in signal integrity, high-speed interconnect design, or related domains with demonstrated skills gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training OR a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with no prior professional experience.
  • Knowledge of signal integrity design and trade-offs, including attenuation, crosstalk, jitter, and power noise.
  • Experience with simulation tools and high-speed equipment for signal integrity analysis.
  • Proficiency in developing and analyzing 2D and 3D models for electrical structures.
  • Familiarity with debugging interconnect challenges and improving design optimization.
  • Intermediate to Advanced English proficiency (both verbal and written).
  • Must have unrestricted - permanent right to work in Costa Rica.

Preferred Qualifications:

Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems and present solutions.
  • Experience working on high-speed platforms, boards, or package designs.
  • Familiarity with industry standards and consortium activities for next-generation interface specifications.

Join Intel and be part of a team that is shaping the future of technology. Your expertise will drive innovation in signal integrity, empowering Intel's products to achieve excellence in performance and reliability.

You will evaluate how innovative technologies fit into the company’s architecture, how they can be integrated and scaled, and what their adoption would mean in a complex enterprise environment. You will work with internal stakeholders to ensure an appropriate fit and reuse of current assets, and with external vendors to understand their solutions in the context of architectural assessment. Your work will be proactive and reactive, depending on the innovation services provided. This role requires an understanding of emerging technologies and technology trends and the ability to stay up to date, particularly in artificial intelligence and other emerging technology areas. You will combine this knowledge with an understanding of business challenges and the outcomes that new technologies might bring.


You will translate innovation ideas into concrete architectural assessments, solution design sketches, and integration options. Your work will provide technically grounded inputs for clear, actionable recommendations, ensuring that proposed solution paths are realistic and aligned with Hitachi Energy’s target architecture.


This role connects emerging technologies and innovative solutions with other architecture and technology departments within Hitachi Energy. Alongside this work, you will collaborate with architecture, technology validation, and prototyping specialists and document architectural insights from completed assessments, contributing to reusable patterns and shared knowledge repositories.


The focus is on internal enterprise innovation, not customer-facing products.


How you’ll make an impact

  • Assess the architectural fit, integration feasibility, and enterprise design implications of emerging technologies and market solutions for innovation topics accepted for assessment. Translate your findings into concise architecture compatibility assessments that support clear technology recommendations.
  • Develop high-level solution design sketches and integration approach options, ensuring proposed solution paths are realistic and enterprise-grade. Provide these as architectural inputs to innovation recommendation packages.
  • Coordinate with Hitachi Energy architects to ensure assessments and proposed solution approaches align with Hitachi Energy’s target architecture standards and approved reference patterns.
  • Investigate the platform and application landscape to avoid duplication and ensure an appropriate fit with existing and onboarded solutions including build-vs-buy-vs-reuse considerations and high-level cost implications.
  • Outline architecture options where a proof of concept or further investigation is recommended. Define the architectural guardrails and constraints for proposed proofs of concept.
  • Identify potential security, data, or compliance considerations early and involve the relevant expert teams where needed.
  • Engage with external vendors and startups to understand their solutions and evaluate them against architectural, integration, and scalability criteria.
  • Participate in preparing recommendation packages, contributing architecture-specific findings, risks, and constraints relevant to next-step decisions.
  • Document architectural insights and solution design lessons from completed innovation assessments. Contribute to architecture knowledge repositories and reusable pattern libraries where applicable.

Your background

  • At least five years of professional experience in solution architecture, enterprise architecture, AI/ML platform design, or cloud architecture in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Demonstrated experience assessing emerging technologies from an architectural perspective, with the ability to develop high-level solution design sketches and integration approach options.
  • Experience working with ambiguous, early-stage innovation topics and translating them into concrete architectural inputs and recommendations.
  • Experience collaborating across innovation, architecture, and delivery stakeholder communities, supported by strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML architecture patterns, large language model integration, cloud-native design, and enterprise integration standards. Understanding of target architecture concepts and architectural guardrails.
  • Strong strategic conceptual thinking skills and Strong ability to prepare architectural outputs that are clear and understandable to other teams.
  • A degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, or a related field is preferred. Fluent English

title: Program Manager
description:
San Diego Youth ServicesJOB ANNOUNCEMENTProgram Manger

San Diego Youth Services seeks a Program Manager in the Resource Family Agency program to be based in San Diego. This is a full-time & exempt position reporting to the Director of Services.


San Diego Youth Services: Who we are


San Diego Youth Services has helped improve the lives of more than 834,000 homeless, runaway and vulnerable youth since its beginning in 1970. We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing to more than 16,000 youth every year at 100+ community and school locations. Through prevention, early intervention and treatment, we also help youth before they need higher levels of care or become homeless.


We aim to:

  1. Meet the basic needs of youth. Hunger, poverty and youth homelessness are on the rise for many youth and their families today. We help meet these basic needs for youth. What could be more vital than food and shelter? We provide safe places to live and long-term solutions through shelter, foster homes, community centers and housing.
  2. Create positive connection. We help youth focus on positive life changes and healthy relationships as part of providing needed resources and services. San Diego Youth Services has long provided foster homes and adoption support services for families considering adopting a youth in the foster care system.
  3. Help youth develop life skills. In addition to a range of safe and stable housing options, we offer support to help youth develop the independent living skills necessary to become self-sufficient and keep off the streets.
  4. Promote overall health and well-being. Early intervention and care for the whole child are critical. We provide a broad continuum of services to help youth overcome trauma and challenges that put them at risk, including case management, counseling, mental health treatment and educational support and resources.

SDYS has a staff of approximately 250 employees and 80 volunteers working across San Diego County and an annual budget of approximately $24 million.


You can learn more about us at .


CONTEXT OF THE POSITION:


Accountable to the Director of Services and responsible for managing the Resource Family Agency (RFA), including oversight of the RFA license, daily operations, contracted services, and quality of trauma-informed services. Responsible for monitoring resource-parent certifications and foster-youth placements; supervising staff; managing program outcomes, budget, data, billing, and contract compliance; and maintaining strong relationships with Child Welfare Services, Community Care Licensing, referral sources, and community partners. Ensures programming complies with Child and Family Well-being/IEU, Community Care Licensing, contractual, fiscal, and agency requirements.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Maintain accurate placement and resource-parent rosters, program records, and required documentation; complete other related duties as assigned or required.
  • Support continuous quality improvement through program and case-file reviews, corrective actions, and readiness for licensing, contract, and quality audits.
  • Participate in applicable State of California, CalMHSA, County, and community-partner meetings, as well as program, agency, planning, and training meetings.
  • Assist with donor and resource development activities, including grant applications, proposal development, funder reports, donation solicitation, and related data collection.
  • Conduct outreach and deliver Foster Care and SDYS program training to internal partners and community stakeholders; represent the RFA and maintain strong relationships with referral sources and community partners.
  • Respond to Child Welfare Services workers regarding placement availability and respond to service partners, resource parents, and staff during crises or urgent matters in accordance with established on-call procedures.
  • Maintain compliance with Child and Family Well-being/IEU and Community Care Licensing requirements; oversee audits and inspections, submit Special Incident Reports, and maintain ongoing communication with IEU, CCL, and County partners.
  • Maintain required data collection, contract documentation, reporting, and follow-up; submit accurate monthly and quarterly reports to funders, Quality Management, the County, and SDYS Fiscal.
  • Develop, monitor, and manage the RFA budget; review expenses and general ledger activity; reconcile program and fiscal records; oversee billing and payment requests; and address discrepancies in a timely manner.
  • Monitor resource-parent certifications, foster-youth placements, and required records, including intakes, assessments, progress notes, treatment plans, discharge summaries, and licensing documentation.
  • Work with the Recruitment and Training Coordinator to recruit, train, certify, support, and retain resource parents, including supporting required certifications, clearances, information sessions, and home studies as needed.
  • Provide case management support to the RFA team as needed.
  • Meet program goals and outcomes identified in scopes of service, grants, and contracts, and provide direct services as needed, including foster-youth placement coordination, crisis intervention, and case management.
  • Manage daily RFA operations and schedules; coordinate the treatment team; respond to staff, resource-parent, and service-partner questions and concerns; and provide office coverage when needed.
  • Provide personnel management through a trauma-informed lens, including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, training, supervision, professional development, and performance evaluations for staff, interns, volunteers, and JVC members.

SDYS EXPECTATIONS:

  • Adhere to and uphold the rigorous standards of SDYS as mandated by its mission, purpose, guiding principles, and standards of quality.
  • Maintain confidentiality and privacy standards of service partner-protected health information and other applicable information and material in accordance with agency and center policies, and applicable regulations and laws including HIPAA.
  • Welcome and support SDYS volunteers and assist them in accomplishing their services whenever applicable.
  • Effectively communicate with people from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Receive and give supportive feedback to foster equity and inclusion in working relationships.
  • Recognize, nurture, and learn from strengths in co-workers.
  • Maintain warm, welcoming, and safe work environments.
  • Possess flexibility to accomplish job responsibilities in several work environments, whether it be from home, on the road, or in an office.

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master’s degree or higher in social work, marriage and family therapy, or related field required.
  • License (LCSW, LMFT, LPCC, PhD, PsyD) and program management experience preferred.
  • Minimum of two years’ experience working with children, youth, and families as a primary duty in the child welfare social services public or private setting.
  • Must have familiarity with Child Welfare Services and Community Care Licensing standards.
  • Must be a team player with the ability to work independently.
  • Must be able to work with and represent a culturally and ethnically diverse community.
  • Must possess or be willing to develop a working knowledge of trauma-informed care and dual diagnosis treatment; experience working in trauma-informed and dual diagnosis preferred.
  • Must have a reliable vehicle, relevant auto insurance, a clean driving record, a valid CA driver’s license, and be willing to drive a vehicle for job-related tasks.
  • Maintain certification in CPR & First Aid.
  • Employment is subject to required clearances which include tuberculosis test, fingerprinting,background checks including FBI, DOJ, and CACI, and drug testing.
  • Must show a willingness to work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends, and be available for on-call emergencies.
  • Must have a reliable vehicle, relevant auto insurance, a clean driving record, a valid CA driver’s license, and be willing to drive a vehicle for job-related tasks.
  • Employment is subject to clearances, which include fingerprinting, background checks, driving records, and drug testing.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to sit and work at a computer for extended periods, including frequent use of a keyboard, mouse, telephone, and other office equipment.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach, and move throughout office, program, community, and other service environments as needed.
  • Ability to travel between SDYS sites, community locations, meetings, resource-parent homes, and other locations as required by the position.
  • Ability to safely enter and navigate residential homes and other community-based settings, including environments that may involve stairs, uneven surfaces, or limited accessibility.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, or pull materials and supplies weighing up to 25 pounds on an occasional basis.
  • Ability to maintain visual and auditory attention sufficient to monitor the safety and needs of youth, resource parents, staff, and service partners.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and through electronic communication.
  • Ability to respond appropriately and safely during urgent or crisis situations, including remaining mobile and physically responsive as necessary to ensure the safety of youth and others.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and on-call periods, as required by program operations.
  • Ability to safely operate a motor vehicle and travel independently for work-related activities.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: This position does have supervisory responsibilities.


Salary Range: $72,000 - $74,000


FULL-TIME STAFF BENEFITS:

  • PTO: 18 days PTO + 2 floating holidays + 12.5 paid holidays (32.5 paid days off)
  • 403b with 2% employer match
  • Medical, dental, vision, pet insurance
  • Mileage reimbursement
  • $2,000 annual bonus for staff who are fully bilingual in Spanish
  • $1,500 annual bonus for staff with proficiency in Spanish

To apply, please send resume and cover letter through job posting on SDYS website.


SDYS offers a comprehensive benefits package to full time employees that includes generous PTO, personal holidays, health, vision, dental, life insurance, parental leave and a 403(b)-retirement plan with matching contribution. SDYS is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) employer.


All are welcome at San Diego Youth Services.

As an organization working to meet the basic needs of youth, create positive connections, help youth develop life skills, and promote overall health and well-being, SDYS believes its practices and actions must reflect the highest level of commitment to access, equity, and social justice.


The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, innovation, self-expression, and talent that our members invest in their work represents not only part of the SDYS’ culture, but the SDYS’ reputation and achievements as well. SDYS remains open to feedback from all communities it touches and knows that input from those with direct experience of issues will make the SDYS more effective in achieving its goals.


SDYS is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities. In compliance with the Immigration and Nationality Act as amended, all new employees must verify their eligibility to work in the United States.


SDYS is proud to be a kindness certified company.

This role creates and coordinates content across public-facing channels, including media relations, social media, and other external communications platforms, while ensuring messaging is consistent, engaging, and aligned with the organization’s brand and strategic objectives. The ideal candidate is a skilled writer, organized project manager, and collaborative communicator who can effectively manage multiple priorities and engage diverse external audiences.


Essential Functions

  • Support the execution of external communications initiatives that align with organizational objectives and brand standards.
  • Develop, edit, and distribute content across external channels, including media relations, social media, website, and public-facing communications.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders and external vendors to gather information and develop content that promotes organizational initiatives and achievements.

  • Coordinate communications projects with internal partners and external vendors to ensure timely delivery.
  • Monitor communications performance and prepare reports on media coverage, audience engagement, and campaign results.

Additional Job Functions

    • Performs other duties as assigned

title: Brand Strategy, Managing Director (Location Flexible)
description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients.
